title: Advance cursor to next code chunk after executing last line
description:
## Summary

When running code line-by-line with Cmd+Enter, executing the last line of a code chunk causes the cursor to "fall out" of the chunk into prose. This is disruptive because the next chunk could be dozens of lines away and the user has to navigate back manually. Worse, if the user keeps pressing Cmd+Enter, the interpreter will try to execute the closing fence or prose text, leading to errors.

With this change, executing the last line of a code chunk moves the cursor to the first line of the next code chunk (if one exists). If there's no next chunk, the cursor lands on the closing fence as before.

This covers three code paths in `RunCurrentCommand`:
- **Source editor** (Positron, VS Code with R extension, fallback executors)
- **Visual editor, Positron** (`executeAtPosition` path)
- **Visual editor, non-Positron knitr** (line-by-line path)

The "run entire cell" paths (plain VS Code with Python/R, non-knitr visual editor) are unaffected since they don't do line-by-line execution.

## Related

#704 describes the same trigger (Cmd+Enter on the last line exits the chunk), though the author there preferred the cursor to stay put rather than advance. Both behaviors could coexist: this PR handles advancing to the next chunk, while Positron's Alt+Enter (posit-dev/positron#2778) already supports executing without moving the cursor.

title: Fix visual editor response to quickSuggestion setting for new default
description:
VSCode changed its default setting for `editor.quickSuggestions` to `offWhenInlineCompletions` and the Visual Editor was not checking the value correctly, causing snippets to not show up in the visual editor when they should. 

This PR makes the VisualEditor consider more values of `editor.quickSuggestions` to be enabled, including `editor.quickSuggestions`.

description:

title: add standalone insert citation dialog for hosts without an editor
description:
This makes the visual editor's Insert Citation dialog usable without an editor instance, so RStudio can offer it in its plain-text source editor (rstudio/rstudio#7876, a long-standing request).

The dialog itself never needed the ProseMirror document. It only read the YAML front matter to find `bibliography:`, `references:` and `zotero:`. `InsertCitationCommand` then applied the result with a transaction: the `[@key]` text and, when a new bibliography file was created, a `bibliography:` line in the front matter. This PR separates those two seams from the rest.

### Changes

- `BibliographyManager` and its providers accept either a document or plain YAML blocks (`YamlBlockSource`). Existing callers keep passing the doc and are unchanged.
- `ensureSourcesInBibliography` is split. The new `writeSourcesToBibliography` does the server writes and the Better BibTeX warning, and the wrapper still adds `bibliography:` to the doc in the same transaction.
- `showInsertCitationDialog` takes a `YamlBlockSource`. The unused `doc` parameter is removed from the panel and the bibliography source panel.
- A new `InsertCitationDialog` class (`editor/editor-citation.ts`) is exported from `editor` and from the panmirror bundle. `show({ yaml, theme?, selectionKey? })` returns `{ citationIds, intextCitationStyle, bibliographyFile?, selectionKey? }`. The host inserts the citation text and declares `bibliographyFile` in its front matter when set.
- `editorUIWithDefaultImages` is extracted from `Editor.create`. This also corrects the `omni_insert` and `citations` merges, which spread the whole `images` object instead of the nested one. `editor-ui` passes the full defaults, so its images are unchanged.
- `ensureTheme` applies the default theme CSS when no editor has applied a theme yet, since the panel relies on the `pm-*` color classes.

### Verification

`tsc --noEmit` passes for `apps/panmirror` and `apps/vscode-editor`, and eslint passes on the changed files.

**Standalone dialog.** I loaded the built bundle in headless Chromium with a stub host and server and drove the dialog:

| Scenario | Result | Bibliography write |
|---|---|---|
| Existing local source, doc has no `bibliography:` | `citationIds: ["smith2020"]`, `bibliographyFile: "references.bib"` | none, already present |
| From DOI, doc declares `refs.bib` | `citationIds: ["rivera2021"]`, no `bibliographyFile` | BibTeX entry appended to `refs.bib` |
| Cancel | `null` | none |

**Visual editor, before and after.** In an RStudio development server, I inserted an R Package citation from the visual editor's Insert Citation dialog in a new `.md` document. I ran it once with the current bundle and once with this branch's bundle served in its place:

| | `[@knitr]` inserted | `bibliography: references.bib` added | `references.bib` has the knitr entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | yes | yes | yes |
| after | yes | yes | yes |

### Notes

- There's no `apps/vscode/CHANGELOG.md` entry, because nothing changes for VS Code or Positron users. The new export is for RStudio. Happy to add one if you'd prefer.
- `packages/editor-collab` and `packages/editor-codemirror` type-check `editor/src` without JSX enabled, so their `tsc` already reports TS6142 for the `.tsx` modules it reaches. The new file adds one more of the same, and neither package has a `tsc` script or CI step.

Updates `axios` from 1.20.0 to 1.21.0
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.21.0 — October 21, 2026

This release adds response timing and opt-in UTF-8 Basic authentication, improves request handling across runtimes, and changes how header defaults are recognized.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Header Defaults: Only plain objects, null-prototype maps, and compatible AxiosHeaders instances are treated as common or method-specific defaults; literal headers such as Link are now preserved. Applications using custom class instances as defaults must convert them to plain maps, for example { post: { ...customDefaults } }, or compatible AxiosHeaders. Otherwise, those instances become literal header values, including on requests using other methods. (#11156)

🚀 New Features

  • Response Timing: Added response.duration, in milliseconds, including on error.response when present. Timing measures adapter execution and excludes interceptors and transforms; streamed responses stop timing when the stream becomes available. Axios replaces any existing duration value supplied by a custom adapter. (#11214)
  • UTF-8 Basic Authentication: Added transitional.encodeBasicAuthUsername: true to support Unicode usernames in XHR and Fetch requests. The option defaults to false, preserving existing authentication behavior; applications opting in should supply the original Unicode username and remove manual pre-encoding workarounds. (#11159)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Fetch Compatibility: Restored requests in runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers that reject the implicit cache: 'default', while preserving explicit caller settings. Response-size failures now retain their original ERR_BAD_RESPONSE and request context when runtime wrappers replace the underlying stream error. (#11194, #11179)
  • Runtime Consistency: Aligned encoded-byte size accounting, multipart uploads, proxy routing, same-origin resolution, parameter merging, and form serialization across adapters. Circular parameters now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and sparse or non-index numeric form fields serialize as keyed objects. With proxy: false, native proxyEnv agents using unsupported pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle overrides now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE; construct those agents without proxyEnv. (#11242)
  • Header Handling: Preserved headers named __proto__ using safe casing without changing the AxiosHeaders instance prototype. Function matchers in has(), delete(), and clear() now receive the headers instance as this, matching their declared contract. (#11134, #11216)
  • URL and Data URL Parsing: Accepted case-insensitive supported URL schemes and Base64 markers, and corrected decoding of percent-encoded Base64 data URLs. Node data URL allocation estimates remain aligned with decoding so configured size limits apply before allocation. (#11138, #11163, #11294)
  • Error Diagnostics: Preserved short reconstructed request stacks and appended wrapped error stacks under Caused by: so tooling that reads only error.stack retains the original failure context. (#11132, #11142)
  • Interceptor Removal: Restored removal through canonical numeric-string interceptor IDs, including after registry compaction. (#11139)
  • Proxy TLS: HTTPS CONNECT tunnels now apply current origin TLS options from an explicit httpsAgent, or from https.globalAgent when no explicit agent is supplied. This preserves process-wide custom CA settings through proxy tunnels. (#11178)
  • XHR Lifecycle: Used asynchronous Cookie Store reads for XSRF tokens where supported, preserving cookie fallback, timeout accounting, and cancellation. Upload and download progress listeners are now removed on completion, failure, timeout, and cancellation. (#11166, #11225)
  • HTTP/2 Sessions: Stopped reusing sessions immediately after GOAWAY and prevented draining sessions from scheduling idle timers that could delay process exit. (#11210)
  • TypeScript Declarations: Exposed the response-default marker as a public type to resolve TS2527 when consumers emit declarations involving unresolved response generics, covering both ESM and CommonJS. (#11125)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Configuration Performance: Reduced request configuration merge overhead, particularly for requests with many headers, while preserving merge semantics and prototype-pollution guards. (#11208)
  • Same-Origin Checks: Removed obsolete Internet Explorer detection without changing origin decisions in supported environments. (#11174)
  • Dependencies: Updated follow-redirects to 1.16.1 and refreshed development, documentation, test, and GitHub Actions dependencies. Removed unused dayjs from the docs package, root chalk, and chai from CJS module tests. (#11169, #11188, #11189, #11195, #11212, #11213, #11218, #11220, #11221, #11230, #11234, #11244, #11245, #11266, #11267, #11268, #11269, #11270, #11271, #11272, #11298, #11302, #11303, #11304, #11305, #11306, #11313, #11321, #11322, #11323, #11342)
  • Documentation: Fixed interceptor test links, updated README CDN examples to the published 1.20.0 bundle, and corrected guidance on interceptor options and request lifecycle ordering. (#11228, #11149, #11335)
  • Contributor Workflow: Consolidated agent instructions in AGENTS.md, standardized PR labels, required prerelease notes and validation evidence, and clarified that npm test requires installed Playwright browsers. (#11238, #11273, #11223, #11284)
  • Sponsors and Support: Added HeroDevs, Code for Japan, and Sweepico sponsor listings, refreshed sponsor data, and documented extended security support for Axios v0. (#11222, #11249, #11252, #11341)
  • Proxy Regression Coverage: Added a long dotted request-hostname test for NO_PROXY handling, extending coverage of an existing denial-of-service fix. (#11235)
  • Release Preparation: Updated package version metadata for 1.21.0. (#11346)

Updates `react-redux` from 9.3.0 to 9.3.1
Release notes

Sourced from react-redux's releases.

v9.3.1

This bugfix release fixes connect type inference under TS 7, fixes several connect and Provider runtime bugs, adds dev-mode logging for errors thrown in mapStateToProps, and updates our build tooling and TypeScript support matrix.

[!WARNING] While connect is still published and technically supported, we officially deprecated connect in 9.3.0 and strongly recommend migrating to use the hooks APIs instead.

Changelog

connect Types and TS 7

We had reports that connect sometimes inferred the wrong props when mapStateToProps or mapDispatchToProps was a factory function. The connected component's props would collapse to {}, and a required prop would show up as "missing" at the call site.

Turns out the connect overloads typed those arguments as unions of the factory form (() => (state) => props) and the plain form. TS7 changed the ordering of which union member got selected, so this broke.

As Anders suggested in microsoft/typescript-go#977, we've split those unions into separate overloads listed in order of preference, factory form first. Overload matching no longer depends on how the compiler orders a union. We then applied the same fix to the mergeProps overloads, which still failed under TS 7.

Bug Fixes

Provider now uses serverState when it's a falsy value like 0, false, or ''. Previously it checked for truthiness, so a falsy root state fell back to the client store's state during SSR and hydration. null and undefined are still treated as "no server state".

A connected component's context prop is now honored in production. The assignment that picked up the custom context sat inside the development-only validation block. In production, a component with only a custom provider would throw, and one rendered under both providers would read the default provider's store.

connect no longer overrides a ref passed as a regular prop when forwardRef isn't enabled (#2251). With React 19's ref-as-prop, the wrapper was always passing its own ref (undefined without forwardRef), which replaced the one you passed in.

An explicit dependsOnOwnProps = false on a mapStateToProps or mapDispatchToProps function is now respected. We had been ignoring it for functions declared with two parameters, even though the option exists specifically for functions whose length isn't reliable.

Rendering <Provider> in a React Server Component without "use client" now throws a clear dev-mode error that tells you what's wrong, instead of failing with "useIsomorphicLayoutEffect is not a function" (#2082). Setups that resolve the react-server export condition already got a clear error. This covers the setups that don't.

mapStateToProps Error Logging

Since v8, an error thrown in mapStateToProps during a store update has been caught in the subscription callback and then effectively swallowed. The component just kept rendering its previous props (#1942). connect now logs those errors to console.error in development, so they show up in DevTools. Production behavior is unchanged.

TypeScript Support

The internal NoInfer helper type has been replaced with TypeScript's built-in NoInfer, which was added in TS 5.4. That makes TS 5.4 the minimum version for React-Redux's types. Our CI matrix now covers TS 5.6 through 5.9, 6.0, 7.0, and next.

Build Tooling

Updates `react-window` from 2.4.1 to 2.5.1
Release notes

Sourced from react-window's releases.

2.5.1

  • scrollToRow (and useVirtualizer's scrollToIndex) supports behavior: "smooth" for dynamic row heights. The scroll is animated by the list so that its destination can be corrected as rows are measured along the way. Corrections for a scroll requested while the page is hidden no longer time out before the page is visible again.

2.5.0

Features

  • Add scrollElement prop to List and Grid for lists and grids that scroll along with other content. Pass "window" to scroll with the page, or an ancestor element that scrolls. The list or grid renders at its full height and only renders the rows visible within the scroll element's viewport; its position within the scroll element is measured whenever it renders, scrolls, or resizes, and whenever content before it is resized, inserted, or removed (e.g. an image loading above it). Imperative scroll methods scroll the scroll element. Grid columns scroll with the scroll element too if the grid is as wide as its content (e.g. style={{ width: "max-content" }}); otherwise they scroll within the grid. Add a scrolling with the page page to the docs site.
  • Add useVirtualizer hook for rendering custom (headless) virtualized content, e.g. a semantic <table>. It returns the items to render (with their offsets and sizes), the total size, the visible range, and a scrollToIndex method; options mirror the props of List (including scrollElement and dynamic sizes from useDynamicRowHeight). Add a useVirtualizer page to the docs site.
  • Add useIsScrolling hook for tracking whether a list, grid, or scroll element is scrolling (e.g. to render simplified rows while scrolling). It uses the "scrollend" event where supported. Add a useIsScrolling page to the docs site (replacing the common question about scrolling indicators).
  • Scrolling to a row, column, or cell (scrollToRow, scrollToColumn, scrollToCell, and useVirtualizer's scrollToIndex) respects the CSS scroll-padding of the element being scrolled, like the browser's scrollIntoView. For example, scroll-padding-top can keep rows from being aligned underneath a sticky header.
  • Add an infinite loading page to the docs site.

Updates `axios` from 1.20.0 to 1.21.0
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.21.0 — October 21, 2026

This release adds response timing and opt-in UTF-8 Basic authentication, improves request handling across runtimes, and changes how header defaults are recognized.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Header Defaults: Only plain objects, null-prototype maps, and compatible AxiosHeaders instances are treated as common or method-specific defaults; literal headers such as Link are now preserved. Applications using custom class instances as defaults must convert them to plain maps, for example { post: { ...customDefaults } }, or compatible AxiosHeaders. Otherwise, those instances become literal header values, including on requests using other methods. (#11156)

🚀 New Features

  • Response Timing: Added response.duration, in milliseconds, including on error.response when present. Timing measures adapter execution and excludes interceptors and transforms; streamed responses stop timing when the stream becomes available. Axios replaces any existing duration value supplied by a custom adapter. (#11214)
  • UTF-8 Basic Authentication: Added transitional.encodeBasicAuthUsername: true to support Unicode usernames in XHR and Fetch requests. The option defaults to false, preserving existing authentication behavior; applications opting in should supply the original Unicode username and remove manual pre-encoding workarounds. (#11159)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Fetch Compatibility: Restored requests in runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers that reject the implicit cache: 'default', while preserving explicit caller settings. Response-size failures now retain their original ERR_BAD_RESPONSE and request context when runtime wrappers replace the underlying stream error. (#11194, #11179)
  • Runtime Consistency: Aligned encoded-byte size accounting, multipart uploads, proxy routing, same-origin resolution, parameter merging, and form serialization across adapters. Circular parameters now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and sparse or non-index numeric form fields serialize as keyed objects. With proxy: false, native proxyEnv agents using unsupported pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle overrides now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE; construct those agents without proxyEnv. (#11242)
  • Header Handling: Preserved headers named __proto__ using safe casing without changing the AxiosHeaders instance prototype. Function matchers in has(), delete(), and clear() now receive the headers instance as this, matching their declared contract. (#11134, #11216)
  • URL and Data URL Parsing: Accepted case-insensitive supported URL schemes and Base64 markers, and corrected decoding of percent-encoded Base64 data URLs. Node data URL allocation estimates remain aligned with decoding so configured size limits apply before allocation. (#11138, #11163, #11294)
  • Error Diagnostics: Preserved short reconstructed request stacks and appended wrapped error stacks under Caused by: so tooling that reads only error.stack retains the original failure context. (#11132, #11142)
  • Interceptor Removal: Restored removal through canonical numeric-string interceptor IDs, including after registry compaction. (#11139)
  • Proxy TLS: HTTPS CONNECT tunnels now apply current origin TLS options from an explicit httpsAgent, or from https.globalAgent when no explicit agent is supplied. This preserves process-wide custom CA settings through proxy tunnels. (#11178)
  • XHR Lifecycle: Used asynchronous Cookie Store reads for XSRF tokens where supported, preserving cookie fallback, timeout accounting, and cancellation. Upload and download progress listeners are now removed on completion, failure, timeout, and cancellation. (#11166, #11225)
  • HTTP/2 Sessions: Stopped reusing sessions immediately after GOAWAY and prevented draining sessions from scheduling idle timers that could delay process exit. (#11210)
  • TypeScript Declarations: Exposed the response-default marker as a public type to resolve TS2527 when consumers emit declarations involving unresolved response generics, covering both ESM and CommonJS. (#11125)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Configuration Performance: Reduced request configuration merge overhead, particularly for requests with many headers, while preserving merge semantics and prototype-pollution guards. (#11208)
  • Same-Origin Checks: Removed obsolete Internet Explorer detection without changing origin decisions in supported environments. (#11174)
  • Dependencies: Updated follow-redirects to 1.16.1 and refreshed development, documentation, test, and GitHub Actions dependencies. Removed unused dayjs from the docs package, root chalk, and chai from CJS module tests. (#11169, #11188, #11189, #11195, #11212, #11213, #11218, #11220, #11221, #11230, #11234, #11244, #11245, #11266, #11267, #11268, #11269, #11270, #11271, #11272, #11298, #11302, #11303, #11304, #11305, #11306, #11313, #11321, #11322, #11323, #11342)
  • Documentation: Fixed interceptor test links, updated README CDN examples to the published 1.20.0 bundle, and corrected guidance on interceptor options and request lifecycle ordering. (#11228, #11149, #11335)
  • Contributor Workflow: Consolidated agent instructions in AGENTS.md, standardized PR labels, required prerelease notes and validation evidence, and clarified that npm test requires installed Playwright browsers. (#11238, #11273, #11223, #11284)
  • Sponsors and Support: Added HeroDevs, Code for Japan, and Sweepico sponsor listings, refreshed sponsor data, and documented extended security support for Axios v0. (#11222, #11249, #11252, #11341)
  • Proxy Regression Coverage: Added a long dotted request-hostname test for NO_PROXY handling, extending coverage of an existing denial-of-service fix. (#11235)
  • Release Preparation: Updated package version metadata for 1.21.0. (#11346)

Updates `react-redux` from 9.3.0 to 9.3.1
Release notes

Sourced from react-redux's releases.

v9.3.1

This bugfix release fixes connect type inference under TS 7, fixes several connect and Provider runtime bugs, adds dev-mode logging for errors thrown in mapStateToProps, and updates our build tooling and TypeScript support matrix.

[!WARNING] While connect is still published and technically supported, we officially deprecated connect in 9.3.0 and strongly recommend migrating to use the hooks APIs instead.

Changelog

connect Types and TS 7

We had reports that connect sometimes inferred the wrong props when mapStateToProps or mapDispatchToProps was a factory function. The connected component's props would collapse to {}, and a required prop would show up as "missing" at the call site.

Turns out the connect overloads typed those arguments as unions of the factory form (() => (state) => props) and the plain form. TS7 changed the ordering of which union member got selected, so this broke.

As Anders suggested in microsoft/typescript-go#977, we've split those unions into separate overloads listed in order of preference, factory form first. Overload matching no longer depends on how the compiler orders a union. We then applied the same fix to the mergeProps overloads, which still failed under TS 7.

Bug Fixes

Provider now uses serverState when it's a falsy value like 0, false, or ''. Previously it checked for truthiness, so a falsy root state fell back to the client store's state during SSR and hydration. null and undefined are still treated as "no server state".

A connected component's context prop is now honored in production. The assignment that picked up the custom context sat inside the development-only validation block. In production, a component with only a custom provider would throw, and one rendered under both providers would read the default provider's store.

connect no longer overrides a ref passed as a regular prop when forwardRef isn't enabled (#2251). With React 19's ref-as-prop, the wrapper was always passing its own ref (undefined without forwardRef), which replaced the one you passed in.

An explicit dependsOnOwnProps = false on a mapStateToProps or mapDispatchToProps function is now respected. We had been ignoring it for functions declared with two parameters, even though the option exists specifically for functions whose length isn't reliable.

Rendering <Provider> in a React Server Component without "use client" now throws a clear dev-mode error that tells you what's wrong, instead of failing with "useIsomorphicLayoutEffect is not a function" (#2082). Setups that resolve the react-server export condition already got a clear error. This covers the setups that don't.

mapStateToProps Error Logging

Since v8, an error thrown in mapStateToProps during a store update has been caught in the subscription callback and then effectively swallowed. The component just kept rendering its previous props (#1942). connect now logs those errors to console.error in development, so they show up in DevTools. Production behavior is unchanged.

TypeScript Support

The internal NoInfer helper type has been replaced with TypeScript's built-in NoInfer, which was added in TS 5.4. That makes TS 5.4 the minimum version for React-Redux's types. Our CI matrix now covers TS 5.6 through 5.9, 6.0, 7.0, and next.

Build Tooling

We've moved the repo to pnpm, Oxlint, and Oxfmt, and switched the library build from tsup to tsdown. The package exports layout is unchanged, but the build output comes from a different bundler. If you see any packaging or import problems with this release, please file an issue.

title: Bump `vscode-languageserver` and `vscode-languageclient` to 11
description: - Closes #1219 - Closes #1220 This PR replaces those two Dependabot PRs that bump vscode-languageserver and vscode-languageclient from 10.1.2 to 11.0.0 separately. LSP features are working correctly: The two packages come from the same `vscode-languageserver-node` repository and share `vscode-languageserver-protocol`, `vscode-jsonrpc`, and `vscode-languageserver-types`. Each Dependabot PR alone adds a nested copy of these shared packages, because the other package still uses the old versions at the top level. This PR bumps both packages together, so the lockfile has one copy of each: - `vscode-languageserver` and `vscode-languageclient`: 10.1.2 to 11.0.0 - `vscode-languageserver-protocol` and `vscode-languageserver-types`: 3.18.4 to 3.18.5 - `vscode-jsonrpc`: 9.0.3 to 10.0.0 - `vscode-languageserver-textdocument`: 1.0.15 to 1.0.16 The PR also raises the `vscode-languageserver-types` floor to `^3.18.5` in each workspace that declares it. The PR adds a `vscode-languageserver-node` group to `.github/dependabot.yml` so that all future bumps of these packages come in one PR, for major, minor, and patch updates. The group comes before `npm-minor-and-patch`, because Dependabot puts a dependency in the first group that matches it. The lockfile diff contains only these packages. I did not run `npm dedupe`, because it also updates unrelated packages.

Updates `axios` from 1.20.0 to 1.21.0
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.21.0 — October 21, 2026

This release adds response timing and opt-in UTF-8 Basic authentication, improves request handling across runtimes, and changes how header defaults are recognized.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Header Defaults: Only plain objects, null-prototype maps, and compatible AxiosHeaders instances are treated as common or method-specific defaults; literal headers such as Link are now preserved. Applications using custom class instances as defaults must convert them to plain maps, for example { post: { ...customDefaults } }, or compatible AxiosHeaders. Otherwise, those instances become literal header values, including on requests using other methods. (#11156)

🚀 New Features

  • Response Timing: Added response.duration, in milliseconds, including on error.response when present. Timing measures adapter execution and excludes interceptors and transforms; streamed responses stop timing when the stream becomes available. Axios replaces any existing duration value supplied by a custom adapter. (#11214)
  • UTF-8 Basic Authentication: Added transitional.encodeBasicAuthUsername: true to support Unicode usernames in XHR and Fetch requests. The option defaults to false, preserving existing authentication behavior; applications opting in should supply the original Unicode username and remove manual pre-encoding workarounds. (#11159)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Fetch Compatibility: Restored requests in runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers that reject the implicit cache: 'default', while preserving explicit caller settings. Response-size failures now retain their original ERR_BAD_RESPONSE and request context when runtime wrappers replace the underlying stream error. (#11194, #11179)
  • Runtime Consistency: Aligned encoded-byte size accounting, multipart uploads, proxy routing, same-origin resolution, parameter merging, and form serialization across adapters. Circular parameters now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and sparse or non-index numeric form fields serialize as keyed objects. With proxy: false, native proxyEnv agents using unsupported pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle overrides now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE; construct those agents without proxyEnv. (#11242)
  • Header Handling: Preserved headers named __proto__ using safe casing without changing the AxiosHeaders instance prototype. Function matchers in has(), delete(), and clear() now receive the headers instance as this, matching their declared contract. (#11134, #11216)
  • URL and Data URL Parsing: Accepted case-insensitive supported URL schemes and Base64 markers, and corrected decoding of percent-encoded Base64 data URLs. Node data URL allocation estimates remain aligned with decoding so configured size limits apply before allocation. (#11138, #11163, #11294)
  • Error Diagnostics: Preserved short reconstructed request stacks and appended wrapped error stacks under Caused by: so tooling that reads only error.stack retains the original failure context. (#11132, #11142)
  • Interceptor Removal: Restored removal through canonical numeric-string interceptor IDs, including after registry compaction. (#11139)
  • Proxy TLS: HTTPS CONNECT tunnels now apply current origin TLS options from an explicit httpsAgent, or from https.globalAgent when no explicit agent is supplied. This preserves process-wide custom CA settings through proxy tunnels. (#11178)
  • XHR Lifecycle: Used asynchronous Cookie Store reads for XSRF tokens where supported, preserving cookie fallback, timeout accounting, and cancellation. Upload and download progress listeners are now removed on completion, failure, timeout, and cancellation. (#11166, #11225)
  • HTTP/2 Sessions: Stopped reusing sessions immediately after GOAWAY and prevented draining sessions from scheduling idle timers that could delay process exit. (#11210)
  • TypeScript Declarations: Exposed the response-default marker as a public type to resolve TS2527 when consumers emit declarations involving unresolved response generics, covering both ESM and CommonJS. (#11125)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Configuration Performance: Reduced request configuration merge overhead, particularly for requests with many headers, while preserving merge semantics and prototype-pollution guards. (#11208)
  • Same-Origin Checks: Removed obsolete Internet Explorer detection without changing origin decisions in supported environments. (#11174)
  • Dependencies: Updated follow-redirects to 1.16.1 and refreshed development, documentation, test, and GitHub Actions dependencies. Removed unused dayjs from the docs package, root chalk, and chai from CJS module tests. (#11169, #11188, #11189, #11195, #11212, #11213, #11218, #11220, #11221, #11230, #11234, #11244, #11245, #11266, #11267, #11268, #11269, #11270, #11271, #11272, #11298, #11302, #11303, #11304, #11305, #11306, #11313, #11321, #11322, #11323, #11342)
  • Documentation: Fixed interceptor test links, updated README CDN examples to the published 1.20.0 bundle, and corrected guidance on interceptor options and request lifecycle ordering. (#11228, #11149, #11335)
  • Contributor Workflow: Consolidated agent instructions in AGENTS.md, standardized PR labels, required prerelease notes and validation evidence, and clarified that npm test requires installed Playwright browsers. (#11238, #11273, #11223, #11284)
  • Sponsors and Support: Added HeroDevs, Code for Japan, and Sweepico sponsor listings, refreshed sponsor data, and documented extended security support for Axios v0. (#11222, #11249, #11252, #11341)
  • Proxy Regression Coverage: Added a long dotted request-hostname test for NO_PROXY handling, extending coverage of an existing denial-of-service fix. (#11235)

Otherwise, those instances become literal header values, including on requests using other methods. (#11156)

🚀 New Features

  • Response Timing: Added response.duration, in milliseconds, including on error.response when present. Timing measures adapter execution and excludes interceptors and transforms; streamed responses stop timing when the stream becomes available. Axios replaces any existing duration value supplied by a custom adapter. (#11214)
  • UTF-8 Basic Authentication: Added transitional.encodeBasicAuthUsername: true to support Unicode usernames in XHR and Fetch requests. The option defaults to false, preserving existing authentication behavior; applications opting in should supply the original Unicode username and remove manual pre-encoding workarounds. (#11159)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Fetch Compatibility: Restored requests in runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers that reject the implicit cache: 'default', while preserving explicit caller settings. Response-size failures now retain their original ERR_BAD_RESPONSE and request context when runtime wrappers replace the underlying stream error. (#11194, #11179)
  • Runtime Consistency: Aligned encoded-byte size accounting, multipart uploads, proxy routing, same-origin resolution, parameter merging, and form serialization across adapters. Circular parameters now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and sparse or non-index numeric form fields serialize as keyed objects. With proxy: false, native proxyEnv agents using unsupported pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle overrides now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE; construct those agents without proxyEnv. (#11242)
  • Header Handling: Preserved headers named __proto__ using safe casing without changing the AxiosHeaders instance prototype. Function matchers in has(), delete(), and clear() now receive the headers instance as this, matching their declared contract. (#11134, #11216)
  • URL and Data URL Parsing: Accepted case-insensitive supported URL schemes and Base64 markers, and corrected decoding of percent-encoded Base64 data URLs. Node data URL allocation estimates remain aligned with decoding so configured size limits apply before allocation. (#11138, #11163, #11294)
  • Error Diagnostics: Preserved short reconstructed request stacks and appended wrapped error stacks under Caused by: so tooling that reads only error.stack retains the original failure context. (#11132, #11142)
  • Interceptor Removal: Restored removal through canonical numeric-string interceptor IDs, including after registry compaction. (#11139)
  • Proxy TLS: HTTPS CONNECT tunnels now apply current origin TLS options from an explicit httpsAgent, or from https.globalAgent when no explicit agent is supplied. This preserves process-wide custom CA settings through proxy tunnels. (#11178)
  • XHR Lifecycle: Used asynchronous Cookie Store reads for XSRF tokens where supported, preserving cookie fallback, timeout accounting, and cancellation. Upload and download progress listeners are now removed on completion, failure, timeout, and cancellation. (#11166, #11225)
  • HTTP/2 Sessions: Stopped reusing sessions immediately after GOAWAY and prevented draining sessions from scheduling idle timers that could delay process exit. (#11210)
  • TypeScript Declarations: Exposed the response-default marker as a public type to resolve TS2527 when consumers emit declarations involving unresolved response generics, covering both ESM and CommonJS. (#11125)

  • Configuration Performance: Reduced request configuration merge overhead, particularly for requests with many headers, while preserving merge semantics and prototype-pollution guards. (#11208)
  • Same-Origin Checks: Removed obsolete Internet Explorer detection without changing origin decisions in supported environments. (#11174)
  • Dependencies: Updated follow-redirects to 1.16.1 and refreshed development, documentation, test, and GitHub Actions dependencies. Removed unused dayjs from the docs package, root chalk, and chai from CJS module tests. Updates `react-redux` from 9.3.0 to 9.3.1
Release notes

Sourced from react-redux's releases.

v9.3.1

This bugfix release fixes connect type inference under TS 7, fixes several connect and Provider runtime bugs, adds dev-mode logging for errors thrown in mapStateToProps, and updates our build tooling and TypeScript support matrix.

[!WARNING] While connect is still published and technically supported, we officially deprecated connect in 9.3.0 and strongly recommend migrating to use the hooks APIs instead.

Changelog

connect Types and TS 7

We had reports that connect sometimes inferred the wrong props when mapStateToProps or mapDispatchToProps was a factory function. The connected component's props would collapse to {}, and a required prop would show up as "missing" at the call site.

Turns out the connect overloads typed those arguments as unions of the factory form (() => (state) => props) and the plain form. TS7 changed the ordering of which union member got selected, so this broke.

As Anders suggested in microsoft/typescript-go#977, we've split those unions into separate overloads listed in order of preference, factory form first. Overload matching no longer depends on how the compiler orders a union. We then applied the same fix to the mergeProps overloads, which still failed under TS 7.

Bug Fixes

Provider now uses serverState when it's a falsy value like 0, false, or ''. Previously it checked for truthiness, so a falsy root state fell back to the client store's state during SSR and hydration. null and undefined are still treated as "no server state".

A connected component's context prop is now honored in production. The assignment that picked up the custom context sat inside the development-only validation block. In production, a component with only a custom provider would throw, and one rendered under both providers would read the default provider's store.

connect no longer overrides a ref passed as a regular prop when forwardRef isn't enabled (#2251). With React 19's ref-as-prop, the wrapper was always passing its own ref (undefined without forwardRef), which replaced the one you passed in.

An explicit dependsOnOwnProps = false on a mapStateToProps or mapDispatchToProps function is now respected. We had been ignoring it for functions declared with two parameters, even though the option exists specifically for functions whose length isn't reliable.

Rendering <Provider> in a React Server Component without "use client" now throws a clear dev-mode error that tells you what's wrong, instead of failing with "useIsomorphicLayoutEffect is not a function" (#2082). Setups that resolve the react-server export condition already got a clear error. This covers the setups that don't.

mapStateToProps Error Logging

Since v8, an error thrown in mapStateToProps during a store update has been caught in the subscription callback and then effectively swallowed. The component just kept rendering its previous props (#1942). connect now logs those errors to console.error in development, so they show up in DevTools. Production behavior is unchanged.

TypeScript Support

The internal NoInfer helper type has been replaced with TypeScript's built-in NoInfer, which was added in TS 5.4. That makes TS 5.4 the minimum version for React-Redux's types. Our CI matrix now covers TS 5.6 through 5.9, 6.0, 7.0, and next.

Build Tooling

We've moved the repo to pnpm, Oxlint, and Oxfmt, and switched the library build from tsup to tsdown. The package exports layout is unchanged, but the build output comes from a different bundler. If you see any packaging or import problems with this release, please file an issue.

  • ignore patterns that start with / now start at the same place as other patterns that start with /: the root option if set, or else the root of the cwd, such as C:\ on Windows.
  • ignore patterns follow the windowsPathsNoEscape option, the same as other patterns.
  • On Windows, patterns that start with a long UNC root like //?/UNC/host/share/ walk that share, the same as //host/share/.

  • When the signal aborts an async walk, the walk stops. Before, it rejected, but continued to read directories.

  • Move the CLI program out to a separate package, glob-bin. Install that if you'd like to continue using glob from the command line.

  • Remove the unsafe --shell option. The --shell option is now ONLY supported on known shells where the behavior can be implemented safely.

title: fix snippet completion incorrect filtering
description:
## Problem

Snippets were being filtered from completions because of a position miscalculation. 

The `itemFrom` function was not correct, it was doing something clever that it is not quite right.

`itemFrom` should calculate how many characters into the document the start of a completion is. It did this by calculating the length of the completion and subtracting that from the text cursor's position. The way it was calculating the length of the completion was not correct. The completion gives its positions in the context of the `cvContext.code`, which is different from the positions in the actual document; For one thing, the line containing the language string (like `{r}`) is removed from `cvContext.code`. So, we can't use the positions the completion gives us directly. That is why `itemFrom` was cleverly not using the positions, but instead using the positions to calculate the length of the completion. 

But, for example, if you are typing `libr`, a completion for the `library` snippet will say that its insertion character position is from 0 to 7. What's up with that? For whatever reason, since your cursor is at the end of a line with 4 characters, the completion pretends that it can replace 3 more non-existent characters in the rest of the line. If there were any characters in the line after `libr`, even just whitespace like `libr `, then the completion would instead say that its insertion character position is from 0 to 4.

This PR fixes the issue by snapping the ending position of a completion to the end of its line in `cvContext.code`.

After I fixed this issue, I was able to easily insert the `library` snippet in R code, and this uncovered a bug in snippets in codemirror autocomplete that I reported here https://github.com/codemirror/dev/issues/1607.

title: Prevent hover hangs outside single-line display math
description:
Hovering over `after` in a `.qmd` file containing `Before $$x$$ after` hangs the language server.

The single-line display-math regex is missing the `g` flag, so `inlineMathRange()` keeps finding the same match when the cursor is outside it. Adding the flag lets the scan advance and terminate.

Includes regression tests for positions before, between and after expressions, plus repeated lookups. The tests use a timeout so this regression cannot hang the test suite.

Reproduced with the language servers bundled in Quarto VS Code 1.138.0 and 1.139.0 on macOS arm64. Core and LSP tests, core lint, and the LSP build pass.

Updates `ovsx` from 1.2.0 to 1.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from ovsx's releases.

CLI v1.3.0

Added

  • Add --follow-symlinks to publish, forwarding vsce's option of the same name so that the file walk recurses into symlinked directories instead of packing each symlink as a file. Needed for a node_modules assembled out of symlinks, as pnpm's is (#368)
  • Add search command to search the registry for extensions, mirroring the web UI's search: --category, --target, --sort-by and --sort-order narrow the query, --size and --offset page through the results, and --json prints the registry's raw response (#2154)
  • Add list command to print the extensions a namespace holds, sorted by name so the output stays stable across registries, with --json for the raw namespace metadata (#2154)
  • Add show command to print an extension's metadata, mirroring vsce show: identity, publisher, rating, notices and a version history listing each version's target platforms (#2149). namespace.extension@version reports a single version, --target scopes the report to one target platform, --all-versions lists every published version instead of the most recent few, and --json prints the registry's raw metadata
  • Add unpublish command to delete an extension or some of its versions, mirroring vsce unpublish (#1958); requires a registry running version 1.2.0 or later, which unpublish checks for before deleting
  • publish checks the packaged extension's size against the limit reported by the registry's /api/version endpoint before uploading, instead of failing only after the upload completes (#1953)
  • Add verify command to check a downloaded .vsix package's signature against the registry's public key, mirroring vsce verify-signature (#993)
  • Add verify-signature command, verifying an already-extracted package/manifest/signature file trio entirely offline (no registry involved), matching vsce verify-signature's own command shape (#993)

Fixed

  • Error messages naming a URL no longer include its query string, which for createNamespace, verifyPat, publish and delete carried the personal access token straight to stderr and into CI logs (#2186)

  • A connection lost after a JSON response has started no longer leaves the command waiting on a body that is not coming: the response's own error is now what settles the request, so it fails with the reset rather than hanging (#2186)

  • Requests now give up after 30 seconds without progress instead of hanging indefinitely when a server accepts a connection and then says nothing. OVSX_TIMEOUT overrides the duration in milliseconds and OVSX_TIMEOUT=0 disables it; it measures inactivity, so a large extension downloading slowly is unaffected, and it covers the trusted-publishing ID token request as well as the registry's own (#2186)

  • Fix downloads that could be read before they were written. download resolved when the response ended rather than when the file was closed, and a write stream opens and flushes asynchronously, so a caller reading the path immediately afterwards could find the file empty or absent - which verify did, intermittently failing to read the public key it had just fetched. A failed download no longer touches the target path: the body is written beside it and renamed into place only once it has arrived whole, so a 404 or a dropped connection leaves what was there alone. A connection dropped mid-download now rejects rather than leaving the caller waiting forever (#2185)

Changed

  • createNamespace, verifyPat, publish and delete now send the personal access token primarily via an Authorization: Bearer header (or, when OVSX_USERNAME/OVSX_PASSWORD are set, an X-OpenVSX-Token header, since Authorization is then already in use for Basic auth to a fronting proxy), moving away from a token query parameter that gets recorded in server and reverse-proxy access logs. The CLI checks the registry's reported version (/api/version) and only still sends the token as a query parameter, alongside the header, when talking to a registry older than 1.3.0, i.e. one that predates header support - including one whose version can't be determined at all, which is treated as too old rather than assumed to be caught up; on 1.3.0 and later the header is all it sends (#1344)
  • publish --trusted-publishing retries the token exchange when the registry answers that it could not verify the ID token (502, 503, 504), rather than failing the build on a blip reaching the identity provider. A refusal is never retried
  • publish --trusted-publishing requests a new token and retries once when the registry refuses the one it was publishing with. The issued token is short-lived and shared by every target platform of a release, so publishing a wide fan-out of large packages could outlive it and fail partway through. Targets that are refused together share one new token, and a token supplied with --pat is never retried
  • Bump minimum supported Node.js version to 22, matching the webui component

Dependencies

  • Bump fast-uri from 3.1.5 to 3.1.7
  • Bump qs from 6.15.2 to 6.16.0
  • Bump @​humanfs/node from 0.16.6 to 0.16.8
  • Bump js-yaml from 4.3.1 to 4.3.2
  • Bump nanoid from 3.3.16 to 3.3.18

Frontend Library v1.3.0

Added

  • Add a /publish page and turn the navbar's Publish button into a drop target: a file drag anywhere in the app turns the button into a drop area, and every .vsix package dropped on it — or on the publish page's own drop area — is queued and uploaded straight away, with no confirmation dialog. The page shows the queue as a line of extension cards — a skeleton while a package uploads, the real card once the registry accepts it, labelled with whatever the registry did with it — and keeps polling anything left under review or still missing its icon
  • Export PublishButton, which carries the publish link, its p shortcut and the app's .vsix drop target in one component, so a deployment with its own menu content keeps drag-and-drop publishing
  • Add a "Data Consistency" page to the admin dashboard (#1622): a live overview of every registered consistency check's finding count, with actions to refresh it and to fix findings one at a time or all at once
  • Show a "Namespace not verified" state on an extension card when it can't be activated because its namespace already exists in a referenced external gallery and hasn't been verified, in both the "My Extensions" and namespace member extension lists. The card keeps its colour and takes a warning-toned frame and icon, since this is the publisher's to fix rather than an extension that is simply switched off
  • Show a warning notice with a claim action wherever an unverified namespace is holding something back — the extension settings page when the extension has a namespace ownership conflict, and the namespace settings page for any unverified namespace — making clear the namespace must be claimed (verified) first. The action is the deployment's configured elements.claimNamespace, falling back to the namespace access documentation when none is configured. The admin dashboard's extension and namespace views show the same explanation without the claim action, since claiming is the publisher's action to take, not an admin's on someone else's behalf
  • Add a "Search Index" page to the admin dashboard: which engine answers searches, how many extensions the index holds against how many it is built from, and a button to rebuild it where there is an index to rebuild. The two counts sit side by side because an index that has quietly lost entries answers searches perfectly well, just with nothing in them, which is indistinguishable from an empty registry unless both numbers are visible at once
  • Mark a version that was published through a trusted publishing workflow with an icon next to "Published by" on the extension detail page, linking to the deployment's trusted publishing documentation. The default deployment points that link at the Trusted Publishing wiki page
  • Add a Pill component — the clickable glass pill the category pills are built on, now usable on its own — and extract the MonoSlash, glassSurface and compactControl page primitives out of the search field, the pills and the search header
  • Add userLoading to MainContext, so custom pages can tell "not logged in" from "still resolving the user"
  • Add a userMenuContent slot to PageSettings.elements: extra entries for the logged-in account menu, rendered above the admin entry. The slot receives a MenuEntry component to build entries with, so each entry is styled by the menu it appears in — the desktop and mobile menus style theirs differently, and a consumer cannot match both on its own
  • Add an adminPages slot to PageSettings.elements: extra admin dashboard pages, each declaring a name, icon, optional description and optional category, and each appearing in the side panel, as a card on the dashboard overview and as a route. Contributions are additive — a category name matching a built-in group appends to it, and a page whose path would shadow a built-in one is ignored
  • Widen the published API for consumers building their own pages: the request layer (sendRequest, sendNonRetriableRequest, ErrorResponse, controllerFromSignal), MainContext, AppProviders, NotFound, createDefaultTheme with the MONO_FONT/NAVBAR_HEIGHT tokens, the createRoute/createAbsoluteURL/addQuery/formatCompactNumber/toRelativeTime utils, the useDebouncedCallback and useGridCursor hooks, the navbar-chrome, search-focus and page-search-bar hooks, the category icon helpers, ExtensionDetailRoutes, and the itemIcon/MenuItemText building blocks for userMenuContent entries

Updates `ovsx` from 1.2.0 to 1.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from ovsx's releases.

CLI v1.3.0

Added

  • Add --follow-symlinks to publish, forwarding vsce's option of the same name so that the file walk recurses into symlinked directories instead of packing each symlink as a file. Needed for a node_modules assembled out of symlinks, as pnpm's is (#368)
  • Add search command to search the registry for extensions, mirroring the web UI's search: --category, --target, --sort-by and --sort-order narrow the query, --size and --offset page through the results, and --json prints the registry's raw response (#2154)
  • Add list command to print the extensions a namespace holds, sorted by name so the output stays stable across registries, with --json for the raw namespace metadata (#2154)
  • Add show command to print an extension's metadata, mirroring vsce show: identity, publisher, rating, notices and a version history listing each version's target platforms (#2149). namespace.extension@version reports a single version, --target scopes the report to one target platform, --all-versions lists every published version instead of the most recent few, and --json prints the registry's raw metadata
  • Add unpublish command to delete an extension or some of its versions, mirroring vsce unpublish (#1958); requires a registry running version 1.2.0 or later, which unpublish checks for before deleting
  • publish checks the packaged extension's size against the limit reported by the registry's /api/version endpoint before uploading, instead of failing only after the upload completes (#1953)
  • Add verify command to check a downloaded .vsix package's signature against the registry's public key, mirroring vsce verify-signature (#993)
  • Add verify-signature command, verifying an already-extracted package/manifest/signature file trio entirely offline (no registry involved), matching vsce verify-signature's own command shape (#993)

Fixed

  • Error messages naming a URL no longer include its query string, which for createNamespace, verifyPat, publish and delete carried the personal access token straight to stderr and into CI logs (#2186)

  • A connection lost after a JSON response has started no longer leaves the command waiting on a body that is not coming: the response's own error is now what settles the request, so it fails with the reset rather than hanging (#2186)

  • Requests now give up after 30 seconds without progress instead of hanging indefinitely when a server accepts a connection and then says nothing. OVSX_TIMEOUT overrides the duration in milliseconds and OVSX_TIMEOUT=0 disables it; it measures inactivity, so a large extension downloading slowly is unaffected, and it covers the trusted-publishing ID token request as well as the registry's own (#2186)

  • Fix downloads that could be read before they were written. download resolved when the response ended rather than when the file was closed, and a write stream opens and flushes asynchronously, so a caller reading the path immediately afterwards could find the file empty or absent - which verify did, intermittently failing to read the public key it had just fetched. A failed download no longer touches the target path: the body is written beside it and renamed into place only once it has arrived whole, so a 404 or a dropped connection leaves what was there alone. A connection dropped mid-download now rejects rather than leaving the caller waiting forever (#2185)

Changed

  • createNamespace, verifyPat, publish and delete now send the personal access token primarily via an Authorization: Bearer header (or, when OVSX_USERNAME/OVSX_PASSWORD are set, an X-OpenVSX-Token header, since Authorization is then already in use for Basic auth to a fronting proxy), moving away from a token query parameter that gets recorded in server and reverse-proxy access logs. The CLI checks the registry's reported version (/api/version) and only still sends the token as a query parameter, alongside the header, when talking to a registry older than 1.3.0, i.e. one that predates header support - including one whose version can't be determined at all, which is treated as too old rather than assumed to be caught up; on 1.3.0 and later the header is all it sends (#1344)
  • publish --trusted-publishing retries the token exchange when the registry answers that it could not verify the ID token (502, 503, 504), rather than failing the build on a blip reaching the identity provider. A refusal is never retried
  • publish --trusted-publishing requests a new token and retries once when the registry refuses the one it was publishing with. The issued token is short-lived and shared by every target platform of a release, so publishing a wide fan-out of large packages could outlive it and fail partway through. Targets that are refused together share one new token, and a token supplied with --pat is never retried
  • Bump minimum supported Node.js version to 22, matching the webui component

Dependencies

  • Bump fast-uri from 3.1.5 to 3.1.7
  • Bump qs from 6.15.2 to 6.16.0
  • Bump @​humanfs/node from 0.16.6 to 0.16.8
  • Bump js-yaml from 4.3.1 to 4.3.2
  • Bump nanoid from 3.3.16 to 3.3.18

Frontend Library v1.3.0

Added

  • Add a /publish page and turn the navbar's Publish button into a drop target: a file drag anywhere in the app turns the button into a drop area, and every .vsix package dropped on it — or on the publish page's own drop area — is queued and uploaded straight away, with no confirmation dialog. The page shows the queue as a line of extension cards — a skeleton while a package uploads, the real card once the registry accepts it, labelled with whatever the registry did with it — and keeps polling anything left under review or still missing its icon
  • Export PublishButton, which carries the publish link, its p shortcut and the app's .vsix drop target in one component, so a deployment with its own menu content keeps drag-and-drop publishing
  • Add a "Data Consistency" page to the admin dashboard (#1622): a live overview of every registered consistency check's finding count, with actions to refresh it and to fix findings one at a time or all at once
  • Show a "Namespace not verified" state on an extension card when it can't be activated because its namespace already exists in a referenced external gallery and hasn't been verified, in both the "My Extensions" and namespace member extension lists. The card keeps its colour and takes a warning-toned frame and icon, since this is the publisher's to fix rather than an extension that is simply switched off
  • Show a warning notice with a claim action wherever an unverified namespace is holding something back — the extension settings page when the extension has a namespace ownership conflict, and the namespace settings page for any unverified namespace — making clear the namespace must be claimed (verified) first. The action is the deployment's configured elements.claimNamespace, falling back to the namespace access documentation when none is configured. The admin dashboard's extension and namespace views show the same explanation without the claim action, since claiming is the publisher's action to take, not an admin's on someone else's behalf
  • Add a "Search Index" page to the admin dashboard: which engine answers searches, how many extensions the index holds against how many it is built from, and a button to rebuild it where there is an index to rebuild. The two counts sit side by side because an index that has quietly lost entries answers searches perfectly well, just with nothing in them, which is indistinguishable from an empty registry unless both numbers are visible at once
  • Mark a version that was published through a trusted publishing workflow with an icon next to "Published by" on the extension detail page, linking to the deployment's trusted publishing documentation. The default deployment points that link at the Trusted Publishing wiki page
  • Add a Pill component — the clickable glass pill the category pills are built on, now usable on its own — and extract the MonoSlash, glassSurface and compactControl page primitives out of the search field, the pills and the search header
  • Add userLoading to MainContext, so custom pages can tell "not logged in" from "still resolving the user"
  • Add a userMenuContent slot to PageSettings.elements: extra entries for the logged-in account menu, rendered above the admin entry. The slot receives a MenuEntry component to build entries with, so each entry is styled by the menu it appears in — the desktop and mobile menus style theirs differently, and a consumer cannot match both on its own
  • Add an adminPages slot to PageSettings.elements: extra admin dashboard pages, each declaring a name, icon, optional description and optional category, and each appearing in the side panel, as a card on the dashboard overview and as a route. Contributions are additive — a category name matching a built-in group appends to it, and a page whose path would shadow a built-in one is ignored
  • Widen the published API for consumers building their own pages: the request layer (sendRequest, sendNonRetriableRequest, ErrorResponse, controllerFromSignal), MainContext, AppProviders, NotFound, createDefaultTheme with the MONO_FONT/NAVBAR_HEIGHT tokens, the createRoute/createAbsoluteURL/addQuery/formatCompactNumber/toRelativeTime utils, the useDebouncedCallback and useGridCursor hooks, the navbar-chrome, search-focus and page-search-bar hooks, the category icon helpers, ExtensionDetailRoutes, and the itemIcon/MenuItemText building blocks for userMenuContent entries

Changelog

Sourced from ovsx's changelog.

[1.3.0] - 2026-10-16

Changed

  • publish checks a package against the size limit that applies to its own namespace, which a size override can raise above the registry default, and refuses an oversized upload before sending it. Against a registry older than 1.3.0, which cannot report that limit, it warns against the default and publishes anyway; if a registry that should be able to report it does not answer, it says the check did not happen rather than passing silently (#2129)

Fixed

  • --version reads the version from package.json at runtime instead of a generated src/version.ts, so it can no longer report a stale version (#2295)
  • publish now deletes the .vsix it packages into the temp directory once publishing finishes or fails, instead of leaving one behind per package and target (#2286)
  • Drop the X-OpenVSX-Token header, which carries the personal access token when --username/--password are set, on a redirect to another origin, as is done for Authorization (#2309)
  • A request with a body that is redirected with 301/302/303 now fails with an error naming the redirect target, instead of being resent as a GET without its body (#2309)
  • Trusted publishing's OIDC ID token request now uses the registry client's request handling: it follows redirects (dropping the runner token on a redirect to another origin) and reports the token service's error message instead of only its status (#2322)
  • An HTML page in a successful response (any <!doctype html> casing, or a text/html Content-Type) now fails with an error naming the status, instead of printing the raw HTML or a JSON SyntaxError (#2326)
  • An error response whose JSON body starts with whitespace now reports the server's message instead of only its status (#2326)

Dependencies

  • Bump commander from 6.2.1 to 14.0.3; a command given more arguments than it takes now fails instead of ignoring the extras (#2294)
  • Bump @​vscode/vsce from 3.7.1 to 4.0.0 (#2288)
  • Bump vitest from 4.1.11 to 5.0.3, adding vite as a direct dev dependency - vitest 5 no longer bundles it, only requires it as a peer (#2291)
  • Remove leven; the command-suggestion distance check now uses a vendored Levenshtein implementation, the same way @vscode/vsce itself replaced its own leven dependency in 4.0.0 (#2290)
  • Remove tmp; temporary file names are now generated with crypto.randomUUID (#2284)
  • Remove follow-redirects; requests use node:http/node:https and the registry client follows redirects itself (#2309)
  • Bump ip-address from 10.4.0 to 10.7.2 (#2264)
  • Bump brace-expansion to 1.1.21, 2.1.7, 5.0.12
  • Bump markdown-it from 14.2.0 to 14.3.2 (#2281)

  • 5d26c73 docs: use Keep a Changelog headings in all change logs (#2343)

  • fc539ff fix(cli): share registry request handling with OIDC (#2322)

Updates `sass` from 1.105.1 to 1.106.0
Release notes

Sourced from sass's releases.

Dart Sass 1.106.0

To install Sass 1.106.0, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Don't normalize CSS escapes in statement contexts that can contain interpolation. For example, @f\6Fo is now emitted as written rather than normalized to @foo.

  • Fix a bug where quotes would be removed from attribute selector values that contained backslashes.

  • Fix invalid source spans that could cause crashes when encountering a syntax error in selectors or media queries that also contain escape sequences.

  • Fix a bug where the indented syntax parser would crash when parsing a file where the first statement was indented and appeared after the first line.

  • Fix a bug that could cause crashes when encountering errors or warnings in interpolations that contain patterns like // */.

  • Potentially breaking compatibility fix: CSS escape codes whose values are 0, for Unicode surrogates, or greater than the maximum allowed code point are now consistently normalized to U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER in expression contexts. Previously, in some cases these were instead normalized to the normalized form of the original escape sequence, which violates the principle that all escape sequences for identical values should be normalized the same way. In other cases, these would simply throw errors.

    As a special case, \0 on its own will continue to be normalized to \0 to support historical CSS hacks.

  • Potentially breaking bug fix: Throw an error for mixins and functions that have rest parameters which are the same as normal parameters. Previously, the positional parameters wouldn't be accessible and calling such a mixin or function with a named argument would crash the compiler.

  • Potentially breaking bug fix: Fix various cases where using a CSS escape code at the beginning of an identifier would change parsing behavior versus using the character directly.

Release notes

Sourced from react-window's releases.

2.4.1

  • Fix performance issues for fixed-size rows or columns with a size of 0 (e.g. a percentage size before the container has been measured). Rendering no longer computes and caches bounds for every item, and only the first item is rendered (previously the last items were rendered, or every item if the scroll offset was negative). title: build: bump p-queue from 9.3.3 to 10.0.0
description:
Bumps [p-queue](https://github.com/sindresorhus/p-queue) from 9.3.3 to 10.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from p-queue's releases.

v10.0.0

Breaking

  • Require Node.js 22 300a52d
  • The queue is now an EventTarget instead of an EventEmitter 300a52d
    • Use .addEventListener() and .removeEventListener() instead of .on(), .once(), .off(), and the other EventEmitter methods.
    • The completed and error events have the result or the error in event.detail.
    • An error thrown in an event listener now exits the process. Node.js reports it as an uncaught exception.
  • .clear() now rejects the promises of the removed tasks with an AbortError instead of leaving them pending forever 64311ff
    • .clear() marks these promises as handled, but a promise made from them, like the one from .addAll() or queue.add(fn).then(…), now rejects, so handle it.
  • TimeoutError is now a DOMException named TimeoutError, like the error of AbortSignal.timeout() 300a52d
  • Remove the deprecated carryoverConcurrencyCount option: use carryoverIntervalCount 300a52d
  • Stricter validation of options 76a48ba d65d567
    • concurrency and intervalCap must be integers (or Infinity). A limit of 1.5 used to let 2 tasks run.
    • timeout and interval above 2147483647 ms (the maximum timer delay) are rejected. They used to fire after 1 ms.
    • .add() rejects with a TypeError when priority is NaN or not a number.
  • .start(), .clear(), and setting concurrency no longer emit empty and idle when the queue is already empty, so idle no longer fires on a queue that never had a task aeedf53
  • A custom queueClass must now implement remove() 300a52d

Improvements

  • Zero dependencies! 300a52d
  • A task now runs in the async context of its .add() call, so it sees the AsyncLocalStorage values of the caller, also when it starts later (Node.js 22.3 and later, Deno, and Bun) (#200) a5b7b54
    • Previously, a waiting task could see the values of whatever started it, like another request on a server.
  • A task with a timeout now gets a signal that aborts when the task times out, so you can pass it on to fetch() and similar to stop the work 300a52d
  • .onEmpty() and the empty event now fire when the last waiting task starts, not when the next task finishes 1cf5b82 cb25a0a
  • .addAll() now resolves with a typed tuple when the tasks return different types 36e83aa

Fixes

  • Fix many rate-limit bugs where intervalCap was exceeded at the end of a window, a waiting task got stuck, or isRateLimited was wrong 6af55a7 1cf5b82 6c08a4f ac89911 450356a
  • Fix slow add, run, and abort for many tasks that share a signal, and PriorityQueue keeping finished tasks in memory 95622a4 6fb8337
  • Fix many edge cases with events and priorities, like infinite recursion in an idle listener and events in the wrong order aeedf53 b33dd44 8792846 e79f970 d65d567 6f6028a
  • Fix undefined options and an invalid .timeout setter breaking the queue d6cf96b 48586f4
  • Fix many TypeScript types 36e83aa fa3c3e0

Migration guide

Events

-queue.on('completed', result => {
-	console.log(result);
-});
+queue.addEventListener('completed', event => {
+	console.log(event.detail);
+});
