title: fix: keep the visual editor's insert symbol popup open across decoration-only transactions
description:
In the visual editor, the Insert Special Characters > Emoji and Insert Special Characters > Unicode popups close on their own about five seconds after the editor is first focused, usually while the user is still typing a search term.

### Cause

`RealtimeSpellingPlugin` (`packages/editor/src/behaviors/spelling/spelling-realtime.ts`) subscribes to the editor's first `FocusEvent` and schedules `updateSpelling()` twice, at 100ms and at 5s. Each call dispatches a transaction carrying only the `updateSpelling` meta; the realtime-spelling preference only gates the decorations computed from it, so the transaction is dispatched even when spelling is off.

`InsertSymbolPlugin` (`packages/editor/src/behaviors/insert_symbol/insert_symbol-plugin.tsx`) closed its popup from the plugin view's `update()` hook on every transaction. A popup still open when the 5s transaction lands is unmounted under the user.

Call stack from a captured repro (RStudio, Firefox 151): `focus` -> `emitEvent(FocusEvent)` -> spelling `setTimeout` -> `updateSpelling` -> `view.dispatch` -> `updatePluginViews` -> `InsertSymbolPlugin.update` -> `closePopup`.

### Fix

`update(view, prevState)` now closes the popup only when the document or the selection changed. Inserting a symbol still dispatches a document change, so the popup still closes after a selection is committed, and clicking elsewhere in the document still dismisses it. Decoration-only transactions leave it alone.

Review also turned up that the plugin's focus listener was registered for `'onfocus'`, which is not a DOM event, so the popup was never dismissed when focus moved elsewhere. It now listens for `'focusin'`, like the completion plugin. Because `Editor.commands()` refocuses the editor after every command unless `keepFocus` is false, and a toolbar menu takes DOM focus in RStudio, that refocus would have closed the popup before it rendered. The Emoji and Symbol commands therefore pass `keepFocus: false`; the popup focuses its own search input on mount and already returns focus to the editor on Escape and on insert.

### Verification

Harness-free Playwright script against an RStudio dev server, in the Playwright Linux image, with the fix applied to the served `panmirror.js` by string replacement:

- Before: open Insert Emoji right after switching a document to visual mode and idle in the popup. The popup disappears after 3 to 4 seconds in both Chromium 149 and Firefox 151. Typing a 27-character search and pressing Enter fails in Firefox in most runs and passes in Chromium only because it finishes just under the 5s mark.
- After: the popup survives a 7s idle in both browsers, and the typed emoji / unicode searches insert the expected characters.

This is what has been failing the "insert special characters" visual editor test in RStudio's Firefox e2e jobs since the panmirror pin moved to `release/rstudio-montauk-daisy`; the code involved is unchanged there, the newer bundle only shifted the timing.

title: Prevent duplicate Quarto groups in the Outline when settings change quickly
description:
Fixes #1209

## Problem

The Outline view can show more than one "Quarto" group for one document. We have had some reports of this in Positron too here and there, but without a firm repro. Seems like this problem can occur when settings change quickly, for example while VS Code starts.

The LSP registers its document symbol provider again each time the configuration changes. Each update disposes the old registration and then waits for a new one. If two updates overlap, both updates dispose the same old registration. Then the second assignment overwrites the first new registration, so the server cannot dispose it later. Each leaked registration adds one more "Quarto" group to the Outline.

## Changes

- The new `documentSymbolRegistrar` in `apps/lsp/src/symbol-registration.ts` puts updates in a queue, so only one update runs at a time. As a result, at most one registration is active, and the last value of `showCodeCellsInOutline` sets the final state.
- If the value of `showCodeCellsInOutline` did not change, the registrar does not register again. The client sends configuration and theme notifications for any setting change, so this skip also stops Outline refreshes that are not necessary.
- If a registration fails, the registrar logs the error and the queue continues. The next update tries again. Before this change, if the first registration failed during startup, `mdLsReady` did not resolve, and symbol and folding requests did not complete.
- The server now attaches the configuration listener before the first registration. As a result, a setting change during startup goes into the queue and is not lost.
- `apps/lsp` now has unit tests for overlapping updates, fast toggles, the skip, and recovery after a failed registration. The overlap and toggle tests fail against the previous code. `npm run test-packages` now includes `quarto-lsp`.

## How to test

1. Open a `.qmd` file that has headings and code cells.
2. Show the Outline view.
3. Run _Developer: Reload Window_ several times. Make sure that the Outline shows one "Quarto" group each time.
4. Run _Quarto: Toggle Code Cells in Outline_ several times quickly. Make sure that the Outline shows one group, and that the code cells match the final setting.
5. Change the color theme. Make sure that the Outline keeps its expanded and collapsed state.

title: don't treat programmatic selection changes as cursor movement in AceNodeView
description:
Fixes #1099.

`AceNodeView.setSelection()` sets `this.updating`, focuses the Ace editor and applies a selection range. That fires `changeCursor`, and the handler set `cursorDirty` without consulting `this.updating` — so the next Ace render called `scrollCursorIntoView()` and scrolled the editing root to that node view, even though nothing moved the cursor. The value-change handlers just above (L508/L513) already guard on `this.updating`; this one didn't.

ProseMirror calls `setSelection()` from `selectionToDOM()` on every `EditorView.focus()`, so any focus restore scrolled the document to whichever embedded editor held the selection. For a freshly opened document that selection is at position 0 — the YAML front matter block — so the document snapped to the very top. In RStudio this shows up as the visual editor jumping to the top of the document whenever you run a code chunk in a file you have just opened (rstudio/rstudio#18490); clicking once anywhere in the prose moves the selection out of an `AceNodeView` and the symptom disappears until the file is reopened.

### Verification

Tested against an RStudio development build by serving a patched `panmirror.js` to the browser and leaving everything else identical, measuring `.pm-scroll-container` scrollTop across a chunk run:

|          | run 1 | run 2 |
|----------|-------|-------|
| before   | jumps 215px to the top, then scrolls back | jumps 163px to the top, then scrolls back |
| after    | no movement | no movement |

Genuine cursor-driven scrollback is unchanged: scrolling a focused code chunk out of view and pressing an arrow key still brings the cursor back into view, identically before and after.

### Notes

No `apps/vscode/CHANGELOG.md` entry — `aceExtension` is only installed when `options.codeEditor === 'ace'` (`editor-extensions.ts:222`), which is RStudio's configuration; the VS Code and Positron visual editors use the CodeMirror code view and are unaffected. Happy to add an entry if you'd rather have one.

title: don't intercept pastes inside citation ids
description:
Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18295

## Problem

In the visual editor on Windows, typing `@` and pasting a DOI (e.g. `https://doi.org/10.1000/182`) does nothing, whereas on Linux/macOS the editor offers to look up the DOI and insert a citation.

## Cause

ProseMirror consults `handlePaste` plugins in registration order, and the generic paste extension (`behaviors/paste.ts`) is registered before the cite mark's `paste_cite_doi` plugin. Inside a `cite_id` mark the generic handlers form a pincer that prevents `paste_cite_doi` from ever running on Windows:

- Clipboards carrying `text/html` (e.g. a DOI copied from a browser page) are consumed by `pasteHtmlHandler`'s `isWindows()` branch (the workaround for ProseMirror freezing on multi-paragraph pastes).
- Plain-text-only clipboards are consumed by `pasteMarkdownHandler` (the cite marks don't set `noInputRules`, so `allowMarkdownPaste` returns true inside a citation). This variant also affects macOS and Linux.

Since `isWindows()` keys off the user agent, this affects any Windows client, including browsers connecting to a Linux server.

## Fix

Both generic handlers now return `false` when the selection is inside a `cite_id` mark, allowing the cite mark's own paste handler to process the paste (insert the DOI, offer to insert a citation, or fall back to a plain-text insert for non-DOI content).

## Tests

Added `apps/vscode/src/test/editor-paste.test.ts` covering the fixed cases plus the preserved behaviors (Office content and Windows `text/html` pastes outside citations are still handled, plain text outside citations is still pasted as markdown). The 3 regression cases fail without the fix.

The tests live in the vscode extension suite (rather than `packages/editor`, whose jest-style tests under `test/api` are orphaned -- no runner is configured for them, and `test/README.md` notes their fixtures no longer work) because it is the only harness exercised by CI, and this avoids adding a new test runner dependency. The tests exercise the editor package directly and don't use the vscode API; the only dependency change is adding the `editor` workspace package as a devDependency of the extension.

Verified `tsc --noEmit` and the panmirror bundle build pass. Manual verification on Windows is still pending.

title: friendlier error for DOIs without citation metadata
description:
When inserting a citation from a DOI, the lookup uses DOI content negotiation (an `Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json` header against `https://doi.org/<doi>`). For DOIs whose registration agency does not support content negotiation (e.g. `10.1000/182`, the DOI Handbook itself), the request just redirects to the HTML landing page, and the editor surfaced a raw JSON parse error:

> invalid json response body at https://www.doi.org/the-identifier/resources/handbook/ reason: Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON

This PR detects the "resolved, but not to JSON" case and reports a human-readable message instead:

> This DOI was found, but no citation data is available for it. This usually means the organization that registered the DOI does not support automatic citation lookup. To cite this work, you can add an entry to your bibliography manually.

Noticed while reviewing #1060 (https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto/pull/1060#pullrequestreview-4767976245).

Verified manually by calling `doiServer().fetchCSL()` directly: `10.1000/182` now returns the friendly error, and a real Crossref DOI (`10.1038/nature12373`) still returns CSL metadata.

title: Visual editor selection support (getSelectedText + selection-change e…
description:
## Motivation

VS Code extensions can read the active editor's selection via `window.activeTextEditor.selection`, but Quarto's visual editor is a webview-based custom editor — its selection lives inside the webview and isn't visible to VS Code's text-editor API. As a result, extensions that act on the current selection (e.g. word-count tools, or sending a snippet to another command) work in source mode but go blind in visual mode. This PR exposes the visual editor's selection through Quarto's public extension API so those integrations work in both modes.

## Summary

Adds read access to the Quarto **visual editor's text selection**, in two layers:

### 1. `getSelectedText()` — pull the current selection on demand
Plumbs a new `getSelectedText()` method through every layer of the editor RPC stack:

- `EditorOperations.getSelectedText()` and the `Editor` implementation (`packages/editor`)
- The `EditorOperations` object built in `Editor.tsx` (`packages/editor-ui`)
- The `VSCodeVisualEditor` interface and the `VSC_VE_GetSelectedText` RPC constant (`packages/editor-types`)
- The webview host server and client transport (`apps/vscode-editor/sync.ts`, `apps/vscode/.../connection.ts`)
- A `quarto.editor.getSelectedText` command returning the selection, or `''` when no visual editor is active (`apps/vscode/.../editor.ts`)

`Editor.getSelectedText()` joins blocks with `\n\n`, preserves `hard_break` as a newline, and returns `''` for an empty selection.

### 2. `onDidChangeVisualEditorSelection` — push selection changes to API consumers
Exposes a new event on the already-public `QuartoExtensionApi`:

```ts
onDidChangeVisualEditorSelection: vscode.Event<{ uri: vscode.Uri; selectedText: string }>
```

It rides the existing `StateChangeEvent -> onEditorStateChanged` plumbing:

- The selected text is carried in the `onEditorStateChanged` RPC payload (sync/cheap), forwarded through the webview transport.
- It is re-emitted on a `vscode.EventEmitter` exposed by `createQuartoExtensionApi`.

Design decisions:
- **Push the text, not just a signal** — the webview already has it, avoiding a round-trip.
- **De-duplicate in Quarto** (per-document, against the previous selection), but **leave time-debouncing to consumers** — `StateChangeEvent` fires on every cursor move.
- **Empty selection (`''`) is a real event** so consumers can reset UI on clear/blur.
- The `getSelectedText` command remains as a backward-compatible pull-based fallback.

## Test plan

- [x] Build the VS Code extension (`yarn build-vscode`) — green across all packages
- [x] API tests pass (`yarn test-vscode --label main --grep "Quarto Extension API"`), including a new assertion that `onDidChangeVisualEditorSelection` is exposed
- [x] Command test asserts `quarto.editor.getSelectedText` returns `''` when no visual editor is active
- [ ] Manually: select text in the visual editor and confirm the command returns it and the event fires; confirm an empty selection emits `''`

🤖 AI disclosure - this change was generated with AI assistant Claude Code Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8

Updates `i18next` from 26.4.2 to 26.4.4
Release notes

Sourced from i18next's releases.

v26.4.4

  • fix(security): the nesting regexp no longer backtracks exponentially (ReDoS) on an unclosed $t(. Its repeated group had overlapping alternatives ([^()"']+ inside (?:...)*?, and inside parentheses [^()] also matched quotes), so a string containing $t( without a closing ) made the engine try every way to split the text: about 2x the runtime per extra character, and a ~25 character value hung t() for minutes. With the default config this was reachable through any interpolated value (t('greet', { name: '$t(aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' })): escaping does not touch $, t or (, and the skipOnVariables check runs the regexp on the interpolated result, so nest: false did not help either. Every alternative now starts with a different character (plain char, ", ' or (), so there is only one way to match and the cost is linear. Quoted strings and one level of parentheses in nesting options keep working (#2336). The only difference: a lone " or ' inside unquoted parentheses within $t(...) is no longer matched. Affects 25.3.3 to 26.4.3. Thanks to Anisetti Chaitanya Eshwar Prasad for the responsible disclosure.
  • fix(security): nest() now resolves $t(...) in a single pass and no longer nests text that came out of a resolved value. Every nested lookup reset the shared nesting regexp, so the loop started over from the beginning of the string after each match. That had two effects. First, a $t(...) inside a variable that the nested lookup deliberately kept literal (default skipOnVariables: true) was resolved anyway by the outer loop: with outer: 'A $t(inner) B' and inner: 'Hi {{name}}', t('outer', { name: '$t(secret)' }) rendered the secret translation. It now stays A Hi $t(secret) B, the same as without the outer nesting; with skipOnVariables: false it is still resolved. Second, the cost was quadratic when an unclosed $t( preceded many nestings, which matters when an app passes untrusted input as the key itself (t(userInput)): 20,000 nestings took ~1.4 s, now ~25 ms. prepare changelog for release
fix: quote document paths for the terminal's shell in preview and render
description:
`terminalCommand()` quotes the target path with `shQuote()`, but `shQuote()`
only quoted on whitespace. A path like `C:/dir(name)/file.qmd` was emitted
unquoted, so in the integrated PowerShell terminal `(name)` parsed as a
subexpression — and `md` is an alias for `mkdir`, stalling "Quarto: Preview"
at a `Path[0]:` prompt. (Bare parens are equally a syntax error in bash.)

`shQuote()` now quotes on whitespace or any shell-special character. Also
fixed `pythonIsCondaEnv()` passing a shell-quoted path to `execFileSync`,
which spawns no shell.

Fixes #1194

title: Show Positron's Viewer stop button for Quarto previews
description: - Addresses posit-dev/positron#10753 - Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/16602 In Positron, the Viewer now shows a stop button for Quarto previews. Before this PR, the only way to stop `quarto preview` was to find the Quarto Preview terminal and press Ctrl+C or close the terminal. The Positron PR adds `PreviewPanel.stoppable` and `onDidRequestStop` to the Positron API. The extension sets `stoppable` while the preview server runs, and Positron shows the button and reports clicks. Quarto starts and stops the server, so Quarto decides when the button shows. The extension uses feature detection (`"onDidRequestStop" in panel`), not a version check. On older Positron versions and in VS Code, nothing changes. A local type covers the new members until `@posit-dev/positron` ships them, so `engines.positron` does not change. Some known limitations: - Without shell integration (for example, the Windows `cmd` path), Ctrl+C in the terminal leaves the button visible until the terminal closes. A click on this button does no harm, and it closes the preview. - A re-render restarts the server. If the user clicks stop during this short time, the new server can still start and open the preview again. A second click stops it. ## Verification - `yarn build-test`: passes, including `tsc --noEmit`. - `yarn test` (label `main`): the 6 new tests pass. 178 passing, 3 pending, 1 failing. The failure is the notebook renderer build test, which fails on stale chunks in my local `out/markdownit`. This PR does not change that code. - ESLint on the changed files: no new warnings. - Manual test in Positron, built from the branch of the Positron PR: - Preview a document. title: build: override Mermaid's KaTeX to 0.18, drop the which dependency
description: Two small dependency cleanups. ## Changes - **KaTeX override.** Mermaid 11.17.2 depends on `katex ^0.16.47`, which has [GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7) (low: prototype pollution elsewhere on the page can turn on KaTeX's `trust` option). The fix is in 0.18.2, and no 0.16.x release has it. The root `package.json` now has `"overrides": { "mermaid": { "katex": "^0.18.2" } }`, which resolves to 0.18.10. - **Why it's safe:** Mermaid 12.2 moved to `katex ^0.18.0`, and its KaTeX code (`renderKatexUnsanitized`: dynamic `import("katex")`, then `renderToString` with MathML output by default) is identical to 11.17.2's. KaTeX's breaking changes don't apply here. 0.17 changed an internal `__defineFunction` API, and 0.18 prefixes KaTeX's CSS classes, which only matters for HTML output styled by KaTeX's stylesheet. We use MathML output and don't load that stylesheet. - **When to remove it:** once Mermaid is at 12.2 or later. npm `overrides` can't carry a comment, so this is recorded here. - **This is scanner hygiene, not a security fix.** It clears the runtime finding from `npm audit`, Dependabot and Snyk, so it doesn't sit open until Mermaid 12. The one place it changes code is the notebook renderer, where the advisory already couldn't do harm: the renderer shows Mermaid's SVG as an `` data URL, so links, scripts and external resources in it are inert. - **Not covered:** the diagram preview's checked-in `assets/www/diagram/mermaid.min.js` is Mermaid's prebuilt bundle with KaTeX 0.16.47 compiled in, so no override or lockfile change reaches it. It's also the more exposed of the two, since `diagram.js` inserts the SVG with `innerHTML` (after Mermaid's default `strict` DOMPurify pass). Fixing it needs Mermaid 12, or bundling Mermaid for the preview ourselves. Scanners don't see that file. - **Drop `which`** (and `@types/which`). It was used once, in `activePythonInterpreter`, to resolve a bare `python` name from the Python extension against `PATH`. A small local `findOnPath` helper now does that, following which@3's rules: `PATHEXT` on Windows, quoted `PATH` entries, executable files only. Names with a directory part are left as they are, as before. which 7 needs Node ≥22.22, newer than VS Code 1.101's extension host, so this also removes a reason for a Dependabot ignore (#1198). ## Verification - `package-lock.json` diff: only `which`, `@types/which`, and `katex` 0.16.47 → 0.18.10 (with its CLI's `commander` 8 → 15, which isn't bundled). `npm ls --all` exits 0. - `npm audit --omit=dev`: 2 low → **0**. - `npm run build -- --force`: 9/9. The notebook renderer's `out/markdownit/katex-*.js` chunk is 0.18.10. - `npm run lint -- --continue`: 17/17, 0 errors, 17 warnings (unchanged). `npm run test-packages`: 13/13. - Headless Chromium, with Mermaid 11.17.2 bundled the way our renderer bundles it (from `mermaid.core.mjs`, so it uses our KaTeX): a flowchart with `$$x^2 + \frac{a}{b}$$` and `$$\sqrt{\alpha}$$` labels and a sequence diagram with `$$\sum_{i=1}^n i$$` render with `` elements, no syntax error, and no console errors or warnings. - `findOnPath` gives the same result as `command -v` for `python3`, `python` (absent), `node`, `git` and a missing name, on macOS. Not checked on Windows. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: build: add Dependabot for npm dependencies
description:
Turns on Dependabot version updates now that the repo is on npm (#1196).

## Changes

New `.github/dependabot.yml` with one `npm` entry at `/`, which covers every workspace through the root `package-lock.json`:

- **Schedule:** weekly, with a **7-day cooldown** (`cooldown.default-days: 7`), so a release has to be a week old before it's proposed.
- **Grouping:** all minor and patch updates go into one `npm-minor-and-patch` PR. Each major update gets its own PR.
- **`versioning-strategy: increase`:** raises the floor in every workspace that declares the package, so ranges stay unified, as the upgrade PRs did by hand.
- **Commit prefix `build`**, to match the repo's `build: …` PR titles. `open-pull-requests-limit: 10`.
- **Ignored**, because they're held back on purpose:
  - `@types/vscode`: all updates. It has to match `engines.vscode` (`^1.101.0`).
  - `@types/node`: majors. It stays on 22, the Node of the oldest supported extension host.
  - `which`: 7 and later, which needs Node ≥22.22. 4–6 are allowed.
  - `mocha`: majors. `@vscode/test-cli` 0.0.15 doesn't support mocha 12.
  - `typescript`: 6.1 and later. typescript-eslint caps its peer range at `<6.1`, and TS 7 has no JS API yet.
  - `markdown-it-attrs`: majors. 5.x calls `require('markdown-it')`, which bundles a second markdown-it.
  - `prettier`: majors. Prettier 3 comes with a repo-wide reformat.
  - `mermaid`: all updates. It must be the exact version of the diagram preview's vendored `mermaid.min.js` (`mermaidVersion.test.ts`), and it should follow quarto-cli.

GitHub Actions updates aren't included.

## Verification

- `check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.dependabot` passes.
- The real check is the first run after merge: the Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot tab shows whether the config parsed and what each job did.

title: build: switch from Yarn 1 to npm
description:
Replaces Yarn 1 with npm workspaces. Supersedes #970, which went stale.

## Changes

- **Lockfile:** `yarn.lock` → `package-lock.json`. The lockfile was generated by running `npm install` with `yarn.lock` still present, so npm resolved every package to the version Yarn had locked. A script comparing the two lockfiles finds no version differences. The only additions are the platform-specific optional binaries (esbuild, rolldown, turbo, lightningcss, …), which npm records for every platform. That avoids the npm/cli#4828 problem of a lockfile that only works on the platform it was generated on. No `overrides` are needed (there were no `resolutions` left), and the workspace deps (`"core": "*"` etc.) all link to the local workspaces.
- **Root `package.json`:**
  - `packageManager` is `npm@11.19.0`, the npm that ships with Node 24.21. Turbo needs this field to detect the package manager, and with Corepack enabled it makes `yarn` refuse to run in the repo.
  - `allowScripts`: npm 11.19 warns about dependency install scripts that aren't reviewed, and a later npm will block them by default. Approved: `esbuild` (puts the native binary in place) and `@vscode/vsce-sign` (copies its platform binary, needed for `vsce`). Denied: `keytar` (only for `vsce login` credential storage; CI uses tokens), `@parcel/watcher` and `fsevents` (both ship prebuilt binaries; the scripts only build from source), and `core-js-pure` (a funding banner). The entries are name-only rather than version-pinned, so Dependabot bumps don't drop the approvals.
  - Root scripts pass arguments through, e.g. `npm run test-vscode -- --label main --grep pattern`.
- **Deleted `apps/vscode/.yarnrc`** (and its `.vscodeignore` line). vsce 4 runs `vscode:prepublish` with yarn when it finds that file. Its `--ignore-engines` isn't needed: npm doesn't enforce `engines` by default.
- **Scripts:** `yarn run build dev` → `npm run build -- dev` etc. in `apps/lsp` and `apps/vscode`.
- **CI:** `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` → `npm ci`, and `yarn <script>` → `npm run <script>`. `yarn --silent vsce/ovsx …` → `npx --no vsce/ovsx …`, which still uses the repo's pinned versions and fails rather than downloading if they're missing.
- **Editor tasks** (`apps/vscode/.vscode/tasks.json`, `launch.json`): the `yarn: dev-vscode` and `yarn: build-test` tasks are now `npm: …`.
- **Docs:** README, `apps/vscode/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `claude.md`, and the "update snapshots" comments in the tests.

## Verification

On Node 24.21 / npm 11.19, from a clean `node_modules`:

- `npm ci`: lockfile unchanged; `npm ls --all` exits 0.
- `npm run build -- --force`: 9/9 tasks.
- `npm run test-packages`: 13/13 tasks.
- `npm run lint -- --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, 17 warnings, the same as on `main`.
- `npx --no vsce package` in `apps/vscode`: runs `npm run vscode:prepublish`, and packages 175 files.
- `npm run test-vscode -- --help`: the arguments reach `vscode-test`.
- `test-vscode` and `test-positron` weren't run locally (they open GUI windows); CI runs them.

## Snyk

The two Snyk checks error on 3 of 30 tests. #1195 passed them, so it's this switch, most likely Snyk projects that were imported from `yarn.lock`. Someone with access to the Snyk org needs to re-import the repo, or point those projects at `package-lock.json`.

## Rebasing

`package-lock.json` was regenerated after rebasing onto #1195 (React 19). Any other change to `yarn.lock` on `main` before this merges needs the same treatment: restore `main`'s `yarn.lock`, delete `package-lock.json` and `node_modules`, run `npm install`, delete `yarn.lock`, and recheck the version comparison. Open PRs that touch `yarn.lock` will need to port their changes to `package-lock.json` after this merges.

## Follow-ups

- Turn on Dependabot (npm ecosystem, plus GitHub Actions).
- `npm audit` reports 16 advisories (ajv, braces, diff, katex, serialize-javascript, source-map-js, …). They're the same package versions as on `main`, just reported by a different tool than Snyk. They should be handled separately.

title: build: upgrade React to 19.3 (react, react-dom, @types/react*)
description:
React PR 3 of 3 in the dependency upgrade: React 19. It follows #1187 (React 18.3, the automatic JSX runtime, react-window 2) and #1188 (Fluent UI 9.74, whose peer ranges accept React `<20`).

## Changes

**Packages.** `^19.3.0` in all four React workspaces (`apps/vscode-editor`, `packages/{editor,editor-ui,ui-widgets}`). 19.3.0 is the current `latest`.

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `react`, `react-dom` | 18.3.1 | 19.3.0 |
| `scheduler` | 0.23.2 | 0.28.0 |
| `@types/react` | 18.3.31 | 19.3.0 |
| `@types/react-dom` | 18.3.7 | 19.3.0 |
| `@types/prop-types` | 15.7.15 | removed (`@types/react` 19 no longer depends on it) |

- The lockfile has one copy each of `react`, `react-dom`, `scheduler`, `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom`, with no `resolutions`. `loose-envify` stays (still used by `prop-types`/`react-transition-group`), but only as one `^1.4.0` entry.
- No new peer warnings. The other React-peered dependencies already accept 19: Fluent 9.74.9 and `react-icons` 2.0.343 (`<20`), `react-redux` 9.3 (`^18 || ^19`), `react-window` 2.3 (`^18 || ^19`), `react-textarea-autosize` 8.5.9 (`^19`), `use-debounce` 10 (`*`), `react-transition-group` 4.4.5 (`>=16.6`). i18next has no React bindings here. The only React-related peer warning is the one that was already there: `react-context-selector`'s `scheduler` peer is not declared (`scheduler` is hoisted from `react-dom`, as before).

**Codemods**, committed separately so they're easy to review:
- `codemod react/19/migration-recipe` changed nothing, as expected: no `ReactDOM.render`, string refs, `act`, `useFormState` or `propTypes`.
- `types-react-codemod preset-19` (3.5.3) changed 11 files. Its output is in its own commit, unedited.

**Hand fixes** (in a separate commit after that):
- `CommandSubMenu`: `isValidElement<CommandMenuItemProps>(child)`. In types 19, `ReactElement` props default to `unknown`.
- `JSX.Element` → `React.JSX.Element` (in `alert.tsx`, `ModalDialog.tsx`, `nonideal.tsx` and `text-popup.ts`). That matches what `Menu.tsx` already does, and it replaces the `type JSX` imports the codemod added.
- `insert-cite.tsx`: the `useRef()` the codemod turned into `useRef(undefined)` is a DOM ref, so it's now `useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)`.
- I reverted the codemod's `ReactElement` → `ReactElement<any>` widening at two sites, because the `unknown` default type-checks there. `HotkeysProvider`'s `children` was `ReactChild`, which types 19 removes. It's now `ReactElement | number | string`, which is what `ReactChild` meant, without the codemod's `any`.
- `insert_symbol-popup.tsx`'s `lastElement()` now returns `RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` (the codemod made this change).
- Nothing else was needed. The Fluent `Slot` types, the `forwardRef` components and the Menu positioning ref in `menu/context.tsx` all type-check under 19's `RefObject` without changes.

There's no CHANGELOG line, because nothing here should be user-visible.

**Not done:**
- `onUncaughtError` on the editor's root (optional step 16 in the plan). React 19 sends uncaught render errors to `window.reportError` instead of rethrowing them. That only changes what the webview console shows.
- `Alert` from `@fluentui/react-components/unstable` in `html-dialog.tsx` is still there (see #1188). Replacing it with `MessageBar` would change how the progress overlay looks.
- I didn't convert any `forwardRef` components to `ref`-as-prop. `forwardRef` still works in 19.

## Verification

On Node 24.21:
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks, including `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/vscode-editor` and `apps/panmirror`, which are the only type-checks of the React packages.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, and the same 17 warnings in `quarto` as on `main`.
- `yarn test-packages`: 13/13 tasks.
- `yarn test-vscode`: I couldn't run it headless locally (the Docker daemon isn't running), so I'm leaving it to CI's `xvfb-run yarn test-vscode`, which includes the visual-editor roundtrip tests that load the React webview.
- **The bundle is React 19.** `apps/vscode/assets/www/editor/index.js` and `apps/panmirror/dist/panmirror.js` both have `version:"19.3.0"` and `react.transitional.element`. The single remaining `react.element` is react-dom 19's check for legacy elements.

  | | `main` | this branch | delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | editor `index.js` | 10,382,968 B (3,213,688 B gzip) | 10,462,623 B (3,237,253 B gzip) | +79.7 KB (+23.6 KB gzip) |
  | `panmirror.js` | 8,557,971 B (2,631,964 B gzip) | 8,637,513 B (2,655,634 B gzip) | +79.5 KB (+23.7 KB gzip) |

- **Runtime check in headless Chromium.** A small Vite page that imports `editor-ui`, built against both React 18.3.1 (`main`'s lockfile) and 19.3.0, in both production and development React builds:
  - `alert()`: the Fluent `Dialog` renders through the ui-widgets dialog root, and OK resolves and unmounts it.
  - `showContextMenu()`: the menu lands at the virtual-element position (it opens at (205, 155) for a click at (200, 150), the same as on 18), the submenu opens on hover, the nested item fires, and the root unmounts.
  - The toolbar `Menu`: trigger click, submenu hover, and item click.

  Every result was identical on 18 and 19, and React logged no warnings in the development build. Both versions also log a Fluent `Keyborg instance … is being disposed incorrectly` error in development, so that one isn't new.

### Manual checks in the Extension Development Host

Open a `.qmd`, switch to the visual editor, and keep the webview devtools console open throughout. Look for React errors or warnings, including *"Attempted to synchronously unmount a root while React was already rendering"*.
1. **Dialogs**: edit attributes, image, link, callout, code block, table, tabset, list, math, raw, Insert Citation by DOI, and an alert/yes-no. Check that each opens, that OK and Cancel work, and that focus lands in the first field (the `insert-cite` ref changed).
2. **Menus**: the menubar and toolbar menus (including submenus such as Format → Text), and the right-click context menu, which should open at the cursor.
3. **Outline sidebar**: expand/collapse, and click and Enter to navigate.
4. **Completion popups**: `@` for citations and cross references, and `:` for emoji. Each should open, filter as you type, and close cleanly.
5. **Find/replace**: the open and close animation, and the debounced search while typing.
6. **Insert → Citation**: switch source panels, type-ahead search, arrow keys through the results, and the detailed list in a Crossref/DOI search.
7. **Insert → Cross Reference**: arrow keys scroll the selection into view; double-click inserts.
8. **Insert → Special Characters / Emoji**: keyboard navigation scrolls the grid, and Tab reaches the skin-tone panel (the `lastElement()` ref change).
9. Attribute-editor decorations on headings and divs, and link/citation hover popups. Delete the node and check that nothing is logged.
10. Light and dark themes.

title: feat: add an experimental quarto.validate.links.enabled setting for LSP link diagnostics
description:
Fixes #1185

The language server's link diagnostics (undefined reference links, missing headers, missing files, unused and duplicate link definitions) could never be turned on. `ConfigurationManager.update()` rebuilt `markdown.validate` from the defaults (`enabled: false`) on every update and never read it from the client. This has been the case since 09dc066d (2023).

Following the discussion below (option 1), the diagnostics are now turned on by a new Quarto setting, and the false positives on Quarto's explicit identifiers are fixed.

## Changes

- **New setting `quarto.validate.links.enabled`** (boolean, default `false`, tagged `experimental`). It's the only switch for link diagnostics in Quarto documents.
  - The level of each rule, and the links to skip, are still read from VS Code's `markdown.validate.*` settings: `referenceLinks.enabled`, `fragmentLinks.enabled`, `fileLinks.enabled`, `fileLinks.markdownFragmentLinks`, `unusedLinkDefinitions.enabled`, `duplicateLinkDefinitions.enabled` and `ignoredLinks`. Missing or invalid values fall back to VS Code's defaults (`warning`, or `hint` for unused definitions), so the setting still works if the client doesn't send them.
  - `markdown.validate.enabled` is ignored. Users who turned it on for `.md` files don't get new warnings in `.qmd` files.
  - The setting's description notes the known limitation: links to files that only exist after rendering (such as `other.html`) are reported as missing, and suggests linking to the `.qmd` source or using `markdown.validate.ignoredLinks`.
- **Explicit identifiers are link targets** (`apps/lsp/src/service/toc.ts`). The table of contents used only the identifier generated from a heading's text, so `[see](#sec-intro)` pointing at `## Introduction {#sec-intro}` was reported as "No header found".
  - As in Pandoc, a heading's explicit `{#id}` (already parsed into the token's `attr` by quarto-core) replaces the generated identifier, and is reserved so a later generated identifier doesn't reuse it. Besides diagnostics, this fixes go to definition, find references, highlights and `#` path completions for such headings. They used the generated identifier before, and that identifier doesn't exist in the rendered document.
  - Divs with an identifier (`::: {#fig-x}`, `::: {.callout-note #nte-x}`, `::: {#thm-x}`) are now valid fragment targets. They're kept in a separate list from the outline entries, so the outline, folding, smart select and completions don't change. Code cell labels (`#| label: fig-x`) were already targets.
- `apps/lsp` gets its first unit tests (`test/config.test.ts`, `test/link-targets.test.ts`, helpers in `test/workspace.ts`) and a `test` script, and `yarn test-packages` now includes `quarto-lsp`. They cover:
  - the setting off: no diagnostics, even with `markdown.validate.enabled: true`;
  - the setting on: diagnostics, with levels from `markdown.validate.*`, and VS Code's defaults when those are missing or invalid;
  - explicit heading identifiers, div identifiers and code cell labels resolving, in the same file and in another file, while `#introduction` for `## Introduction {#sec-intro}` is still flagged;
  - divs staying out of the outline, and find references and go to definition for an explicit identifier.
- `apps/vscode/src/test/lsp-features.test.ts`: an end-to-end test turns on `quarto.validate.links.enabled`, waits for a diagnostic on a broken fragment link in a new fixture (`lsp-link-diagnostics.qmd`), then turns the setting off and waits for the diagnostic to clear. The existing `lsp-features.qmd` fixture linked `[the section](#first-section)` to `## First Section {#sec-first}`, a link that's broken in the rendered document; it now links to `#sec-first`, so the "references to a header" test checks the Pandoc behavior.
- Two `apps/vscode/CHANGELOG.md` lines: the new setting, and the explicit identifier fix.

### Not covered, for follow-ups

- **Other Quarto cross-reference targets.** Identifiers attached to inline or block content that the LSP's block parser doesn't record are still flagged as missing when linked with `[..](#id)`: figures (`![](plot.png){#fig-x}`), tables (`: Caption {#tbl-x}`), equations (`$$ ... $$ {#eq-x}`), listings (code blocks with `{#lst-x}`), and spans (`[text]{#id}`). Quarto documents usually reference these with `@fig-x`, not links, so I left them out. Fixing them needs inline attribute parsing in quarto-core's markdown-it parser.
- **Rendered-output links.** Links to files that only exist after rendering (`other.html` from `other.qmd`) are reported as missing files. Quarto recommends linking to the `.qmd` source, so this is lower priority. It's noted in the setting's description.
- The other `markdown.*` settings the server models (`preferredMdPathExtensionStyle`, `suggest.paths.*`) are still never read from the client.
- #1139 (the middleware stub that replaces the definition handler) is related but separate, and isn't touched here.

## Verification

On Node 24, rebased onto `main` (a83c5cc5):

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`: lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks.
- `yarn test-packages`: 14/14 tasks (13 on `main`, plus `quarto-lsp`), including the 11 `quarto-lsp` tests.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, 17 warnings, all in `quarto`, the same as on `main`.
- `apps/vscode` `yarn build-test`: compiles.
- `yarn test-vscode` wasn't run locally: the VS Code tests open GUI windows, and no headless container was available. CI runs the new `lsp-features.test.ts` test.

title: build: remove packages/ojs (moving to quarto-cli)
description:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Don't merge this until quarto-cli has the OJS sources** (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15043). Merging first would leave the runtime with no home.

The OJS runtime and the vendored Observable subtrees are moving to quarto-cli, which is where the runtime bundle ships (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15043). This PR now removes `packages/ojs/` from this repo.

This PR started as a modernization of `quarto-ojs-runtime`'s rollup tooling: rollup 4, `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve` 16, `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` 29, `@rollup/plugin-terser`, mime 4, and dropping unused dependencies. That work is commit `acd4fec2` in this PR's history (with `d6d16518` before it), so quarto-cli can take it along with the sources, as #15043 asks.

## Changes

- Delete `packages/ojs/`: `quarto-ojs-runtime` and the five vendored subtrees (`@observablehq/parser`, `runtime` and `stdlib`, `d3-require`, and the unofficial compiler).
- Remove the `packages/ojs/*` workspace from the root `package.json`.
- Prune `yarn.lock`: 279 entries go, and nothing is added. This removes these dev-only duplicates and advisories:
  - rollup 1, 2, 3 and 4, `rollup-plugin-*`, `@rollup/*` and terser.
  - mocha 9 (with nanoid 3.3.1 and the js-yaml 4.1.0 pin) and mocha 10. mocha 11 is the only one left.
  - eslint 8 and its ESLint 8 dependencies, prettier 1, and `@types/node` 14.
  - `http-server` and `union`, which also removes `qs` 6.14.0. One `qs` (6.16.0) and one `side-channel` are left.
  - exceljs, with its uuid 8 and dayjs 1.11.13.
  - minimatch 3, 4 and 5, glob 7 and 8, rimraf 2 and 3, `inflight`, `tape` and the `es-abstract` tree.
- README: remove the "OJS Runtime" (ISC) row from the license table.

No turbo config, CI workflow, ESLint config, `.gitignore`, `.vscodeignore` or other docs referred to `packages/ojs`. CI never built it. The extension's OJS language support (`{ojs}` cells, highlighting, comment characters, snippets) stays as it is.

## Verification

On Node 24, after merging `main`:

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 9/9 tasks, down from 14 because the five OJS builds are gone.
- `yarn test-packages`: 13/13 tasks.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, 17 warnings (all in `quarto`, the same as `main`).
- I didn't run `yarn test-vscode`, because OJS isn't part of the extension.

title: build: upgrade Mermaid to 11.17.2 in the notebook renderer and the diagram preview, unpin cytoscape
description:
Upgrades the Mermaid in both of the extension's Mermaid previews to **11.17.2**: - the notebook Markdown cell renderer (`apps/vscode-markdownit`, npm `mermaid`), from 9.4.3; - the Diagram preview (`apps/vscode/assets/www/diagram/mermaid.min.js`, vendored), from 11.12.0. It also releases the `cytoscape` 3.23.0 hold from #1176. **Why 11.17.2 and not Quarto CLI's 11.12:** - **Snyk.** Six Mermaid advisories affect every 11.12.x release and are fixed in 11.14.1 or 11.16.1: GHSA-c4c3-pg64-4m4v, GHSA-6x64-9x62-f2gx, GHSA-87f9-hvmw-gh4p, GHSA-xcj9-5m2h-648r, GHSA-ghcm-xqfw-q4vr and GHSA-6m6c-36f7-fhxh. They cover config prototype pollution, CSS and HTML injection, and a Gantt infinite loop. 11.17.2 has none. - **The syntax changes are additive.** 11.13–11.17 add new diagram types and node shapes (e.g. `venn-beta`, and `person` used below). They deprecate `flowchart.htmlLabels` and `mermaidAPI.setConfig()`, and nothing here uses either. - **We drift only by being ahead.** A diagram that `quarto render` (11.12) accepts also renders here. The reverse doesn't always hold, since newer syntax can preview here and then fail in the CLI. `mermaidVersion.test.ts` already allows us to be ahead of the CLI; it fails only if we fall behind. - **One visible default change:** in 11.17, `classDiagram` and C4 moved to Mermaid's unified (v2) renderer. Class and C4 diagrams will look somewhat different from the CLI's 11.12 output until the CLI catches up. I'll open a quarto-cli issue to bump its Mermaid once this merges. Out of scope, and still deferred to the UX review: whether to keep our notebook Mermaid rendering next to VS Code 1.121's built-in notebook Mermaid, and `securityLevel: "loose"` vs. inline SVG. The notebook output model is unchanged: an inert `` with the SVG as a data URL. ## Changes **Packages.** `mermaid` `^9.1.7` → `~11.17.2` in `apps/vscode-markdownit`, the only workspace that imports it. - I script-deleted the lock entries that only Mermaid reached and re-ran `yarn install`. Entries shared with other workspaces kept their locks (`d3-array`/`d3-dsv` for OJS, `lodash-es`, `lodash`, …). No `resolutions`. | Package | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `mermaid` | 9.4.3 | 11.17.2 | | `cytoscape` | 3.23.0 (held) | 3.34.3 | | `cytoscape-fcose` / `-cose-bilkent` | 2.2.0 / 4.1.0 | same | | `d3` | 7.9.0 | same | | `dompurify` | 2.4.3 | 3.4.16 | | `dagre-d3-es` | 7.0.9 | 7.0.14 | | `@mermaid-js/parser` | — | 1.2.1 (Langium and Chevrotain are bundled in it) | | `katex` | — | 0.16.47 (lazy chunk) | | `uuid` | 9.0.x | 14.0.2 | | new | — | `marked` 16.4.2, `roughjs` 4.6.6, `@iconify/utils` 3.1.7, `es-toolkit` 1.52.0, `fastdom` 1.0.12 (+ `strictdom`), `@upsetjs/venn.js` 2.0.0, `dayjs` 1.11.23 | | removed | present | `elkjs`, `web-worker`, `non-layered-tidy-tree-layout`, `heap` | - **Duplicates:** there's one copy each of `cytoscape`, `dompurify`, `katex`, `d3` and `@mermaid-js/parser`. The rest: - `d3-sankey` 0.12.3 (a Mermaid dependency) still requires the d3 v1/v2 line, so `d3-array` 2.12.1, `d3-path` 1, `d3-shape` 1 and `internmap` 1 sit next to the v3 copies, as they do upstream. - `marked` 16 (Mermaid) is separate from `marked` 18 (vsce, dev-only). - `uuid` 14 (Mermaid) is separate from `uuid` 8 (exceljs, OJS, dev-only). - `dayjs` 1.11.23 (Mermaid) is separate from 1.11.13 (exceljs, OJS, dev-only). **Diagram preview.** `assets/www/diagram/mermaid.min.js` is now `dist/mermaid.min.js` from the `mermaid@11.17.2` npm tarball. - That's the same provenance as before: the 11.12.0 file it replaces was byte-identical to `mermaid@11.12.0`'s `dist/mermaid.min.js`, which is what quarto-cli vendors. - It still sets `globalThis.mermaid`, and `diagram.js` works unchanged with its async `parse`/`render` and `initialize({ startOnLoad: false })`. - Size: 2,748,992 → 3,572,661 B. **Async rendering in the notebook renderer** (`apps/vscode-markdownit/src/mermaid.ts`). Mermaid 10 removed `mermaidAPI.render`'s synchronous callback, but markdown-it renderer rules have to return a string synchronously. So now: - The fence rule emits `
`. `N` comes from a module-wide counter, so ids stay unique across renders. It wraps `md.renderer.render` to collect the diagrams from that call. - VS Code's notebook Markdown renderer sets `previewNode.innerHTML` synchronously right after `md.render` returns. So a microtask then loads Mermaid (on the first diagram only, with `import("mermaid")`), calls `mermaid.initialize`, and awaits `mermaid.render` for each diagram. Afterwards it looks the placeholder up in the cell's shadow root, via `env.outputItem.id`, the same hook VS Code's built-in Mermaid renderer uses. If that fails, it searches the open shadow roots. - The placeholder gets an `` built with DOM APIs. Its `max-width` is taken from the SVG's root `style`, since the old code read it from Mermaid 9's temporary element. On an error, the placeholder instead gets a `
Failed to render mermaid diagram. …
`, set through `textContent`. The error only replaces that one diagram, so other diagrams and cells still render. `suppressErrorRendering: true` stops Mermaid from drawing its own error diagram. - If a cell re-renders while an earlier render is still running, the earlier render can't find its (now removed) placeholder, so it drops its result. No stale SVGs. - Nothing is written into the page as markup, so the Restricted Mode sanitizer isn't bypassed, and `securityLevel: "loose"` stays as inert as before inside the ``. The placeholder class is `quarto-mermaid`, not `mermaid`, so VS Code's built-in renderer (it selects `.mermaid`) ignores it. - **Theme:** `dark` or `default`, from the same `vscode-dark`/`vscode-high-contrast` body classes as before. It's now read on every render instead of once at activation, so a re-rendered cell picks up a theme switch. The callout colors in `index.ts` are still read once. - **AMD `define`:** another renderer in the notebook webview can load an AMD loader (RequireJS). fastdom's UMD wrapper (new in Mermaid 11.17) then calls `define()` instead of setting `module.exports`, and Mermaid fails to load with "h.default.extend is not a function". `vite.config.ts` now defines `define` as `undefined`, so no bundled UMD wrapper checks for it. - I dropped the `...options` spread into `mermaid.initialize`, which passed our `{ dark }` through as a Mermaid config key. I also removed the stale `// TODO: mermaid breaks other plugins`. It dates from April 2023, when the plugin was briefly commented out, and was left in when it was re-enabled the next day. The rendering check below renders Mermaid next to callouts, divs and footnotes. **Tests:** - Node doesn't load Mermaid anymore (the fence rule doesn't touch it), so the test-only Mermaid/DOM stub is gone. - The `quarto-syntax` snapshot changes only where the two Mermaid fences were. They used to be ``s of the stub's fake SVG, and now they're the two placeholders. - A new test checks that re-rendering the same source produces fresh ids. - A new `Notebook renderer build` test fails if any built chunk in `out/markdownit` still has a `typeof define` check. - `mermaidVersion.test.ts`: - **The notebook renderer and the Diagram preview must be on the exact same Mermaid version.** Both come from the same npm release, and re-vendoring is a file copy from `node_modules/mermaid/dist/`. So an exact match is cheap to keep, and it makes a diagram render identically in both. The version is read from the renderer's hashed chunks, and the test fails if stale chunks contain more than one version. - **Neither may be behind the installed Quarto CLI.** Being ahead is fine. On the `pre-release` channel this is still only a warning. - **Version reading:** Mermaid 11.17 builds no longer embed `name:"mermaid",version:"…"`. The reader now also recognizes the version literal that `render()` passes to each diagram's renderer (`renderer.draw(text, id, "11.17.2", diagram)`), in both minified and unminified builds. It still reads 11.12-style builds, such as the CLI's current one. ## Verification On Node 24.21: - `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged. - `yarn build --force`: 14/14. `yarn test-packages`: 13/13, including the renderer snapshot tests. `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17, 0 errors, the same 17 warnings. - `yarn test-vscode`, headless (Xvfb in a linux-arm64 container, VS Code 1.139.1, Quarto 1.10.18 with Mermaid 11.12.0, a clean extract of this branch): main 169 passing and 3 pending (`main` is at 168; the extra one is the new Mermaid version test), r-project 3 passing. All three Mermaid version tests pass, including "not behind the installed Quarto CLI" against the CLI's 11.12.0. - **The other bundles are unaffected.** `grep -c mermaidAPI` gives 0 for `out/main.js`, `out/lsp/lsp.js` and `assets/www/editor/index.js`, and their sizes are byte-identical to `main` (4,345,005 / 2,869,803 / 10,350,698 B). - **`out/markdownit`** (measured after a clean build): | | `main` (Mermaid 9.4.3) | this branch (11.17.2) | |---|---|---| | files | 7 (`index.js`, 5 chunks, `styles.css`) | 97 (`index.js`, 95 chunks, `styles.css`) | | total | 3,927,967 B | 4,535,087 B | | `index.js` | 117,260 B, statically importing the 1,141,217 B Mermaid chunk at activation | 118,553 B; Mermaid (113 KB core plus the diagram's chunks) loads with the first diagram | | largest chunk | 1,993,034 B (`flowchart-elk`) | 820,917 B | Mermaid 11 doesn't bundle ELK (it's the separate `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` package, which the IIFE build doesn't include either). The build is still an ES library with lazy chunks, which rolldown#11001 doesn't affect (that's a UMD issue), and the chunks load (below). - **Notebook renderer check in headless Chromium.** I served the built `out/markdownit` and mimicked `vscode.markdown-it-renderer`: a markdown-it instance with VS Code's options and `highlight`, plus a `renderOutputItem` that renders into a shadow root and passes `{ outputItem: { id } }`. - I rendered, in light, dark, and dark with DOMPurify using VS Code's untrusted-workspace `ALLOWED_TAGS` (simulating Restricted Mode): - flowchart, sequenceDiagram, mindmap, timeline, gantt, classDiagram, stateDiagram-v2 and a C4Context; - an `A@{ shape: text }` / `cyl` node, an `A@{ shape: person }` node, and a `venn-beta` diagram; - an invalid flowchart, and two diagrams in one cell (flowchart + pie); - a diagram between a callout, a `.column-margin` div and a footnote; - a `{mermaid}` attribute fence, and a cell re-rendered twice synchronously. - Every diagram became an `` with a non-zero size, with the dark theme's colors in dark. The class and C4 diagrams render with the new renderer. - The invalid one showed "Failed to render mermaid diagram. Parse error on line 2: …", and the rest of the page still rendered. - The shape syntax rendered its labels (not "undefined"). - The re-rendered cell showed only the second version. - 52 chunks loaded. There were no console errors and no failed requests. - That page had no global `define`, so it missed the AMD failure above. After the fix, I loaded each of the 95 built chunks in Node with a stub `define` (and `define.amd`) global, and they all load. Before the fix, the core chunk and `architectureDiagram` threw "h.default.extend is not a function". - **Diagram preview check in headless Chromium.** I loaded the preview page's scripts (`lodash`, the new `mermaid.min.js`, d3, graphviz, `diagram.js`) with a stubbed `acquireVsCodeApi`, and posted `render` messages. - `window.mermaid.parse`/`render`/`initialize` are functions. - A flowchart with a `person` node and a classDiagram rendered as SVG. - An invalid diagram showed the parse error banner. - There were no console errors. **Manual checks, please** (Extension Development Host, and Positron's legacy Jupyter notebook editor; the default Positron Notebook editor does its own Markdown and Mermaid rendering and doesn't use this renderer). Open an `.ipynb` whose Markdown cells contain: 1. The diagram types above (flowchart, sequence, mindmap, timeline, gantt, class, state-v2, C4, `A@{ shape: text }`, `venn-beta`), and check that they render and look reasonable next to `quarto render`'s output. 2. **Class diagram look:** compare a `classDiagram` (with members, methods and a few relationships) against `quarto render` on the CLI's 11.12. Differences are expected from the unified renderer; check that nothing is broken or unreadable, in both light and dark. 3. An invalid diagram: the error shows up in place of the diagram, and the other diagrams and cells still render. 4. Two diagrams in one cell. Then edit a cell several times: no stale or duplicated diagrams. 5. Mermaid next to callouts, divs and footnotes. 6. Theme switching: switch between light, dark and high contrast, then edit a cell. Its diagram should follow the new theme (the callout colors still need a reload). 7. **Restricted Mode** (untrusted workspace): diagrams still render. 8. **Developer: Open Webview Developer Tools** on the notebook: no CSP violations or failed chunk loads. 9. **Diagram preview:** in a `.qmd`, "Preview Diagram" on a `{mermaid}` cell (including a `classDiagram`) renders, and an invalid one shows the error banner. 10. **VS Code ≥ 1.121** (built-in Mermaid Markdown Features enabled): `` ```mermaid `` fences should render once, with our renderer (the ``), and not twice. Note any interaction with the built-in renderer (its `::: mermaid` container syntax is separate). This is input for the deferred UX review. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: build: upgrade Fluent UI to 9.74 (react-components, react-icons)
description:
This is React PR 2 of 3 in the dependency upgrade. It moves Fluent UI from 9.21 to 9.74 while we're still on React 18.3. React 19 (PR 3) needs Fluent 9.70 or later, because 9.21's peer range is `react <19`.

## Changes

**Packages.** I deleted every `@fluentui/*` and `@griffel/*` lock entry, plus the dependencies only Fluent uses, and re-ran `yarn install`. Nothing else was re-resolved: React, OJS, prettier and `@types/node` keep their lock entries.

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `@fluentui/react-components` | 9.21.0 | 9.74.9 (`^9.74.9` in `apps/vscode-editor`, `packages/editor-ui`, `packages/ui-widgets`) |
| `@fluentui/react-icons` | 2.0.203 **and** 2.0.201 | 2.0.343, one copy (`^2.0.343` in `editor-ui` and `ui-widgets`) |
| `@fluentui/react-tree` | 9.0.0-beta.18 | 9.16.8 (stable) |
| `@griffel/react` / `@griffel/core` | 1.5.7 / 1.11.0 | 1.7.8 / 1.21.4, one copy each |
| `tabster` / `keyborg` | 4.4.3 / 2.0.0 | 8.8.1 / 2.14.1 + 3.498.0 (see below) |

- The three workspaces that import Fluent are the only ones that declare it, and they all use the same ranges. `packages/editor` and `apps/panmirror` don't import Fluent.
- React is still a single 18.3.1 copy, and `scheduler` is a single 0.23.2 copy. Every Fluent peer is satisfied: `react`, `react-dom` and `@types/react` (`>=16.14 <20`), and `scheduler` (`>=0.19`). There are no `resolutions`.
- **Two `keyborg` copies. Fluent causes this, not our lockfile.** `@fluentui/react-tabster` 9.26.18 (the latest) asks for `keyborg ^2.14.1` and `tabster ^8.8.0`, and `tabster` 8.8 depends on `keyborg ^3`. A fresh install of `@fluentui/react-components` gets the same two copies.
- Other shared dependencies that re-resolved: `tslib` collapsed to one 2.8.1 copy (there were three), and `csstype` to one 3.2.3 copy.

**Outline sidebar (`EditorOutlineTree.tsx`).** `Tree`, `TreeItem` and `TreeItemLayout` moved from `/unstable` to the stable `@fluentui/react-components` entry point.
- `onNavigation_unstable` is now `onNavigation`.
- The data type (`TreeNavigationDataParam`) is no longer generic. `data.value` is a `TreeItemValue` (`string | number`), so it goes through `String()` before `editor.navigate`.
- Opening and closing still use the uncontrolled `defaultOpenItems`, which works the same as in the beta.
- A click, including a click on the chevron, still toggles a branch and navigates the editor.
- **Small behavior changes from the stable Tree:**
  - Expanding and collapsing are now animated (Fluent's `Collapse` motion).
  - Pressing Enter on a branch also navigates the editor to it. Before, it only toggled the branch.

**Griffel `shorthands.*` → CSS shorthands.** Griffel deprecated the `shorthands.*` helpers now that it supports CSS shorthands natively. There were 4 uses: the toolbar border in `menu/styles.ts` and the citation preview padding in `insert-cite.tsx`. The styles they generate are equivalent.

**Held back:** `html-dialog.tsx` still imports `Alert` from `@fluentui/react-components/unstable`. 9.74.9 still exports it (`@fluentui/react-alert` 9.0.2-beta.1), it compiles, and it logs no runtime warning. Its JSDoc marks it `@deprecated` in favor of `MessageBar`/`Toast`. Moving the progress overlay to `MessageBar` would change how it looks, so I left that for a follow-up.

I found no other deprecated Fluent APIs, checked with TypeScript's deprecation diagnostics across `editor-ui`, `ui-widgets` and `vscode-editor`. The `fui-*` class names our CSS targets (`fui-DialogSurface__backdrop`, `fui-DialogContent`, `fui-Input`, `fui-Textarea`, `fui-Field`, `fui-Tab`) all still exist.

No CHANGELOG entry: the only user-visible differences are the outline animation and Fluent's own style refresh.

## Verification

On Node 24.21:
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks, including `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/vscode-editor` (the only type-check of `editor-ui` and `ui-widgets`).
- `yarn test-packages`: 13/13 tasks.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, and the same 17 warnings in `quarto` as on `main`.
- `yarn test-vscode`, headless (Xvfb in a linux-arm64 container, VS Code 1.139.1, Quarto 1.10.18, a clean extract of this branch): main 168 passing and 3 pending, r-project 3 passing. This includes the visual-editor roundtrip tests, which load the React webview.
- **Bundle:**

  | | `main` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `apps/vscode/assets/www/editor/index.js` | 10,350,698 B (3,232,988 B gzip) | 10,382,994 B (3,244,420 B gzip), +32 KB / +11 KB gzip |
  | `apps/vscode/assets/www/editor/style.css` | 35,283 B | 35,283 B |
  | `apps/panmirror/dist/panmirror.js` | 8,557,971 B | 8,557,971 B (identical; panmirror doesn't bundle Fluent) |

  There's only one `@griffel/*` and one `@fluentui/react-icons` in `node_modules`, so only one Griffel can end up in the bundle.
- **Outline tree, checked in headless Chromium.** A small Vite harness mounted the real `EditorOutlineTree` with a stub `EditorOperations`.
  - All items render open by default.

title: Fix first character of non-code lines highlighted as a comment
description:
Fixes #985.

Semantic tokens for code cells come from a virtual doc where every non-cell line is a `#` filler.
Language servers that emit comment tokens colored the first character of each paragraph, heading and YAML line as a comment.

Now only tokens on lines inside the language's code cells are kept.
This also drops tokens on the virtual doc's injected header lines (e.g. `# type: ignore`), which mapped to negative lines and made the provider throw, losing semantic highlighting for Python cells.

Adds a unit test for `unadjustedSemanticTokens`.

title: build: upgrade React to 18.3 with the new JSX transform, react-window 2, use-debounce 10
description:
React PR 1 of 3 in the dependency upgrade: React 18.3, the automatic JSX runtime, react-window 2 and use-debounce 10. Everything here still runs on React 18. Fluent UI (PR 2) and React 19 (PR 3) come later.

## Changes

**Packages.** I deleted the lock entries in scope and re-ran `yarn install`. Fluent UI (`@fluentui/react-components` 9.21, `@fluentui/react-icons`) keeps its lock entries.

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `react`, `react-dom` | 18.2.0 | 18.3.1 (`^18.3.1` in all four React workspaces) |
| `scheduler` | 0.23.0 | 0.23.2 |
| `@types/react` | 18.0.26 **and** 18.2.6 | 18.3.31, one copy |
| `@types/react-dom` | 18.0.10 **and** 18.2.4 | 18.3.7, one copy |
| `react-window` | 1.8.8 | 2.3.3 |
| `@types/react-window` | 1.8.5 | removed (v2 ships its own types) |
| `use-debounce` | 9.0.4 | 10.1.1 (`packages/editor-ui` only) |

- `@types/react`/`-dom` are now declared in `apps/vscode-editor` and `packages/ui-widgets` too. Both import React but were getting the types through hoisting. Every workspace that declares them uses the same range.
- `packages/editor` declared `use-debounce` but never imported it, so I removed it there.
- `react-textarea-autosize` (8.5.9) and `packages/editor-ui`'s `@types/react-transition-group` were already where the plan wanted them, so they didn't need changes.
- The lockfile has a single copy of `react`, `react-dom`, `scheduler`, `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom`. There are no `resolutions`. The only `@types/react@*` request came from `@types/react-window`, and it went away with that package.

**`@types/react` 18.3 type fixes:**
- `CitationSourcePanelProps` declared `ref` as an ordinary prop, and 18.3's `forwardRef` (`Omit<P, 'ref'>`) rejects that. I removed it from the props. `panel` is now typed as a `ForwardRefExoticComponent`, and the ref is passed at `createElement`.
- The callout dialog set `placeholder` on the Fluent `Field` (a `div`), where it had no effect. It's now on the caption `Textarea`, so "(Optional)" actually shows up there.

**Automatic JSX runtime:**
- `"jsx": "react-jsx"` in the five tsconfigs that set `jsx`: `apps/vscode-editor`, `apps/panmirror`, `packages/editor`, `packages/editor-ui` and `packages/ui-widgets`.
- Vite 8 transforms with Oxc, so the Vite configs of `apps/vscode-editor` and `apps/panmirror` set `oxc: { jsx: { runtime: 'automatic' } }` (the `esbuild` option is deprecated). Setting it explicitly means the runtime doesn't depend on which tsconfig Oxc picks up for files under `packages/*`.
- I removed six `React` imports that became unused (TS6133 under vscode-editor's `noUnusedLocals`).

**react-window 2 port:** the navigation tree, the cross-reference list, the citation list and its two row components, and the symbol/emoji grid.
- `FixedSizeList`/`FixedSizeGrid` → `List`/`Grid`, and `itemData` → `rowProps`/`cellProps`. Those props are spread onto the row's props, so rows read `props.x` instead of `props.data.x`.
- `children` → `rowComponent`/`cellComponent`, and `height`/`width` → `style`.
- Rows and cells spread v2's `ariaAttributes` (`role="listitem"`/`"gridcell"`).
- `scrollToItem` → `scrollToRow({ index, align: 'auto' })`. `'auto'` was v1's default, so keyboard navigation still scrolls just enough to bring the selection into view.
- v2 sets its imperative handle only after the parent's first effects have run. Where scrolling happens in an effect (tree, citation list, grid), I hold the handle with `useListCallbackRef`/`useGridCallbackRef`, so the effect runs again once the list has mounted.
- v2's `scrollToRow` throws a `RangeError` for an out-of-range index, where v1 clamped it. A stale `selectedIndex` after a new citation search would otherwise throw inside an effect and unmount the dialog. The citation list and symbol grid now check the bounds first. The cross-reference list's index was already clamped.
- v2 renders rows directly inside the scroll container (there's no inner wrapper div) and positions them with `transform`. None of the `.pm-*` CSS selectors depended on the wrapper.

## Verification

On Node 24.21:
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged. `@fluentui/*` entries are untouched.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks, including `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/vscode-editor` and `apps/panmirror`.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, and the same 17 warnings in `quarto` as on `main`. There are none in the React packages.
- `yarn test-packages`: 13/13 tasks.
- `yarn test-vscode`, headless (Xvfb in a linux-arm64 container, VS Code 1.139.1, Quarto 1.10.18, a clean extract of this branch): main 160 passing and 3 pending, r-project 3 passing. That's the same as `main`'s baseline, and it includes the visual-editor roundtrip tests, which load the React webview.
- **The JSX transform is in the bundle.** Counts are for the minified `apps/vscode/assets/www/editor/index.js`, excluding `document.createElement`:

  | | `main` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `createElement(` calls | 692 | 73 (explicit `React.createElement` calls and library code) |
  | `(0,x.jsx)(` / `(0,x.jsxs)(` calls | 0 / 0 | 498 / 122 |
  | size | 10,353,843 B (3,242,564 B gzip) | 10,350,711 B (3,243,618 B gzip) |

  `panmirror.js`: 281 → 17 `createElement` calls, 0 → 201/64 `jsx`/`jsxs` calls, and 8,561,296 → 8,557,984 B.
- **react-window port, checked in headless Chromium.** A small harness mounted the real `NavigationTree`, `CitationSourceList` and `SymbolCharacterGrid` and moved the selection. With `main`'s code and react-window 1.8.11, then with this branch, both gave identical `scrollTop` values:
  - on mount with the selection far down the list,
  - when the selection moves up,
  - when it moves to an item that's already visible (the position doesn't change),
  - at the end of the list.

  An out-of-range selection doesn't throw on either.

Manual smoke tests in the Extension Development Host (open a `.qmd`, switch to the visual editor, and keep the webview devtools console open to watch for React 18.3 deprecation warnings; there should be none):
1. **Insert → Cross Reference**: the arrow keys and PageUp/PageDown scroll the selection into view; clicking selects; double-clicking inserts; Cancel closes cleanly.
2. **Insert → Citation**: the source tree on the left (arrow keys scroll it), switching source panels, type-ahead search in the bibliography panel, and arrow keys through the results. Also the detailed list items in a latent search (Crossref/DOI), and running a second search after selecting an item far down the first result list.
3. **Insert → Special Characters / Emoji**: keyboard navigation across rows scrolls the grid, hover selects, click inserts, and Tab reaches the skin-tone panel. Check that the grid looks the same as before.
4. The completion popups for `@` and `:`.
5. **Find/replace**: the open and close animation, and the debounced search while typing (use-debounce 10).
6. **Insert → Callout**: the caption box now shows the "(Optional)" placeholder.
7. Toolbar, menus, the context menu, the outline, and the edit-attribute/image/link/table dialogs, as a general check of the React 18.3 + JSX-runtime switch.

title: refactor: chain resolveHeadingIds passes explicitly and add heading-id tests
description:
No behavior change.

#1168 added a comment in `resolveHeadingIds` (`packages/editor/src/pandoc/pandoc_to_prosemirror.ts`) saying that the first `mapTokens` pass's result is discarded, so its link rewrite has no effect. That comment is wrong. The rewrite does take effect, because `mapTokens` changes the tokens it's given in place (`mappedTok.c = mappedTok.c.map(mapValue)`). When the callback returns a block like `Para` unchanged, its children are replaced with the mapped ones, so a rewritten Link ends up in `ast.blocks` anyway. Links are always inline, so the rewrite is never lost.

That rewrite changes a shortcut heading link such as `[My Heading]` to href `'#'`. `linkHeadingsPostprocessor` then binds the link to the heading, so the link is written back as `[My Heading]` and follows heading renames.

## Changes

- `resolveHeadingIds`: the second pass (which strips heading ids that are neither explicit nor targeted by a link) now maps the first pass's result instead of `ast.blocks`. The code no longer depends on `mapTokens` changing its input. The ASTs it produces are identical.
- Replace the #1168 comment with one describing what the first pass does.
- Export `resolveHeadingIds` and add `packages/editor/test/heading-ids.test.ts` with 3 unit tests:
  - A shortcut heading link loses its target (href `'#'`).
  - A heading keeps its id only when the id is explicit or an explicit link targets it.
  - Nothing is rewritten when `shortcut_reference_links` is off.

## Verification

- With the second pass pointed back at `ast.blocks` (the upstream code), the new tests still pass. That confirms the refactor keeps the existing behavior.
- `yarn build` passes.
- `yarn test-packages` passes (18 editor tests, including the 3 new ones).
- `yarn lint --continue` gives 0 errors and the same 17 existing warnings, all in `quarto`.
- None of the visual-editor round-trip snapshots in `apps/vscode` contain heading links. Since the output is unchanged, I didn't run the VS Code tests locally; CI runs them.

title: fix: keep the images dir and extension for colliding image names, and fix Windows image path slashes
description:
When an image is pasted, dropped, or inserted from outside the document's directory, the extension picks a name in `images/` next to the document: `paste-1.png`, `paste-2.png`, ... (or `plot.png`, `plot-2.png`, ... for copied files). After 100 collisions it falls back to a random suffix. That fallback, present since the code was written in 2023, had two problems. It used `path.join(docDir, `${stem}-${id}`)`, so the file got no extension, and it went into the document directory instead of `images/`. The result was files like `paste-<uuid>` next to the `.qmd` that don't render.

Fixes #728

## Changes

- `apps/vscode/src/providers/editor/images.ts`: `uniqueImagePath` moves out of `documentImageResolver` and becomes an exported function. It takes the images directory as an argument, and file-existence checks and ID generation can be injected, so it can be tested without the VS Code host. The fallback now uses the same directory and extension as the numbered names (`images/paste-<uuid>.png`).
- Both callers (pasted base64 images and images copied in by drag/drop or the file picker) go through this function, so the one fix covers both. The file has no other fallback path.
- **Also fixes: Windows relative image paths with more than one separator.** `ensureForwardSlashes` used `/\\/` without the `g` flag, so only the first backslash was converted, and paths like `..\..\images\plot.png` came out as `../..\images\plot.png`. It's now a top-level exported function with a global replace. This is a separate commit.
- `apps/vscode/src/test/images.test.ts`: new unit tests for numbered names, stem preservation, the `.png` default, the post-100 fallback, and a path with several backslashes.
- `apps/vscode/CHANGELOG.md`: one entry for each fix.

## Verification

- `yarn build`: passes.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 0 errors, 17 warnings (unchanged from `main`).
- The new tests are part of the `main` label of `yarn test-vscode`. I didn't run that suite locally because it opens VS Code windows, so CI will run it. As a check, I compiled the tests (`yarn build-test`) and ran `test-out/images.test.js` under plain mocha with a stubbed `vscode` module. All 5 pass.

Not addressed here: #728 also mentions that pasting the same image again creates a new file each time instead of reusing the existing one. That's a separate enhancement.

title: fix: only strip #| cell options before execution for languages that use them
description:
Fixes #1182

## Changes

- `hasYamlHashOptions` now checks `includes(language)` against its list (python, r, julia, bash, sh, shell) instead of returning the list itself, which was always truthy. The list is the set of executable languages from when the bug was introduced in 2c85ea1e, and it is exactly the set of executable languages whose cell options are written as `#|`. The comment #1168 added about the bug is gone.
- The only executable languages whose behavior changes are **stata** and **csharp**. Leading `#|` lines in their cells are now sent to the kernel instead of being dropped. Quarto doesn't read those lines as options for these languages (stata uses `*|`, C# uses `//|`), and `quarto render` doesn't strip them either, so running a cell in the editor now matches render. Options written in the correct syntax for these languages were never stripped, and they still aren't. Both syntaxes are comments in their language, so this is harmless.
- A new `cellExecutors.test.ts` covers `codeWithoutOptionsFromBlock`: `#|` lines are stripped from python and bash cells and kept in a stata cell.
- CHANGELOG entry.

## Verification

- `yarn lint --continue`: 0 errors and 17 warnings, all in `quarto`. This is unchanged from `main`.

**Type fixes** for the new typings:
