title: build: minor/patch dependency batch (CodeMirror 6.43, lezer 1.2, drop stub types)
description:
Phase 1 of the dependency upgrade: the minor/patch batch. Most of these updates were already allowed by the declared ranges; the lockfile was just stale.

## Changes

**Re-resolved within existing ranges.** I pruned the lockfile entries for everything in scope and let `yarn install` re-resolve them. (Per-workspace `yarn upgrade` wrongly copies devDependencies into `dependencies`, and a root `yarn upgrade` only sees the root's dependencies.) These stay where they are, together with everything they depend on:
- The packages other steps own: `markdown-it` and its plugins/types, `linkify-it`; `vscode-languageclient`/`-server*`, `vscode-nls`, `vscode-uri`, `@types/vscode`; the `prosemirror-*` packages, `orderedmap` and their types; `react`, `react-dom`, `react-window` and their types; `@fluentui/react-components`; `prettier` and `eslint-config-prettier`.
- `@fluentui/react-icons`. 2.0.343 needs `@griffel/react ^1.6.1`, which would put a second Griffel runtime next to the one `react-components` 9.21 uses. This belongs with the Fluent UI PR.
- The `packages/ojs/*` subtrees (Phase 4).
- `cytoscape`, held at 3.23 (see below).

**Declared floors raised** to the resolved versions and unified across workspaces. Peer ranges (`eslint ^10.0.0` in the two ESLint configs) are left alone.

Notable version changes, by workspace:
- **`packages/editor-codemirror`:** the whole CodeMirror 6 set, for example `@codemirror/view` 6.7 → 6.43, `@codemirror/language` 6.4 → 6.12, `@codemirror/autocomplete` 6.4 → 6.20, `@codemirror/lang-sql` 6.3 → 6.10 and `@codemirror/lang-markdown` 6.0 → 6.5. Also `style-mod` 4.1 and `codemirror` 6.0.2. **`@lezer/highlight` 1.1.6 → 1.2.5**, with `@lezer/common` re-resolved from 1.0.2 to one 1.5.3 entry, so the parser and highlighter share one node-prop registry. The other `@lezer/*` parsers moved up with it.
- **`packages/editor`:** `react-textarea-autosize` 8.5, `transliteration` 2.6, `thenby` 1.4, `semver` 7.8, `use-debounce` 9.0.4, `clipboard` 2.0.11.
- **`packages/editor-ui`:** `@reduxjs/toolkit` 2.13, `typo-js` 1.3.2.
- **`apps/vscode`:** `axios` 1.20, `highlight.js` 11.12, `semver` 7.8.5, `@posit-dev/positron` 0.2.10, `which` 3.0.1, `mocha` 11.8.
- **`apps/lsp`:** `@vscode/l10n` 0.0.14 → 0.0.18. The caret range doesn't cover this bump, but only `l10n.t` is used.
- **root:** `turbo` 2.11.5.
- **Transitive:** `picomatch` 2.3.1/4.0.2 → 2.3.2/4.0.7, `js-yaml` 3.15.0/4.3.0 → 3.15.2/4.3.2, and `@babel/runtime` 7.20 → 7.29. Mermaid 9.4.3's dependency tree also moved up: `@braintree/sanitize-url` 6.0.4, `d3` 7.9, `khroma` 2.1, `lodash-es` 4.18.1 and `dayjs` 1.11.23. The mermaid version itself is unchanged. On the dev side, `cheerio` rc.12 → 1.2 (under vsce/ovsx).
- `@types/*` patch bumps: lodash.*, semver, tmp, wcwidth, zenscroll, diff-match-patch, typo-js, react-transition-group, vscode-webview, vscode-notebook-renderer, and node 22.20.4 (still on 22).

**Dropped:**
- `@types/axios` and `@types/highlight.js`. Both are deprecated stubs, and axios 1 and highlight.js 11 ship their own types.
- `@types/ace`. Nothing references it, and since TS 6 no longer loads `@types` packages automatically, it wasn't being loaded anyway.

**Fixes the upgrades needed:**
- `packages/editor-codemirror/src/behaviors/toolbar.ts`: the code-view toolbar widget was a plain object literal. `@codemirror/view` 6.43 adds `lineBreaks` and `coordsAt` to `WidgetType`, so the literal no longer type-checks. It now subclasses `WidgetType`, whose defaults (`eq`/`updateDOM` false, `estimatedHeight` -1, `ignoreEvent` true) match what the literal spelled out.
- `cytoscape` is held at 3.23.0. 3.34 adds an `exports` map that blocks mermaid 9's deep import of `cytoscape/dist/cytoscape.umd.js`, and that breaks the `vscode-markdownit` build. This goes away with the Mermaid step.

## Verification

On Node 24.21:
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks.
- `yarn test-packages`: 10/10 tasks.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, and the same 17 warnings in `quarto` as on `main`.
- `yarn test-vscode` (VS Code 1.139.1, Quarto CLI on PATH): main 150 passing (3 pending), r-project 3 passing.
- Bundle sizes compared with `main`: `out/main.js` +62 KB (4.19 → 4.25 MB, probably highlight.js 11.12's extra languages and axios 1.20), `out/lsp/lsp.js` −24 KB, `assets/www/editor/index.js` +16 KB (CodeMirror), `panmirror.js` −80 KB. The Mermaid chunks and `markdownit/index.js` are byte-identical in size.
- Still to do: a manual smoke test of the visual editor in the Extension Development Host, especially code cells (CodeMirror 6.43 and the toolbar widget), syntax highlighting, autocomplete, search and spelling (typo-js 1.3).

title: build: upgrade markdown-it to 15 and its plugins, drop the linkify-it resolution
description:
The markdown-it step of the dependency upgrade: markdown-it 13 → 15 and its plugins, and the root `linkify-it` resolution is no longer needed. ## Changes **Versions**, unified across every workspace that declares them: - `markdown-it` `^15.0.2` in all five workspaces: `apps/vscode`, `apps/vscode-markdownit`, `packages/core`, `packages/quarto-core` and `packages/editor-codemirror`. - Renderer plugins: `markdown-it-deflist` `^4.0.0`, `markdown-it-footnote` `^4.0.0`, `markdown-it-sub` `^2.0.0`, `markdown-it-sup` `^2.0.0`, `markdown-it-task-lists` `^2.1.1`. - `markdown-it-highlightjs` `^4.3.0`, with `highlight.js` `^11.12.0`. The highlight.js bump is required: the plugin now wants `^11.9`, and without it we'd ship a second copy. - **`markdown-it-attrs` `^4.5.0`, not 5.0.1.** 5.x calls `require('markdown-it')`, so esbuild bundles markdown-it's CommonJS build next to the ESM build our own imports use. That means two copies of markdown-it: +118 KB in `lsp.js`, +170 KB in `main.js` and +51 KB in the notebook renderer. 4.5.0 bundles the same types without the `require`. 5.x's one addition, `fenceAttrsOnPre`, can't take effect for us: the LSP only parses, and the renderer runs on the host's markdown-it. - **Removed:** - the root `resolutions: { linkify-it }` - `@types/markdown-it` (in 3 workspaces) and `@types/markdown-it-attrs`, because markdown-it 15 and markdown-it-attrs 4.5 ship their own types - `@types/markdown-it-highlightjs`, a deprecated stub that pulled in highlight.js 10 - the unused `markdown-it-implicit-figures` Resulting lockfile: - The only markdown-it that ships is 15.0.2, hoisted. The nested 12.3.2 copies are gone. The only other copy is a dev-only 14.3.2 from ovsx. - `linkify-it` 6.1.0, plus 5.0.2 for ovsx. Both are outside the advisory's affected range (<5.0.1), so the resolution isn't needed. - `mdurl` 2.1 and `uc.micro` 2.1/3.0. No `@types/markdown-it*` or highlight.js 10 is left. **Code changes:** - Every `markdown-it/lib/*` deep import is replaced with public type imports (`import type { MarkdownIt, Token, StateBlock, ... } from "markdown-it"`). That covers 12 files in `packages/core/src/markdownit`, including gridtables, and quarto-core's `markdownit.ts`. - The core plugins no longer use runtime code from our own copy of markdown-it. `callouts.ts` and `decorator.ts` create tokens with `state.Token`, and `shortcodes.ts` uses `md.utils.escapeHtml`. In the notebook renderer these plugins run on the host's markdown-it, so before this they were mixing our bundled `Token` class with the host's tokens. - Type fixes for markdown-it 15's stricter types: - The attribute helpers take `Token["attrs"]` and convert values with `String()`. - `divs.ts` reads `state.env` through a small `DivEnv` interface. - `Callout` is now a `type` alias. - quarto-core uses `meta?.`. - `yaml.ts` now stores the raw front matter in `token.content` instead of `token.meta`. The only reader is the optional callback, and nothing passes one. - `new MarkdownIt(...)` everywhere (calling it without `new` is deprecated in 15), and `validateLink.bind(md)` in `render-assist.ts`. - Renderer (`apps/vscode-markdownit`): `md.use()` no longer passes `{}` to plugins that take no options, the `src/@types` stubs are rewritten for markdown-it 15, and the implicit-figures and gridtables stubs are deleted. In `mermaid.ts`, only a type import changed. - New test: `packages/core/test/markdownit-plugins.test.ts` covers callouts, the code-block decorator, shortcode escaping and the YAML callback. It passes on both `main` and this branch. **Snapshot tests** for every markdown-it path. Each area has a focused fixture, plus a few `apps/vscode/src/test/examples` files that exercise distinct syntax. The snapshots are committed as readable `.html`/`.json` files next to the tests; `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` rewrites them. - **Notebook renderer** (`apps/vscode-markdownit/test/renderer.test.ts`, 5 inputs): - The plugin setup moved out of `activate()` into an exported `extendMarkdownIt(md, mermaidPlugin)` in `src/extend.ts`, so the test runs the real setup on a markdown-it instance configured like VS Code's (`html`, `linkify`). - Mermaid is stubbed at the module and DOM level, so the snapshots pin which fences become diagrams and the `` the plugin emits, but not Mermaid's own SVG. - The package is no longer `"type": "module"`: with it, Node can't load `core`'s TypeScript source from an ES module. `chunkFileNames` keeps Vite's chunks named `.js`, and the bundle is otherwise unchanged. - **Help panel** (`apps/vscode/src/test/helpPanelMarkdown.test.ts`, in the VS Code suite): the markdown-it setup moved to `providers/assist/markdown.ts` (`renderAssistMarkdown`). The fixture covers bare URLs, `www.x.org`, `README.md`, Unicode punctuation, e-mail addresses, highlight.js, the `vscode-resource:`/`file:`/`data:` link overrides, raw HTML and ``. - **Visual editor completion docs** (`packages/editor-codemirror/test/completion-markdown.test.ts`): the commonmark rendering moved into `renderCompletionMarkdown()` in `behaviors/completion-markdown.ts`. The single instance is now created once, not on every completion. - **quarto-core parser** (`packages/quarto-core/test/parser.test.ts`, 6 inputs): `markdownitBlockParser()` is exported. Each snapshot has a compact projection of its token stream (nesting, type, tag, map, attrs, info, meta), plus the Quarto tokens `markdownitParser()` derives from it. The inputs include the `::: {#fig-a}` + `{width=50%}` case. - New `test` scripts in `quarto-core`, `editor-codemirror` and `quarto-vscode-markdownit`, with `tsx` declared in each. `yarn test-packages` now also filters in `quarto-vscode-markdownit`; CI's "Test packages" job runs that script. - The snapshots also pin two existing quirks that this PR doesn't change: - The front-matter token's `map` ends at a character offset rather than a line. - In the renderer, markdown-it-attrs turns a `{python}` fence into ``. **The DEP0040 punycode warning:** on `main`, `lsp.js` and `main.js` each have exactly one `require("punycode")`, inside markdown-it 13. markdown-it 15 bundles the userland `punycode.js`, and "punycode" no longer appears anywhere in `apps/vscode/out`. This should remove the warning. That's shown from the bundles, not from a live run. **Rendering changes.** I compared output before and after on a synthetic `.qmd` and all 51 files in `apps/vscode/src/test/examples`. Each file went through the quarto-core parser, the renderer plugins running on a host markdown-it 14.3.2, the help-panel renderer, and the commonmark renderer. - **LSP parser:** no differences across the test examples. On the synthetic file, one bug is fixed: inside `::: {#fig-a}`, an image's `{width=50%}` no longer leaks onto the div's attributes. - **Help panel (linkify-it 6):** bare `www.x.org` and `x.com` are no longer auto-linked, and Unicode punctuation now ends a link. I kept the new default, because fuzzy linking also turns things like `README.md` into links. - **Help panel and commonmark:** lowercase `` is now treated as an HTML block instead of escaped text. - **Notebook renderer:** - Loose definition lists now get `

` inside `

`, as Pandoc does. - The task-list class changed from `task-list` to `contains-task-list`. No CSS targets either class. **CHANGELOG:** one line, covering the help-panel links and the definition lists. **Bundle sizes** (bytes, before → after): - `lsp.js`: 2,880,036 → 2,875,676 - `main.js`: 4,192,731 → 4,239,683, probably highlight.js 11.12's larger grammars - `markdownit/index.js`: 213,118 → 117,187, because the markdown-it 12 pieces are gone ## Verification On Node 24.21: - `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged. - `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks. - `yarn test-packages`: 13/13 tasks. core goes from 21 to 26 tests, and there are new ones in quarto-core (6), quarto-vscode-markdownit (5) and editor-codemirror (1). - Sanity check: each of these breaks at least one snapshot test, and restoring it makes the tests pass again. - Dropping `deflistPlugin` from `extendMarkdownIt` (2 renderer snapshots fail). - Removing `attrPlugin` from the quarto-core block parser (all 6 fail). - Setting `linkify: false` in the help panel (its test fails). - `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, and the same 17 warnings as on `main`. - `tsc --noEmit` is clean for core, quarto-core, `apps/vscode`, `apps/lsp` and `apps/vscode-markdownit`. - `yarn test-vscode` (VS Code 1.139.1, Quarto CLI on PATH): main 151 passing (including the new help-panel test) and 3 pending; r-project 3 passing. - **Still not covered by tests:** LSP folding and document links, which are computed from the parser tokens but not tested themselves. - **Still to do by hand**, in the Extension Development Host and Positron: - A notebook with markdown cells: the renderer loads on the real host markdown-it (no "Error extending markdown-it" in the webview console); Mermaid actually renders; and callouts and definition lists look right with the stylesheet. - The help panel and the visual editor's completion popup in their webviews: image paths rewritten to webview URIs, and MDN-only link paragraphs removed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: build: upgrade vscode-languageclient/-server to 10.1 and -types to 3.18, drop vscode-nls
description:
The VS Code platform / LSP step of the dependency upgrade: `vscode-languageclient` and `vscode-languageserver` 8.1 → 10.1, and the protocol types to 3.18.

## Changes

**Versions**, unified across every workspace that declares them:
- `vscode-languageclient` `^8.1.0` → `^10.1.2` (`apps/vscode`, `packages/core-node`).
- `vscode-languageserver` `^8.1.0` → `^10.1.2` (`apps/lsp`; dev in `apps/vscode` and `packages/editor-server`).
- `vscode-languageserver-types` `^3.17.3` → `^3.18.4` (`apps/{vscode,lsp}`, `packages/{editor,editor-codemirror,editor-server,editor-types,quarto-core}`).
- `vscode-languageserver-textdocument` `^1.0.4` → `^1.0.15` (`apps/lsp`; dev in `apps/vscode`).
- These bring `vscode-languageserver-protocol` 3.18.4 and `vscode-jsonrpc` 9.0.3. The lockfile has one entry for each of the six packages.
- Removed `vscode-nls` from `apps/vscode`. Nothing imports it.
- Removed `vscode-languageserver` from `packages/core-node`. It was declared there but never used.

v10 needs VS Code ≥1.91, which `engines.vscode` `^1.101.0` (#1157) already covers. Resolving its `exports`-only entry points needs `moduleResolution: bundler`, which is already in place (#1165). `@types/vscode`, `engines`, and `@vscode/l10n` are unchanged.

**API breaks:**
- **`documentLink/resolve` must return a link.** v10 types the handler as `DocumentLink`, not `DocumentLink | undefined`. `apps/lsp/src/index.ts` now returns the unresolved link when there's nothing to resolve. This also fixes a latent bug: the client passes a resolve result straight to `asDocumentLink()`, which throws on `null`.
- Nothing else needed changing. v10's other breaking changes don't apply here:
  - Our middleware signatures are unchanged.
  - We already pass a `LogOutputChannel`.
  - We don't use the `showDocument` middleware, color requests, the browser client, or `getFeature`.
  - Dispatch stays unbounded by default (`maxParallelism: -1`), so ordering is as before.
  - `ProposedFeatures.all` is now empty, but `createConnection(ProposedFeatures.all)` still type-checks.

**Import tidying:**
- `packages/core-node/src/jsonrpc-lsp.ts` imports `LanguageClient` as a type. `core-node` is also bundled into the server, so a value import could pull the client, and its `require("vscode")`, into `lsp.js`.
- The client imports in `apps/vscode` now all come from `vscode-languageclient/node`. v10's root entry is `lib/common/api`, not `lib/node/main`.
- `MarkupContent` in `render-assist.ts` now comes from `vscode-languageserver-types`.

**New test** (`apps/vscode/src/test/lsp-features.test.ts`): before this PR, the tests reached the Quarto language server only through symbols and formatting. The diagnostics tests use a fixture server, and `yamlProviders.test.ts` covers the extension's own YAML providers. The new suite adds end-to-end checks for:
- crossref and YAML completions
- YAML and math hovers
- YAML diagnostics
- document links, including resolve
- folding and selection ranges
- references

Definitions aren't covered, because the server's definition handler is a stub that returns null (#1139). That's unchanged here.

## Verification

On Node 24.21:
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks, including `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/lsp` and `apps/vscode`.
- Bundles, checked with an esbuild metafile: `out/main.js` and `out/lsp/lsp.js` each contain one copy of `vscode-languageserver-types` (its ESM build) and of the protocol and jsonrpc packages. `vscode-languageserver` isn't in `out/main.js`.
- `yarn test-packages`: 10/10 tasks.
- `yarn lint --continue`: 17/17 tasks, 0 errors, and the same 17 warnings in `quarto` as on `main`.
- `yarn test-vscode` (VS Code 1.139.1, Quarto CLI on PATH):
  - Before the new test: main 150 passing and 3 pending, the same as `main`.
  - With it: main 159 passing and 3 pending; r-project 3 passing. The new suite passed on 5 of 5 runs.
- The same suite on the engine floor (`version: '1.101.0'` set temporarily in `.vscode-test.mjs`): main 159 passing and 3 pending; r-project 3 passing.
- `yarn test-positron`: 4 passing. These tests don't exercise the LSP or its middleware.

title: build: upgrade VS Code test and packaging tooling, publish with the repo's vsce
description:
Phase 2 of the dependency upgrade: the VS Code test and packaging tooling, plus a new publish workflow.

## Changes

**Dev dependencies in `apps/vscode`** (latest releases as of today):
- `@vscode/test-electron` `^2.5.2` → `^3.1.0`. It resolves the macOS executable from `CFBundleExecutable`, so `yarn test-vscode` works again on VS Code ≥1.110 on macOS (it had looked for `Contents/MacOS/Electron`, which 1.110 renamed).
- `@vscode/test-cli` `^0.0.11` → `^0.0.15`. I removed the root `package.json`'s copy of it: nothing at the root uses it, and test-cli resolves everything from `apps/vscode/.vscode-test.mjs`.
- `@vscode/vsce` `^2.15.0` → `^4.0.0`.
- `mocha` `^9.2.1` → `^11.7.6`, and `@types/mocha` `^9.1.0` → `^10.0.10`. That matches the mocha 11 that test-cli 0.0.15 uses to run `yarn test-vscode`, so the CLI suite, the Positron suite and the debug launch config all run on the same major. Mocha 12 waits for a test-cli release that uses it. The OJS subtrees' mocha 9/10 are untouched.
- Removed the deprecated `vsce` package. Nothing imports it, and it competed with `@vscode/vsce` for the `vsce` bin: on `main`, `node_modules/.bin/vsce` is vsce **2.15.0**, so `yarn install-vscode` wasn't even using `@vscode/vsce`.
- Added `ovsx` `^1.2.0` for publishing to Open VSX.
- Nothing here ships: the VSIX contains only bundles.

**Packaging:**
- `"vsce": {"dependencies": false}` in `apps/vscode/package.json`. vsce no longer runs `yarn list`/`npm list` over the hoisted workspace (the result was thrown away anyway, because `.vscodeignore` excludes `node_modules/**`). Local `yarn install-vscode` and CI both pick this up.
- `.vscodeignore` now excludes `test-out/**` (so a VSIX built after running the tests no longer ships the test bundle) and `.positron-test/**`. `yarn test-positron` downloads Positron there, and with vsce 4 a later `vsce package` tried to include its ~32,000 files, then failed in the secret scan (`EISDIR` on a symlinked directory in the app bundle).

**Publishing** now follows [posit-dev/publisher](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yaml) and drops `HaaLeo/publish-vscode-extension`, which bundles its own vsce 3.2.2 (so vsce's secret scan had never run on this extension in CI):
- **`build.yaml`** is also a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`). It runs `yarn vsce package --out quarto-<version>.vsix` in `apps/vscode` with the repo's pinned vsce, uploads it as the `quarto-vscode-<sha>` artifact (as before), and outputs the artifact name, VSIX name and version. Its push and PR triggers are unchanged, except that they now also fire when `build.yaml` itself changes.
- **`publish.yaml`** keeps its trigger (`workflow_dispatch` with the `ready_to_go` checkbox) and its secrets (`VS_MARKETPLACE_TOKEN`, `OPEN_VSX_TOKEN`). It calls `build.yaml` once. Then two parallel jobs download that one VSIX and run `yarn vsce publish --packagePath <vsix> --skip-duplicate` and `yarn ovsx publish <vsix> --skip-duplicate`, with the tokens passed as `VSCE_PAT`/`OVSX_PAT` env vars. The GitHub release job runs after both publish jobs succeed, and attaches the same VSIX. The version comes from the package job, so `euberdeveloper/ga-project-version` is gone too. The workflows default to `contents: read`; only the release job gets `contents: write`.
- **Behavior differences:**
  - Open VSX no longer waits for the Marketplace publish.
  - Because of `--skip-duplicate`, "Re-run failed jobs" is safe after a partial failure.
  - The PR/push build artifact is no longer marked pre-release. The old dry run passed `preRelease: true`, which would have been wrong for the VSIX that's now published.
- `apps/vscode/CONTRIBUTING.md` describes the new workflow and the re-run.

## Verification

On Node 24, with Quarto from Positron's bundle on `PATH`:
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged. `yarn why`: `@vscode/test-electron` 3.1.0 for `apps/vscode`, with 2.5.2 nested under `@posit-dev/positron-test-electron`. `apps/vscode` and test-cli both get mocha 11.8.0. `node_modules/.bin/vsce` → `@vscode/vsce` 4.0.0.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks. `yarn test-packages`: 9/9. `yarn lint --continue`: 5/5, 0 errors, 17 warnings (unchanged).
- `yarn test-vscode` on macOS, **without the local 1.109 pin**: it downloaded VS Code 1.139.1 and passed (main 150 passing, 3 pending; r-project 3 passing). `--label r-project` alone: 3 passing. `--label main --grep Symbols`: 9 passing, so `--grep` still reaches mocha.
- `yarn test-positron` (stable): 4 passing.
- **VSIX contents:** I packaged `main` from a clean checkout (vsce 2.15.0) and this branch from a clean `out/` (vsce 4.0.0), and compared `unzip -Z1` listings. Both have 86 files, and the lists are identical except that vsce 4 stores `README.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` as `readme.md`/`changelog.md`. The manifest gains the `ExecutesCode` and `EnabledApiProposals` properties, and the space is stripped from the `Graphviz (DOT)` tag. Then I ran the whole test suite plus `test-positron`, which left `test-out/`, `.vscode-test/` and `.positron-test/` behind, and repackaged with the CI command (`yarn --silent vsce package --out quarto-1.139.0.vsix`). I got the same 86 files, and the secret scan passed.
- **Bundle sizes shrank slightly** (`out/main.js` 4.58 → 4.45 MB, `lsp.js` 3.32 → 3.28 MB, the editor's `index.js` 10.93 → 10.86 MB). This isn't a version change. Removing vsce 2 freed the root `node_modules` slots it held for `markdown-it` 12 and `tmp` 0.2.1. So `markdown-it` 13.0.1 (plus `entities` 3.0.1), `tmp` 0.2.7 and `debug` are now hoisted once, instead of being nested and bundled separately for each of `apps/vscode`, `packages/core` and `packages/quarto-core`. I confirmed this for `main.js` by comparing esbuild metafiles on both lockfiles: every bundled package has the same version, and there are just fewer duplicate copies. I didn't check `lsp.js` or the editor bundle, but they depend on the same packages.
- **Workflows:** `actionlint` 1.7.12 reports nothing for all four workflows (shellcheck wasn't installed, so the `run:` scripts weren't checked). This PR's `build.yaml` run exercises the new packaging job end to end. **Not tested:** `publish.yaml` itself (the reusable call, artifact download, `vsce publish`, `ovsx publish`, and the release). Nothing can exercise those without a real release. I did check locally that `yarn --silent vsce publish --help` and `yarn --silent ovsx --version` resolve the pinned 4.0.0 and 1.2.0 from `apps/vscode`, and that both CLIs read `VSCE_PAT`/`OVSX_PAT` and support `--skip-duplicate`.
- Not done: a manual smoke test of the installed VSIX (activation, preview, LSP, visual editor).

title: build: lint every workspace (incl. .tsx and apps/vscode recommended rules) and run lint in CI
description:
Phase 0.5b of the dependency upgrade: lint every non-OJS workspace, and run lint in CI. This closes the lint half of #1143.

## Changes

**Lint scripts everywhere.** The 12 `packages/*` workspaces that have an `eslint.config.mjs` (build, core, core-browser, core-node, editor, editor-codemirror, editor-core, editor-server, editor-types, editor-ui, quarto-core, ui-widgets) now have a `lint` script: `eslint src`, plus `test` in `core` and `editor`, which have test directories. `yarn lint` goes from 5 to 17 tasks.

**`.tsx` is linted.** The app scripts change from `eslint "src/**/*.ts"` to `eslint src`. Under flat config, that lints every file the config's `files` pattern (`**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}`) matches, so `apps/vscode-editor` and the React code in `packages/editor`, `editor-ui` and `ui-widgets` are now linted. I dropped `TIMING=1` from the scripts, since it only adds a timing table to the output. `apps/lsp` keeps its `tsc --noEmit &&` prefix.

**`apps/vscode` adopts the shared recommended config.** It extends `eslint-config-custom-server` (ESLint recommended, typescript-eslint recommended, eslint-config-prettier, Node globals), and keeps its existing ignores and `warn` rules (`naming-convention`, `@stylistic/semi`, `curly`, `eqeqeq`, `no-throw-literal`). That turned up about 125 errors across 57 files, nearly all mechanical. It now declares `eslint-config-custom-server`, and drops its direct `typescript-eslint` devDependency because the config no longer imports it. The lockfile is unchanged.

**One rule relaxed, in the shared config:** `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` now ignores bindings that start with `_` (`args`, `vars`, `caughtErrors`, `destructuredArrayIgnorePattern`). The code already uses `_` to mean "intentionally unused" (for example `catch (_)`, `const [_first, _second, third] = …`, and `_state` parameters in base-class stubs), and `apps/lsp` already had the `args` half of this as a local override. That override moves into the shared config, so `apps/lsp/eslint.config.mjs` is now a one-line re-export. No other rules were turned off. Where a rule was right in general but not at one site, I added an inline disable with a reason:
- the `node-sqlite3-wasm` triple-slash reference: an ambient `declare module` file can't be imported
- the ANSI-escape regex in `convert.ts` (`no-control-regex`)
- `any` for arbitrary YAML front matter in `reveal.ts`
- `any` in 5 test stubs of overloaded `vscode.window` APIs

**Real bugs the lint found, and fixed:**
- `packages/editor` `insert_citation-source-panel-list.tsx`: the `switch` had two `case CitationSourceListStatus.default:` labels with identical bodies (`no-duplicate-case`). I kept one, with the `default:` fallthrough.
- `packages/editor` `cite-completion_doi.tsx`: in `` `${author} ${date}` || '' `` the fallback could never apply, because the template literal is always truthy (`no-constant-binary-expression`). It now trims the result instead.
- `packages/editor` `attr_edit-command.ts`: `tr.setNodeMarkup(...), dispatch(tr)` used the comma operator; it's now two statements.
- `packages/editor` `user_comment/ui/plugin.tsx`: removed a stray empty template literal (` `` `) after `root.render(...)`.
- `apps/vscode` `render.ts`: `resolveFormat` used an `async` Promise executor (`no-async-promise-executor`), so if `quartoProjectConfig` rejected, the error was swallowed and the promise never settled. It now awaits the config first and only wraps the quick pick in a `Promise`.
- `apps/vscode` `core/doc.ts`: `findQuartoEditor`'s `includeVisible` parameter has been ignored since #1007, and no caller passes it. I removed it.
- `apps/vscode` `lsp/client.ts`: removed a `symbol.children = symbol.children` self-assignment.
- `apps/vscode` `yaml-links.ts`: removed `IGNORE_PATTERNS`, which was never used.

**Found but deliberately not changed.** These would change behavior, so each one has a comment now and is left for a follow-up:
- `packages/editor` `pandoc_to_prosemirror.ts` `resolveHeadingIds`: the first `mapTokens` pass rewrites shortcut heading links, but its result has always been thrown away, because the second pass maps the original `ast.blocks` (`no-useless-assignment`). So the first pass only collects heading ids. Using its result would change round-trip output. I kept the current behavior and made the discard explicit.
- `apps/vscode` `cell/executors.ts`: `hasYamlHashOptions(language)` returns a (truthy) array instead of checking whether it includes `language`. As a result, `#|` lines are stripped before execution for every language, not just python/r/julia/bash/sh/shell. "Fixing" it would start sending `#|` lines to kernels for other languages.

**Everything else is mechanical:**
- removed unused `eslint-disable` directives (21) and unused imports
- `catch (e) {` → `catch {` where the error is never read
- prefixed unused parameters with `_`
- `let` → `const`
- removed dead initializers and assignments
- removed unnecessary regex escapes
- replaced `any` with real types where the API is known (`HTMLDivElement`, `Extension<unknown>`, `SemanticTokensLegend`, `unknown`, `object`, `Record<string, unknown>` instead of `{}`), and used the typed `activeNotebookEditor`, `onDidSaveNotebookDocument` and `registerDocumentDropEditProvider`, which the 1.101 engine floor guarantees

**CI:** a new `Lint` job in `test.yaml` runs `yarn install --frozen-lockfile && yarn lint`. It fails on errors; warnings don't fail it.

**Not changed:** OJS (its subtrees keep their own ESLint 8 configs), Prettier (Phase 4.5), `turbo.json`, and dependency versions.

## Verification

All on Node 24.
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`: lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn lint --continue`:
  - `main`: 5/5 tasks.
  - This branch: **17/17 tasks, 0 errors.** There are 17 warnings, all in `quarto` (`apps/vscode`), and they're the same 17 as on `main`. No other workspace has warnings.
- Before the fixes, `eslint src` (plus `test` where it exists) reported these errors:

  | Workspace | Errors |
  | --- | --- |
  | `editor` | 22 in `src`, 8 in `test` |
  | `quarto-core` | 6 |
  | `editor-codemirror` | 6 |
  | `core` | 2 |
  | `editor-server` | 2 |
  | `editor-ui` | 1 |
  | `apps/vscode`, with the shared config | 126 |

  Widening to `.tsx` added no new errors in `apps/vscode-editor` (just 1 unused directive); the `.tsx` errors in `packages/editor` are included in its count above.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks. This includes the `tsc --noEmit` runs in `apps/vscode`, `apps/vscode-editor`, `apps/panmirror` and `apps/lsp`, which type-check the packages they pull in.
- `yarn test-packages`: 9/9 tasks.
- `yarn test-vscode` (VS Code 1.109, Quarto CLI on PATH): main label 150 passing and 3 pending; r-project 3 passing.

title: build: upgrade small Node utilities (drop uuid/nanoid, p-queue 9, picomatch 4, node-html-parser 9, regexpp fork, plist 5)
description:
Phase 2 of the dependency upgrade: the small Node utilities.

## Changes

**`uuid` and `nanoid` → `crypto.randomUUID()`.** Every call site used only `uuid.v4()` or `nanoid()` with no arguments, so the built-in does the same job. With `engines.vscode` at `^1.101.0` (Node 22), `crypto` is always available.
- **Node side** (extension host, LSP, editor server) imports `randomUUID` from `node:crypto`: `preview.ts` (render token), `vdoc-tempfile.ts` (temp file name), `images.ts` (fallback image file name), editor-server `pandoc.ts` (bibliography etag) and `dictionary.ts` (ignored-words file name), quarto-core `storage.ts` (scratch dir name), and core-node `shortUuid()`.
- **Webview side** (`apps/vscode-editor`, `packages/editor-ui`) calls the global `crypto.randomUUID()`. It needs a secure context, which VS Code webviews are. `editor-ui` is only bundled into the VS Code webview. Panmirror (which RStudio loads) only uses `packages/editor`, which has its own hand-rolled `uuidv4()`, and this PR doesn't change that.
- **ID formats:** every replaced value is either opaque (a token, etag, React key, or map key) or goes into a file name. The UUID values are the same format as before. The fallback image name used to be `<stem>-<21-char nanoid>` and is now `<stem>-<36-char UUID>`. It's still filename-safe, and it's only used after 100 name collisions.
- This removes the undeclared `uuid` imports in `core-node`, `editor-ui` and `quarto-core`. It also removes `uuid` from `apps/lsp` (where it was never imported), `apps/vscode`, `apps/vscode-editor` and `packages/editor-server`, and removes `nanoid` and `@types/uuid` from `apps/vscode`. Other packages still pull in `uuid` transitively: jayson (8.x), mermaid (9.x) and OJS's exceljs.

**`p-queue` `^8.0.1` → `^9.3.3`.** No code change: `ExecuteQueue` doesn't use the removed `throwOnTimeout` option.

**`picomatch` `^2.3.1` → `^4.0.7` and `@types/picomatch` `^2.3.0` → `^4.0.3`** in `apps/lsp` and `apps/vscode`. picomatch 4 still ships no types, so `@types/picomatch` stays. 4.0.7 includes the fixes for CVE-2026-33671 and CVE-2026-33672. Every call site is `isMatch` on forward-slash URI paths or hrefs, so 3.0's change to Windows separator handling doesn't affect them. Transitive copies of picomatch 2.3.1 (readdirp, anymatch, micromatch, `@rollup/pluginutils`) and 4.0.2 (`@rollup/plugin-node-resolve`) are still in the lockfile. Phase 1's lockfile refresh is what picks those up.

**`node-html-parser` `^6.1.5` → `^9.0.4`** in `apps/lsp`. No code change: `document-links.ts` uses `parse`, `HTMLElement`, `tagName`, `attributes`, `outerHTML`, `range` and `childNodes`, and these are unchanged. `outerHTML` is still serialized from the raw attribute text, which the link offsets depend on.

**`regexpp` → `@eslint-community/regexpp` `^4.12.2`**, in both `packages/json-validator` and `packages/_json-validator`, to keep the two copies in sync. `regexpp` is deprecated, and this is its maintained fork. Only the import specifier changes. `prefixes()` gives identical output under both libraries on a handful of sample patterns. Publishing a new `@quarto/json-validator` is a separate step.

**`@types/which` `^2.0.2` → `^3.0.4`**, to match the installed `which` 3. `which` itself stays on 3, because `which@7` needs Node ≥22.22, which only VS Code ≥1.125 provides.

**`plist` `^3.0.6` → `^5.0.0`.** plist 5 is ESM-only, and its `exports` has no `require` condition. So `syntaxes/build-lang.js` is now `build-lang.mjs`:
- it uses `import` for js-yaml, plist and `comment-chars.ts` (it still runs under tsx, which resolves the `.ts` import)
- `__dirname` is replaced by `import.meta.dirname`

The `build-lang` script and two comments now point at the new file name. The generated `syntaxes/quarto.tmLanguage` is byte-identical. I kept the XML plist grammar rather than switching to JSON, in case anything outside the extension reads it as XML.

No CHANGELOG entry: nothing here changes user-visible behavior.

## Verification

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks. `randomUUID` appears in `out/main.js`, `out/lsp/lsp.js`, and the editor webview bundle.
- `yarn build-lang`: `git status` is clean under `syntaxes/`, and regenerating after corrupting `quarto.tmLanguage` restores it exactly.

title: build: upgrade MathJax to 4 (@mathjax/src, with the TeX font)
description:
Phase 2 of the dependency upgrade: MathJax 3 → 4, for LSP math hovers and visual editor equation previews.

**Stacked on #1170.** Only the last commits are new here: "replace mathjax-full 3 with @mathjax/src 4" and the CHANGELOG line. This PR reuses the `editor-server` test script that #1170 adds. Once #1170 merges, I'll rebase this onto `main`.

## Changes

**`mathjax-full` `^3.2.2` → `@mathjax/src` `^4.1.3`.** `mathjax-full` is deprecated in favor of the scoped package. `@mathjax/mathjax-tex-font` and `@mathjax/mathjax-mhchem-font-extension` (both `^4.1.3`) are added too.
- **Font:** we use the static MathJax TeX font, MathJax 3's font ported to v4, through `fontData: MathJaxTexFont`. v4's default font (newcm) loads glyph ranges on demand. That breaks our synchronous `html.convert()` with retry errors, and it can't find its files from inside the bundle. The TeX font also keeps output visually the same as v3.
- **mhchem:** v4 moved mhchem's arrow glyphs (`-mhchem` variant, U+E4xx) into a font extension. Without `MathJaxTexFont.addExtension(MathJaxMhchemFontExtension)`, `\ce{A -> B}` renders the arrow as a missing-glyph `<text>`.
- **Imports:** `AllPackages` is gone, so `mathjax.ts` imports each of the 28 TeX packages we use (`baseExtensions` + `supportedExtensionList`). They're imported from the physical `@mathjax/src/mjs/...` paths, because `moduleResolution: node` ignores `exports`. These imports keep working after TS 6's `moduleResolution: bundler`. `TexError` is now a type-only import with `.js`, and the unused `digits` option is gone from the local type.
- **XML serialization:** v4 adds a `data-latex` attribute holding the source TeX. `adaptor.innerHTML()` doesn't escape `<`/`>` in attribute values, so any math containing `<`, such as `a < b` or `\ce{A <=> B}`, produced an SVG that isn't well-formed, and the hover image didn't render. The SVG is now serialized with `adaptor.serializeXML()`.
- **Bundle (`packages/build`):** MathJax's SVG output imports its default font through the `#default-font/*` subpath import, even when another font is passed in. A small esbuild `onResolve` plugin maps that import to `@mathjax/mathjax-tex-font/mjs/*`, which keeps newcm (about 950 KB minified) out of `lsp.js` and `main.js`.
- **`ThirdPartyNotices.txt`:** updated for the new packages.

**Tests:** `packages/editor-server/test/mathjax.test.ts` covers:
- inline and display math, environments, and the alternate fonts (`\mathbb`, `\mathcal`, `\mathfrak`, `\mathscr`)
- a `\newcommand` defined elsewhere in the document, which must match the expanded output
- mhchem, physics and cancel on request, and every supported extension together
- theme color and scale in the injected CSS, crossref label stripping, and the data URI
- escaping of `<`/`>` in attributes
- TeX errors

All of these except the escaping test also pass against MathJax 3 (the escaping problem didn't exist there).

## Output equivalence

I typeset about 40 expressions with the bundled v3 and v4 code and compared them in headless Chrome, side by side. They covered each of the 22 opt-in extensions, delimiters, arrows, accents, macros, and errors.
- **Glyphs:** identical. It's the same font. Widths match to within about 0.1–2% on most expressions.
- **Heights:** some bounding boxes are tighter in v4 (for example `E = mc^2`, stretchy arrows, amscd), so the image sizes differ slightly.
- **Improvements:** `\begin{numcases}` (cases) failed in v3 (`\empheqlbrace` undefined) and works in v4. `\norm` in physics renders properly. `\braket` gets v4's wider spacing.
- **Regressions (minor, opt-in extensions only):**
  - `\xtwoheadrightarrow` (extpfeil) loses its double head.
  - Short labels on some extpfeil/mathtools arrows (`\xlongequal`, `\xtwoheadleftarrow`) sit a little lower and touch the arrow.

  These look like MathJax 4 TeX-font metrics issues. `\xrightarrow`, `\xleftrightarrow`, `\xRightarrow` and `\xmapsto` are fine.
- **Unchanged v3 gaps:** glyphs that the TeX font never had (`\celsius`, `\micro`, `\perthousand`, `\upalpha`, `\unicode{x263A}`) still fall back to `<text>`, exactly as in v3.
- **Same behavior:** error messages are the same (for example "Missing close brace"), and so is the undefined-macro red text.

title: build: remove jayson, upgrade node-sqlite3-wasm to 0.8, replace cross-fetch with fetch
description:
Phase 2 of the dependency upgrade: the editor-server dependencies, minus MathJax. MathJax 4 is in a separate PR stacked on this one, because it slightly changes how math renders.

## Changes

**Removed jayson** instead of upgrading it. Nothing imports `jaysonServerMethods`, `jsonRpcMethod` or `jsonRpcBrowserRequestTransport` now that the writer is gone, but they were still bundled into `main.js` and `lsp.js`. So this PR deletes `core-node/src/jsonrpc.ts` and `core-browser/src/jsonrpc/browser.ts`, their `index.ts` exports, and `jayson` from `core-browser`, `core-node`, `editor` and `editor-server`. (The first commit bumps jayson to 5, and a later commit removes it; the squash is what matters.)

**Dropped `cross-fetch`** in favor of the global `fetch`. The LSP runs on VS Code's Node 22 (`engines.vscode ^1.101`).
- **No-host detection:** node-fetch put `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` in the error message. Undici instead rejects with `TypeError: fetch failed` and puts the system error in `cause`. So the two substring checks that drive the "no internet / host not found" handling would have stopped matching:
  - `server/response.ts`: DOI, Crossref, PubMed and DataCite lookups (`kStatusNoHost`)
  - `core/zotero/web/api.ts`: Zotero web sync (503)

  Both now use a new `isNoHostError()` in `core/fetch.ts`, which checks `cause.code` for `ENOTFOUND` or `EAI_AGAIN`. The error text now includes the cause (`fetch failed: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND doi.org`), so it's as informative as before.
- **Types:** `Response` and `Headers` now come from `@types/node` 22's globals. Before, cross-fetch's typings injected `lib: dom`. There was no type fallout.
- **Bundle:** removing cross-fetch also drops node-fetch, whatwg-url and tr46 from `lsp.js` and `main.js`.

**Explicit `lib` settings:** on `main`, two dependencies were quietly supplying type libraries. cross-fetch's typings contain `/// <reference lib="dom" />`, and jayson's typings pull in `@types/node`. Once both are removed, and with TS 6 (#1165) no longer loading every `@types` package, those libraries disappear. So this PR declares them where they're used:
- `apps/lsp` and `apps/vscode` get `"DOM"`, because they type-check `packages/editor-types` (`HTMLElement`, `VoidFunction`).
- `apps/panmirror` gets `"ES2022.String"`, because `packages/editor` uses `String#at`.

These are type-only changes, with no runtime effect.

**node-sqlite3-wasm `^0.5.2` → `^0.8.60`** (SQLite 3.41 → 3.53.4).
- **File locking:** 0.6 added a lock to its VFS. For each query it `mkdir`s `<db>.lock` next to the database, and it reports `SQLITE_BUSY` while that directory exists. If the LSP is killed mid-query (for example on a window reload), the lock would be left behind, and local Zotero would stay broken until someone deleted the cache by hand. `db.ts` now removes a stale lock before it opens the cached copy, and also when it cleans up a copy that failed to open. This is safe because the per-`dataDir` queue means no query in this process holds the lock, and the copy is only ever read.
- **Read-only:** the copy is now opened with `readOnly: true`.
- **Types:** 0.6.2 ships its own types, so I deleted our ambient shim, `src/@types/node-sqlite3-wasm.d.ts`. There was no type fallout.
- **Unchanged:** `forceLegacyJournalMode` is still needed, because the VFS still has no WAL support. The wasm file is still `dist/node-sqlite3-wasm.wasm`, so the copy step in `apps/lsp/build.ts` is unchanged.

**Tests:** `editor-server` now has a `test` script (`node --import tsx --test`) and declares `tsx`. The new tests are:
- `test/fetch.test.ts`: `isNoHostError`/`fetchErrorMessage`, plus a real `fetch` to a `.invalid` host through `handleResponseWithStatus`.
- `test/zotero-db.test.ts`: it builds a WAL-mode `zotero.sqlite` with `node:sqlite` and queries it through `withZoteroDb`. It also checks that a leftover `.lock` directory doesn't block queries (this test fails without the fix), and that concurrent callers are serialized.

Out of scope: #1137 and #1138 (both in the Zotero code), and `uuid` in editor-server (that's the node-utils PR).

## Verification

On Node 24, rebased onto `main` after #1165 (TS 6):
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks.
- `yarn test-packages`: **10/10** tasks, because editor-server is new (8 tests).
- `yarn lint --continue`: 5/5 tasks, 0 errors, and the same 17 warnings in `quarto`.
- `yarn test-vscode` (VS Code 1.109, Quarto CLI on PATH): main 150 passing, r-project 3 passing.
- **Bundled sqlite:** I esbuild-bundled `withZoteroDb` (cjs, node22, minified, the wasm copied alongside) and queried a WAL-mode database with it.
- **Bundle size** (measured before the jayson removal, which shrinks the bundles further): `lsp.js` went from 3,318,520 to 2,993,329 bytes (−325 KB; gzipped 1,053 → 971 KB). `main.js` went from 4,578,509 to 4,253,472 bytes (gzipped 1,394 → 1,312 KB). The saving is mostly node-fetch/whatwg-url/tr46.

Not tested by hand: a Zotero library, and DOI/PubMed lookups with the network off.

title: build: upgrade TypeScript to 6.0
description:
Step 0.7 of the dependency upgrade: TypeScript 5.9 → 6.0.

## Changes

**`typescript` `^5.9.3` → `~6.0.3`** (the latest 6.0.x) in all ten workspaces that declare it: the root, `apps/{lsp,panmirror,vscode,vscode-editor,vscode-markdownit}`, and `packages/{annotated-json,json-validator,mapped-string,tidyverse-errors}`. The lockfile has a single `typescript@~6.0.3` entry. It's a tilde range because typescript-eslint 8.71 (still the latest) peers on `typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0`. typescript-eslint doesn't need a bump, and lint prints no "unsupported TypeScript version" warnings.

**tsconfig.** TS 6 deprecates `moduleResolution: node` (node10). I fixed each deprecation instead of setting `ignoreDeprecations`.
- **`packages/tsconfig/base.json`:** `moduleResolution: "bundler"` and an explicit `module: "esnext"`. Everything that extends base is bundled by esbuild or vite, so `bundler` describes how it's actually resolved. It also honors `package.json` `exports`, which `vscode-languageclient` 10 needs. `apps/lsp` and `apps/vscode` keep `module: commonjs`, which 6.0 allows alongside `bundler`.
- **The four published `@quarto/*` packages:** `module: "node20"` + `moduleResolution: "node16"`, not `bundler`. These packages emit CommonJS that Node loads straight from npm, with no bundler in between. `node16` resolution type-checks imports the way Node will resolve them at runtime, so it's the accurate mode for them. `bundler` would accept imports that Node can't load. Their `package.json` has no `"type"` field, so `node20` emits CommonJS, and `tsconfig.cjs.json` no longer needs `module: commonjs` (only `outDir` is left). **The emitted `dist/cjs` JS, `.d.ts` and `.d.ts.map` files are byte-identical to the TS 5.9 output** (`diff -r` of all four packages), so what npm consumers see doesn't change.
- **`apps/{vscode-editor,panmirror}/tsconfig.json`:** TS 6 defaults `types` to `[]`, so packages under `typeRoots` are no longer loaded automatically, and the ambient `tlite` declaration in `packages/editor/src/@types` stopped resolving. I replaced the `typeRoots` entry with `"include": ["./src", "../../packages/editor/src/@types"]`.
- **`packages/tsconfig/vite.json`:** `customConditions: ["browser"]`. use-debounce 9's `exports` map only exposes types under its `node`/`browser` conditions, and bundler resolution uses neither by default. vite resolves the `browser` condition for these webview builds, so this matches what actually ships.

**`noUncheckedSideEffectImports`** is now on by default. I added `declare module '*.css';` to the ambient `@types/index.d.ts` files in `apps/vscode-editor`, `apps/panmirror` and `packages/editor`, rather than turning the check off. It stays on for side-effect imports that aren't CSS (for example, `import 'vscode-webview'`).

**Source and dependency fixes:**
- **`@lezer/highlight` `^1.1.3` → `^1.1.6`** (`packages/editor-codemirror`). 1.1.3's `exports` map points at `dist/index.js`, but its types live in `dist/highlight.d.ts`, so bundler resolution can't find them. 1.1.4 renamed that file to `dist/index.d.ts`. I stayed on 1.1.x so this PR doesn't pull in a second `@lezer/common` (1.2.x needs `@lezer/common ^1.3.0`, and the lock has 1.0.2), which would split the parser and highlighter's node-prop registries. All three ranges (`^1.0.0`, `^1.1.3`, `^1.1.6`) resolve to one 1.1.6 entry. The Phase 1 batch can take lezer to 1.2.
- **`packages/editor-codemirror/src/behaviors/diagnostics.ts`:** `StateEffect.define<void>(…)` for `removeUnderlines`. TS 6 no longer infers `Value = void` from the `map: () => { }` callback, so `removeUnderlines.of()` started requiring an argument. With the same tsconfig, 5.9 accepts the old code, so this is an inference change, not a resolution change.

`apps/lsp`, `apps/vscode` and `apps/vscode-markdownit` needed no changes beyond base.json.

**Checked ahead for the LSP bump (not done here):** with TS 6.0.3, `module: commonjs` + `moduleResolution: bundler`, a scratch project resolves and type-checks `vscode-languageclient/node` and `vscode-languageserver/node` at 10.1.2. Both entry points have a `types` condition, and node10 can't resolve them at all.

title: test: wait for the visual editor to sync in roundtrip snapshot tests
description:
Fixes the roundtrip snapshot flake that shows up only under the Quarto pre-release: `valid-nesting.qmd` on #1152, and `valid-basics.qmd` on #1162. On #1162 the "actual" text was the unmodified source file, which means the visual editor hadn't loaded yet.

## Changes

**The race:** `roundtrip()` opened the visual editor, slept a fixed `APPROX_TIME_TO_OPEN_VISUAL_EDITOR` (1700ms), then switched back to source. The visual editor rewrites the document only once its webview has loaded and the host's `onEditorReady` handler has run `syncManager.init()`. That handler gives the editor the markdown and writes the canonicalized result back to the document. When loading takes longer than 1700ms, as it does with the slower pre-release, the test switched back first and read the untouched source.

- **New internal command `quarto.test_isVisualEditorSynced(uri)`** (in `providers/editor/editor.ts`, next to the existing `quarto.test_isInVisualEditor`). `VisualEditorProvider` records a webview panel in a private set after `syncManager.init()` resolves, and removes it when the panel is disposed. The command reports whether the tracked visual editor for the URI is in that set. It has to be a command because the tests run against the bundled extension, so they can't import provider state directly (see the note in `quartoEditor.test.ts`). Production behavior doesn't change: the only runtime cost is one set insert and one set delete per editor.
- **`roundtrip()` now calls `waitForVisualEditorSynced(doc)` instead of sleeping.** It polls until the visual editor is active and synced, with a 10s timeout. On timeout the message names the file and says which of the two conditions wasn't met.
- The roundtrip tests set `this.timeout(ROUNDTRIP_TIMEOUT)` (15s) instead of relying on mocha's 5s default, so a slow CI load can still finish and the failure message comes from our timeout rather than mocha's.
- `APPROX_TIME_TO_OPEN_VISUAL_EDITOR` is kept, because the two skipped visual-editor tests in `quartoEditor.test.ts` still use it.

## Verification

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`, `yarn build --force` (14/14), `yarn lint --continue` (5/5, 0 errors, same 17 warnings as `main`).
- `yarn test-vscode`: main label 150 passing, 3 pending; r-project 3 passing. Passed on 4 of 4 full runs.
- **Reproduced the race and showed the fix:** I temporarily added a 2.5s delay before `syncManager.init()` to simulate a slow load.
  - With the old 1700ms sleep, all 7 snapshot tests failed and the "actual" text was the unmodified source, the same failure seen in CI. `hello.qmd` passed, but only because its roundtrip is a no-op.
  - With the new wait, 8 of 8 roundtrip tests passed (about 3.7s each).
- **Repeated runs without the delay:** `--grep Roundtrip` passed 8 of 8 on 27 of 28 runs, including 8 runs with every core saturated. Each test now takes about 1.1s instead of about 2.1s. The one failure happened before I added the diagnostic message, and its output was filtered away, so I don't know what caused it. It took about 30s longer than a normal run, so it doesn't look like the snapshot mismatch. The new message reports whether the editor wasn't active or wasn't synced if it happens again.
- All local runs used VS Code 1.109 (pinned locally, not committed) with Quarto 1.10.18 on PATH.

I removed it from `packages/editor-server`, `packages/quarto-core` and `apps/vscode-markdownit`, because they don't import it directly any more (see the next point).
- **Removed `@types/js-yaml`:** v5 is written in TypeScript and ships its own `.d.ts`.
- **Empty input:** v5's `load()` throws on empty, whitespace-only *and comment-only* input, where v4 returned `undefined`. I added `loadYaml()` to `packages/core/src/yaml.ts`. It's built on `loadAll()`, returns `undefined` for empty input, and still throws on invalid or multi-document YAML, so it's a drop-in for v4's `load()`. It's used at every call site that parses user YAML:
  - cell options: `packages/core/src/jupyter/options.ts` and `apps/vscode/src/providers/cell/options.ts`
  - front matter: markdown-it preview, `quarto-core` `parseFrontMatterStr`, and the visual editor's `parseYaml`
  - `_quarto.yml`/`_metadata.yml`: `quarto-core` metadata and editor-server biblio
  - inline `references:`

  Without it, a cell whose only option line is a blank `#|` or a `#| # comment` would throw out of `partitionCellOptions`. That call is uncaught in the LSP's embed-shortcode completion. A comment-only `_quarto.yml` would also log an error every time it's read. I named it `loadYaml` instead of `parseYaml` so it doesn't collide with the visual editor's existing `parseYaml`, which catches errors.
- **`packages/editor/src/api/yaml.ts`:** v5 has no default export, so `import yaml from 'js-yaml'` is now `import * as yaml`. I also dropped the `onWarning` option, which v5 removed. Its handler, `logException`, was a no-op anyway.
- **`asYamlText`:** dropped `sortKeys: false`, which is deprecated in v5 and is the default. On a representative metadata object, the output is byte-identical to v4.

**Decisions** (taken from the research doc's recommendations):
- **We accept v5's default schema (YAML 1.2 `CORE_SCHEMA`).** Merge keys (`<<`) are no longer resolved, and timestamps such as `date: 2024-01-15` are read as strings, not `Date`. Both changes match quarto-cli, whose `QuartoJSONSchema` has no merge or timestamp types. So the extension no longer shows merged values that are ignored at render time. title: build: upgrade Vite to 8 (via 7.3), static-copy 4, sass 1.105
description:
Phase 2 of the dependency upgrade: Vite 3 → 7.3 → 8 for `apps/vscode-editor` (visual editor webview), `apps/vscode-markdownit` (notebook renderer) and `apps/panmirror`.

## Changes

The commits are in order: Vite 7.3 (still Rollup/esbuild), a renderer fix that the 7.3 step needed, a Mermaid plugin move that Vite 8 needed, and then Vite 8 (Rolldown/Oxc).

**Vite 3.2 → 7.3** (`394f3878`)
- `vite` `^3.0.0` → `^7.3.6`, `vite-plugin-static-copy` `^0.13.0` → `^4.1.1`, `vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js` `^2.1.1` → `^4.0.1` (panmirror).
- **Copy paths:** static-copy 4 always keeps the directory structure, so `dist/index.js` would have landed in `assets/www/editor/dist/index.js` and `out/markdownit/dist/index.js`, and panmirror's LICENSE in `dist/vscode/LICENSE`. I added `rename: { stripBase: 1 }` to every target. I used `1` rather than `true` so that nested output keeps its relative paths. I also changed `src` to `dist/**/*`, because in v4 `dist/*` matches only top-level files.
- **`build.lib.cssFileName: 'style'`** in vscode-editor. Since Vite 6, the default CSS name comes from `package.json` (`quarto-vscode-editor.css`), but `editor.ts` loads `style.css`.
- **`build.target`:**
  - Webview bundles: `chrome134`. VS Code 1.101, the `engines.vscode` floor we decided on, runs webviews in Chromium 134 (the same floor as #1151's `node22`).
  - panmirror: pinned to Vite 3's old `modules` default (`es2020, edge88, firefox78, chrome87, safari14`), so its syntax floor doesn't change under RStudio. Raising it is RStudio's call. I checked that the output has no ES2021 logical-assignment operators.
- **panmirror config → `vite.config.mts`.** The package isn't `"type": "module"`, and Vite 7+ is ESM-only. I didn't add `"type": "module"`, because `exports.require` points at the UMD file.
- **sass** `^1.56.1` → `^1.105.0` in vscode-editor. Vite 7 only uses the modern API, so the legacy-API deprecation warnings are gone. I also changed the 4 `@import '…variables.scss'` lines to `@use '…variables' as *;`, because `@import` is deprecated in Dart Sass. `variables.scss` only declares `$vars`, so nothing else changes.
- This drops esbuild 0.15 and rollup 2.79 from `yarn.lock`. Vite 7 shares the repo's esbuild 0.28.

**Notebook renderer `styles.css` lookup** (`1b0bda45`)

`vscode-markdownit/src/index.ts` built the stylesheet URL by rewriting its own `import.meta.url` with `/index\.[\d\S]*\.?js$/`. That regex matches Vite 3's `index.8201be0b.js` chunk name, but not Vite 5+'s `index-<hash>.js`. So on 7.3 the `<link>` would have pointed at the JS chunk and the renderer would have been unstyled. It now replaces the last path segment, whatever it's called. (On Vite 8 the code happens to end up in `index.js` itself, so the old regex would also have worked there, but only by luck.)

**Move the Mermaid plugin from `packages/core` into `apps/vscode-markdownit`** (`abf200ca`)

On Vite 8, both UMD builds (the visual editor and panmirror) failed with `INVALID_OPTION … UMD and IIFE are not supported for code-splitting builds`, even though Vite already sets `codeSplitting: false` for UMD. The cause is [rolldown/rolldown#11001](https://github.com/rolldown/rolldown/issues/11001) (open, rolldown 1.2.11 is the latest). The visual editor never uses Mermaid, but it reaches it through the `core` barrel. Rollup tree-shook Mermaid out entirely. Rolldown still emits Mermaid's lazy diagram chunks (flowchart-elk/mindmap/timeline) as a second chunk, and UMD can't have one. The notebook renderer is the plugin's only consumer, so I moved the file there unchanged (a `git mv` plus two import lines). This is the move the Mermaid research doc already recommends. It also means `packages/core` no longer imports the undeclared `mermaid`; `vscode-markdownit` already declares it.

**Vite 7.3 → 8.3** (`1e14c26e`)
- `vite` → `^8.3.1` (Rolldown 1.2.11, Oxc, Lightning CSS) and `vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js` → `^5.0.2` (5 needs Vite 8; 4 is the last version that supports 7).
- `build.rollupOptions` → `build.rolldownOptions`.
- **Legal comments:** I removed `esbuild: { legalComments: 'eof' }`, which Oxc silently ignores. Vite 8 also *strips* legal comments when minifying, so every config sets `rolldownOptions.output.comments: { legal: true }`. The banners (React, clipboard.js, XRegExp, …) are kept, but inline rather than at the end of the file. I didn't turn on `build.license`: `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` stays the authoritative notice file.
- `__dirname` → `import.meta.dirname` in the configs. Vite 8 warns that its native config loader won't support `__dirname`.

**Decisions on the research doc's open questions**
- Q1: the renderer keeps code splitting (the Mermaid lazy chunks).
- Q2: license banners are kept inline, as described above. There's no `.vite/license.md`.
- Q3: panmirror is upgraded rather than removed, with its target pinned to what it had before.
- Q5/Q6: not addressed. The configs still aren't type-checked, and the copy step still happens outside turbo's `outputs` (#1144).
- Q7: `sass`, not `sass-embedded`.

## Verification

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`: lockfile unchanged. `yarn.lock` no longer has `esbuild@^0.15` or `rollup@^2.79.1`. The only esbuild left is 0.28.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 at each step, with no Sass deprecation warnings and no static-copy "No file was found". On 8 there's one new warning, `MISSING_GLOBAL_NAME` for `vscode-webview` in the editor's UMD wrapper. `index.tsx` has a side-effect-only `import 'vscode-webview'` (its types are what matter), so the guessed global is never used.
- Build outputs compared with `main`. I deleted the stale copies in `apps/vscode/assets/www/editor/` and `apps/vscode/out/markdownit/` before each build, so a wrong file name would have shown up as a missing file:

  | Output | main (Vite 3) | Vite 7.3 | Vite 8.3 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `assets/www/editor/` | `index.js` 12.84 MB, `style.css` 35.7 kB | same files; 10.70 MB / 35.5 kB | same files; 10.72 MB / 35.0 kB |
  | `out/markdownit/` | `index.js` (74 B stub) + `index.<hash>.js` 1.35 MB + 3 Mermaid lazy chunks + `is_dark` + `styles.css` | same layout (`index-<hash>.js`) | `index.js` 212 kB (now holds the renderer code) + `mermaid-<hash>.js` 1.14 MB + the same 3 lazy chunks + `is_dark` + `styles.css` |
  | `panmirror/dist/` | `panmirror.js` 11.08 MB, LICENSE, ThirdPartyNotices.txt | same; 8.99 MB | same; 8.96 MB |

  - Everything lands flat, with no `dist/` or `vscode/` subdirectories. The extension loads `index.js`/`style.css` and `out/markdownit/index.js`, and those names are unchanged.
  - Most of the JS size drop is the charset change: Vite 3 escaped non-ASCII as `\uXXXX` (about 700k escapes in the editor bundle), and newer Vite emits UTF-8. The webview HTML declares `<meta charset="UTF-8">`, and the renderer is an ES module (always UTF-8).
  - The UMD bundles have no `import(`, `import.meta` or `document.currentScript`. The UMD wrappers still expose `QuartoVisualEditor` and `Panmirror` (`{Editor, UITools}`).
  - The `@license` banner counts match `main` (7 in the editor, 3 in panmirror).
- `yarn test-packages`: 8/8 tasks.
- `yarn lint --continue`: unchanged from `main` (the 6 pre-existing `quarto-lsp` `no-unused-vars` errors).
- `yarn test-vscode` (VS Code 1.109, Quarto CLI on PATH): main 150 passing (3 pending); r-project 3 passing.
- `yarn dev-vscode`: both Vite watchers start (Rolldown watcher). An edit in `vscode-editor/src` and in `vscode-markdownit/src` triggers a rebuild and re-copies into `apps/vscode`.
- CI caveat: this PR doesn't touch `apps/vscode/**` or `apps/lsp/**`, so `build.yaml`'s packaging job won't run on it. `test.yaml` (which builds everything) does run.

**Not done: manual checks in the Extension Development Host.** I couldn't do these, and they're the main remaining risk. Vite 8 changes the bundler, and CommonJS default-import interop is the part most likely to show up only at runtime, as "x is not a function":
- Visual editor:
  - It loads and is styled: toolbar, outline sidebar, find panel (CSS modules + Sass variables), and the omni-insert images.
  - CodeMirror code cells work.
  - Cut/copy (`clipboard`), emoji insert (`pinyin`/`transliteration`), spell-check (`typo-js`), tooltips (`tlite`), and outline scroll (`zenscroll`) work.
  - The webview console shows no errors.
- Notebook renderer: `styles.css` loads, dark theme works, and a Mermaid flowchart, mindmap and timeline render (the lazy chunks).
- panmirror: RStudio should check `window.Panmirror` and the injected styles.

title: build: upgrade editor libraries (bibliojson, fuse.js 7, sentence-splitter 5, i18next 26)
description:
Phase 2 of the dependency upgrade: the visual editor's small libraries.

## Changes

**`biblatex-csl-converter` 2.1 → `bibliojson` 4.1** (`packages/editor`)
- `biblatex-csl-converter` 3.x is deprecated on npm in favor of `bibliojson`, which is the same project renamed. We only use two of its data tables, `BibTypes` and `BibFieldTypes`, for CSL → BibTeX export when a citation is inserted into a `.bib` bibliography. BibTeX parsing happens on the server and isn't affected.
- bibliojson ships its own types but doesn't export the BibDB node types (`NodeArray`, `NameDictObject`, `RangeArray` and so on). They now live in `packages/editor/src/api/bibliography/bibliojson-types.ts`, and `BibType`/`BibField` are derived from the exported tables. The hand-written `declare module 'biblatex-csl-converter'` shim is deleted.
- Removed the dead `toBibLaTeX()` function and its `BibLatexExporter` import. Nothing called it.
- **User-visible output change:** bibliojson has BibDB types for CSL types that 2.x didn't know about. In 2.x these fell back to `BibTypes.misc`, whose CSL type is `article`, so they were written as **`@article`**. They're now written as **`@misc`**, which is more correct. The affected types are `software`, `graphic`, `song`, `motion_picture`, `legislation`, `legal_case`, `personal_communication`, `interview`, `hearing`, `map`, `figure` and `classic`. The set of fields written for those types may also differ slightly. CSL types that bibliojson still doesn't know about still fall back to `@article`, as before. For the types that already existed, the field lists are unchanged apart from ordering, which we don't depend on. There's a changelog entry for this.
- bibliojson declares `engines.node: ">=22"`, which is fine now that `.nvmrc` is on Node 24.
- `ThirdPartyNotices.txt`: renamed the LGPL entry to bibliojson.

**fuse.js 6.6 → 7.5**: v7 dropped the `Fuse` TypeScript namespace. The five `Fuse.FuseOptionKeyObject<…>` uses now import the named `FuseOptionKeyObject` type. There are no runtime API changes for us. 7.5's scoring fixes can reorder `@` citation completion results a little, for example when two keys tie on the prefix, the entry with the shorter title may now come first.

**sentence-splitter 3.2 → 5.0**: `split()`'s return type is stricter. `wrap.ts` now binds the next part to a variable, so the `WhiteSpace` discriminant narrows it before `.value` is read. The research found no splitting differences on a set of tricky English, French and Japanese strings.

**i18next 22 → 26** (`packages/editor-ui`): no code or resource changes needed. We have no plural keys, no `compatibilityJSON` setting, and none of the removed options.

**Removed `flat` and `@types/flat`** from `packages/ui-widgets`. Nothing has imported them since Formik was removed. Also removed from `ThirdPartyNotices.txt`, since `flat` was never bundled. It stays in `yarn.lock` because mocha's `yargs-unparser` depends on it.

**Replaced `lodash.orderby`** with a native stable sort (`sortPackagesByName`), and removed `lodash.orderby` and `@types/lodash.orderby`. The only caller is the R-packages citation panel. Its second sort key, `'in.project.library'`, isn't a field of `RPackageInfo`, so it was always `undefined` and had no effect. The panel itself is effectively dead in Quarto, because `getRPackageState` isn't implemented in `editor-server`. I left it in place; deleting it is a separate decision.

**Tests:** `packages/editor` now has a `test` script (`node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts`, the same as `packages/core`), with tests for:
- The BibTeX entry type mapping: `@article`, `@book`, the new `@misc` types, and the fallback for unknown types.
- The package sort.

The outdated fixtures under `test/api/` aren't picked up by this script.

Decisions on the research doc's open questions:
1. **Track `bibliojson`; don't vendor its tables.** Vendoring the tables would mean bundling LGPL-derived data into the MIT extension, which needs a licensing decision. The measured size cost (below) is small compared with the bundle.
2. **Accept the `@article` → `@misc` change** for the types above, with a changelog line.
3. **Keep i18next** (upgraded) rather than replacing it with a local `t()`.
4. **Keep the R-packages panel** for now; only its sort changed.
5. **Accept fuse.js 7.5's ranking changes** rather than pinning `~7.4`, which would keep known scoring bugs.

## Verification

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`: leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks. `apps/vscode-editor`'s `tsc --noEmit` type-checks `editor`, `editor-ui` and `ui-widgets`, and `apps/panmirror` builds too.
- `yarn test-packages`: 9/9 tasks. That's one more than on `main`, because of the new `editor` test task (15 tests passing).
- `yarn lint --continue`: unchanged from `main` (the 6 pre-existing `quarto-lsp` `no-unused-vars` errors).
- `yarn test-vscode` (VS Code 1.109, Quarto CLI on PATH): main 150 passing, r-project 3 passing.
- Bundle size, `apps/vscode-editor/dist/index.js`:

  | | bytes | gzip |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main` | 12,840,535 | 3,392,370 |
  | this PR | 13,077,335 (+236,800, +1.8%) | 3,435,918 (+43,548) |

  bibliojson accounts for about +254 KB of that, and the other changes net about −17 KB. To isolate it, I rebuilt with `bibliojson` aliased to a stub, then to `biblatex-csl-converter` 2.1:

  | | bytes | gzip |
  |---|---|---|
  | `biblatex-csl-converter` 2.1 | 269,941 | 61,801 |
  | `bibliojson` 4.1 | 523,704 | 109,083 |
  | difference | +253,763 | +47,282 |

  Most of the increase comes from bibliojson's extra importers, locales and specs, which Rollup can't fully tree-shake (the package doesn't set `sideEffects`).
- **Not done: a manual smoke test of the visual editor** in the Extension Development Host. Remaining checks:
  - Insert a citation into a `.bib` bibliography for a journal article, a book (both should be unchanged) and a software/dataset DOI (should now be `@misc`).
  - `@` citation completion and `@fig-`/`@sec-` xref completion, plus Insert → Cross Reference and Insert → Citation search.
  - `wrap: sentence` on save.
  - UI strings: Find/Replace labels, the outline sidebar, and command names in menus.

title: ci: add dependabot config for npm and GitHub Actions
description:
Closes #1135

Adds `.github/dependabot.yml` with weekly updates for:

- **npm**: one entry at the root, which covers every Yarn v1 workspace (`apps/*`, `packages/*`, `packages/ojs/*`). Minor and patch bumps are grouped into one PR; major bumps get separate PRs. At most 10 open PRs at a time.
- **GitHub Actions**: all updates grouped into one PR, which keeps the actions updated after #1129.

Deliberate exceptions:

- `@types/vscode` is ignored. It's pinned to `1.75.0` to match `engines.vscode`, and bumping it would let code use newer VS Code APIs and quietly raise the minimum supported VS Code version.
- `@types/node` major bumps are ignored. The version tracks the Node runtime each package runs on.

Security-only Dependabot PRs are turned on separately in repo Settings → Code security.

title: build: require VS Code 1.101 (engines.vscode and @types/vscode)
description:
Phase 0.6 of the dependency upgrade.

## Changes

- **`engines.vscode`: `^1.75.0` → `^1.101.0`** (`apps/vscode/package.json`). VS Code 1.101 is the first release with a Node 22 extension host, which is what the esbuild `target: 'node22'` from #1151 already assumes. `engines.positron` (`^2026.04.1`, Code-OSS 1.109) is unchanged. The Marketplace and Open VSX serve older hosts the newest extension version whose `engines.vscode` they satisfy, so users on VS Code 1.75–1.100 (or forks pinned there) stay on the current release rather than breaking.
- **`@types/vscode`: `1.75.0` → `1.101.0`**, keeping the exact pin so it can't drift above the engine floor (vsce refuses to package when it does). `apps/vscode` is the only workspace that declares or imports `vscode` types.
- **No type fallout:** `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/vscode` (which now runs as part of its build) is clean against 1.101 with no source changes, including `TestLogOutputChannel implements LogOutputChannel` and the drop-edit provider.
- **Not included:** the LSP library upgrade (`vscode-languageclient`/`-server` 10, protocol types 3.18, `@vscode/l10n`, dropping `vscode-nls`). It needs a `moduleResolution` change, so it'll be a separate Phase 2 PR.
- CHANGELOG entry for the new minimum.

Nothing else keys off the engine floor: `.vscode-test.mjs` doesn't pin a version (it tests against stable), the launch configs and CI don't reference one, and CONTRIBUTING doesn't mention it. The `packages/build` comment added in #1151 already refers to `^1.101`.

## Verification

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged. The only lockfile change in this PR is the `@types/vscode` entry.
- `yarn build --force`: 14/14 tasks.
- `yarn test-packages`: 8/8 tasks.
- `yarn lint --continue`: unchanged from `main` (the 6 pre-existing `quarto-lsp` `no-unused-vars` errors).
- `yarn test-vscode` (Quarto CLI on PATH), run against two versions by temporarily setting `version` in `.vscode-test.mjs`:
  - VS Code 1.109.0: main 150 passing (3 pending), r-project 3 passing
  - **VS Code 1.101.0 (the new floor):** main 150 passing (3 pending), r-project 3 passing
- Not done: `vsce package`, and a manual smoke test in the Extension Development Host.

title: build: move to ESLint 10 flat config and typescript-eslint 8
description:
Phase 0.5 of the dependency upgrade.

## Changes

**ESLint 7/8 → `^10.11.0`, with flat config.** ESLint 10 removes eslintrc entirely, so every non-OJS `.eslintrc.*` (the root one plus 17 per-workspace files) is replaced.
- **Per-workspace `eslint.config.mjs` only, no repo-root config.** The OJS subtrees under `packages/ojs/` still run ESLint 8.57 from their `test` scripts. ESLint 8.57 switches to flat-config mode if it finds an `eslint.config.*` anywhere above cwd, which would make it ignore their `.eslintrc.json` and fail. ESLint 10 looks up the config from each linted file's directory, so per-workspace files work both under turbo and in the editor extension. `.mjs` works whether or not the workspace is `"type": "module"`.
- **`eslint-config-custom`** is now an ESM flat config: `@eslint/js` recommended + `typescript-eslint` recommended + `eslint-config-prettier/flat`, browser globals, on `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}`. It declares everything it imports (`@eslint/js` ^10.0.1, `typescript-eslint` ^8.71.0, `globals` ^17.12.0, `eslint-config-prettier` ^10.1.8) and has `eslint` ^10 as a peer. It keeps `no-non-null-assertion: off` and sets `no-require-imports` to `allowAsImport: true`, so the `import X = require(...)` lines in the `declare module` shims stay legal.
- **`eslint-config-custom-server`** imports `eslint-config-custom` by package name (it used to `extends` a relative path) and adds Node globals and `ecmaVersion: "latest"`. I dropped its dead `**/__tests__/**` jest override (there are no such directories).
- **`typescript-eslint` 5 → 8**, via the unified `typescript-eslint` package. This replaces `@typescript-eslint/{eslint-plugin,parser}`. typescript-eslint 5 only officially supported TS <5.1, and 8.71 supports TS `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`.

title: build: upgrade Redux Toolkit to 2.12 and react-redux to 9.3
description:
Part of the Phase 2 dependency upgrade. Redux Toolkit ships in the visual editor (`packages/editor-ui`'s store, consumed by `apps/vscode-editor`), so this PR changes shipped code.

## Changes

**`@reduxjs/toolkit` 1.9.7 → 2.12.0 and `react-redux` 8.0.5 → 9.3.0.** These are the latest on the registry as of today. They bring in `redux` 5.0.1, `immer` 11, `reselect` 5 and `redux-thunk` 3. The lockfile now has exactly one copy of each. The two `redux` 4.x copies, `immer` 9, `reselect` 4, `redux-thunk` 2, `@types/hoist-non-react-statics` and the `react-is@18` entry are gone.

**Dependencies**
- `packages/editor-ui`: `@reduxjs/toolkit ^2.12.0`, `react-redux ^9.3.0`. I dropped `redux`: nothing in `editor-ui` imports it.
- `apps/vscode-editor`: `react-redux ^9.3.0`. I dropped the direct `redux` dependency too: its only use was `import { Store } from 'redux'`, for the `App` prop type. `App.tsx` now types that prop as `EditorUIStore` from `editor-ui`, matching what `EditorContainer.tsx` already did.

**Code (`packages/editor-ui/src/store/`)**
- `rtk.ts` deep-imported `@reduxjs/toolkit/dist/query/...`. RTK 2's `exports` map doesn't allow that, so it now imports `QueryReturnValue` from the public `@reduxjs/toolkit/query` entry.
- In RTK 2, `QueryReturnValue` takes a third `meta` type parameter, and the `queryFn` return type has to match the base query's meta type (`{}`). With the default `unknown`, every endpoint failed to type-check. `rtkHandleQuery` never sets `meta`, so it now returns `QueryReturnValue<T, JsonRpcError, undefined>`.
- `rtkFakeBaseQuery` worked around reduxjs/redux-toolkit#2314. I replaced it with the built-in `fakeBaseQuery<JsonRpcError>()` in `prefs.ts` and `dictionary.ts`, which type-checks cleanly on 2.12.

**Behavior changes I reviewed and left alone**
- In RTK 2, `configureStore` adds `autoBatchEnhancer` by default. RTK Query's internal actions still update state synchronously, but subscriber notification is deferred to `requestAnimationFrame`. The editor webview uses `retainContextWhenHidden`, and rAF is throttled in hidden pages. However, 2.12.0 falls back to a 100ms timer when rAF doesn't fire (`createRafWithFallbackTimer`), so I didn't pin `autoBatch: { type: 'tick' }`. The synchronous `readPrefsApi` → `getState()` reads in `sync.ts`/`theme.ts` aren't affected.
- Reselect 5 now memoizes with `weakMapMemoize` by default. The six `createSelector` selectors in `editors.ts` have stable input selectors and don't return their inputs, so the new dev-mode checks have nothing to flag. Vite defines `NODE_ENV` as `production`, which strips those checks from the bundle anyway.

**Decisions**
- Keep RTK/RTK Query in the editor. I didn't rewrite it to React context or `useSyncExternalStore`. A rewrite would risk behavior regressions (the optimistic prefs update, tag invalidation) for a modest bundle-size gain. It can be considered separately.
- React stays on 18 and `@types/react` is unchanged. react-redux 9's `@types/react` peer (`^18.2.25 || ^19`) is optional, so Yarn doesn't warn about it. It will be satisfied by the React PR.
